title: Deterministic backward for blocksparse impl
body: Stacked PRs: * #2512 * __->__#2253 --- --- --- # Deterministic backward for blocksparse impl PyTorch PR: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174813 ## Summary This make it possible to run bwd with blocksparse tensors w/ determinism. At a very high level, the current implementation needs two things 1. For every M x N block, a way to figure out for N_i is it this columns turn to accumulate DQ into the global memory. For dense it can infer this by predefined sparsity, I.e. dense, causal, sliding window. 2. Some coordination with the tile schedule to ensure that we throws work tiles in the queue in a way that will not block any given row from making progress. This is a fun little problem and I made some animations: https://x.com/drisspg/status/2022438130893426731?s=20 But that being said I feel as though there are two approaches for block sparsity, we could either compute the semaphore lock value for every N tile at runtime based off of the sparse data, Or we can precompute the lock values ahead of time. I did not go with approach 1 and went with approach 2 because in terms of total work, since sparsity is typically consistent across layers we get to amortize the construction and I was concerned that doing the scan across kv_blocks and indices would be too much overhead. ### So what does this look like We introduced 3 new attributes to `BlockSparseTensors` ( I wish this was 2 but we will come back to this): New dq_write_order(partial|full) mirroring the q_block_idx(num_blocks) tensors. They are used as such: ```Py dq_write_order: int32[B, H, num_n_blocks, max_q_per_n] ``` Parallel to `q_block_idx[B, H, num_n_blocks, max_q_per_n]`. Each KV column worker iterates from 0 to max_q_per_n, so for the i-th M-block in the CTA's iteration list: ```Py m_block = q_block_idx[b, h, n_block, i] my_lock_value = dq_write_order[b, h, n_block, i] ``` If we we can figure out via the total counts whether I corresponds to partial or full block and thats basically it. See animation :) ### Scheduling I implemented this and perf was terrible since by default we would use the `non-spt` path. SPT is fancy word for right to left. `spt=shortest processing time` for most causal masks they look lower triangular which means the amount of work for a column is highest on the left, since q_idx = 0 which is >= to all kv_indices and thus all m_blocks will contribute - and smallest on the right since the only block that has any actual dQ to compute is the last block for Nth columns iteration. ``` n_block (KV) 0 1 2 3 4 ┌────┬────┬────┬────┬────┐ 0 │ ██ │ │ │ │ │ ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ 1 │ ██ │ ██ │ │ │ │ m ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ (Q) 2 │ ██ │ ██ │ ██ │ │ │ ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ 3 │ ██ │ ██ │ ██ │ ██ │ │ ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ 4 │ ██ │ ██ │ ██ │ ██ │ ██ │ └────┴────┴────┴────┴────┘ work: 5 4 3 2 1 ``` Bad scheduling is terrible for perf, you turn beautiful parallel GPU into terrible serialized turtle. So I also add 1 more flag which is SPT. And that says in stead of scheduling using the default left to right flip the lock values so that go from lowest to highest from right left. This does require coordination with the scheduler. Why? Again lets look at causal for simplicity - Lets say your num_sms was 2 and your total KV blocks was 5 if you did the default scheduling we would throw work into the queue starting with kv_block 0 and kv_block 1 for m_tile 0 we would be good for m_tile 1 we would also be good since there is their lock values are 0 and then 1,0 but for m_row 2 we would have lock values (2, 1) and semaphore value 0 is at kv_block 2! So our workers will never be able to continue ``` n_block 0 1 2 3 4 ┌────┬────┬────┬────┬────┐ 0 │ 0 │ │ │ │ │ ✓ only CTA 0, lock=0 ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ 1 │ 1 │ 0 │ │ │ │ ✓ CTA 1 lock=0 goes first, then CTA 0 m ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ (Q) 2 │ 2 │ 1 │ 0 │ │ │ ✗ lock=0 is at n_block=2 — not running! ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ 3 │ 3 │ 2 │ 1 │ 0 │ │ ├────┼────┼────┼────┼────┤ 4 │ 4 │ 3 │ 2 │ 1 │ 0 │ └────┴────┴────┴────┴────┘ ``` So long story short with SPT for most causally blocks we are seeing around the 20-30 perf drop from deterministic bwd -> see attached data. ### Better Scheduling I was toiling with ideas for more optimal scheduling. Since the distribution of tiles can be arbitrary for BlockSparse, I think if we could ahead of time compute a `least blocking schedule` and then we use this schedule to submit kv_tiles, again this requires coordination with the scheduler and would probably add some slow down since get_next_tile_info will need a global read to figure out where to go. I think we would need to have 1 lock value per column in order to avoid any deadlocks and I thought of some good heuristics but afaik this is NP complete. Hard to say if all this AOT work would be worth the potentially faster bwd. Sounds like a future problem. Although lets say we did this I do kinda want `spt` attribute to really be `schedule` attribute which can either be non spt, spt or a permutation. Couldnt think of anything really elegant here ** ideas from reviewer welcome**. #### Fuzzing Side note I did a bunch of fuzzing for this PR, one really nice aspect (or not lol) is that the ratio of compile time to gpu work is very high so both testing and fuzzing is very amenable to parallel workers. This fuzzing lead to this PR: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2258 ### Performance: Sliding window size = 2048 and eventually starts to get majorly blocked This is with SPT = True And here is SPT = False

title: [CuTe, SM100] Preserve hd256 output alignment for vectorized stores
body:
## Summary

Preserve output alignment through the dedicated SM100/SM110 HD256 forward kernel so its epilogue can use vectorized stores.

The output is already physically aligned, but the kernel loses the compiler's stride/pointer alignment information when creating its view and applying a packed-query offset. In the diagnosed 512-token prefill specialization this scalarized the output stores (`STG.E.U16` instead of `STG.E.128`).

- Use the existing `assume_tensor_aligned` helper for the output view.
- Use the existing `domain_offset_aligned` helper for the cumulative-query row offset.
- First zero dynamic strides on singleton output axes. PyTorch considers tensors with arbitrary unused singleton strides contiguous, so the existing output validator accepts them; asserting divisibility on those raw strides would be incorrect. This normalization changes only the kernel's view, not the caller's tensor, accepted layouts, cache signature, or storage.

Attention math, tiling, pipeline synchronization, and backward kernels are unchanged. No new package dependency.

## Safety and coverage

Adds 14 cases covering FP16/BF16, paged and packed KV, padded/transposed outputs, minimally 16-byte-aligned storage offsets, nonzero cumulative-Q offsets, and singleton batch/sequence/head strides. The tests compare against independent FP64 math attention with low-precision math attention as the error baseline, check finite outputs, and verify that output guards and caller strides are preserved.

For nonsingleton axes, the existing output validator guarantees 16-byte-aligned strides. A cumulative-Q offset moves by whole rows, preserving that alignment. For singleton axes, the normalized stride is zero before the alignment assumption. Static strides receive no new divisibility assumptions.

These are layout-safety tests, not timing assertions; the original implementation is numerically correct on these fixtures too. The performance regression is demonstrated separately below.

## Performance

GPU time per **forward attention call**, in microseconds; lower is better. Speedup is parent time / patched time. Baseline: `0f3fb00d3f34196ca55f30d2f6c5dce0709b4667`.

| Workload | Parent (µs) | Patched (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Decode, batch 1, Q=1, KV=512 | 11.45 | 11.03 | 1.04× |
| Decode, batch 1, Q=1, KV=4096 | 40.77 | 40.32 | 1.01× |
| Decode, batch 8, Q=1, KV=4096 | 91.17 | 90.26 | 1.01× |
| Prefill, batch 1, Q=KV=128 | 40.71 | 9.61 | 4.24× |
| Prefill, batch 1, Q=KV=512 | 44.58 | 13.12 | 3.40× |
| Chunked prefill, batch 4, Q=128, KV=4096 | 80.33 | 50.85 | 1.58× |
| Prefill, batch 1, Q=KV=4096 | 245.12 | 116.54 | 2.10× |
| Ragged batch 2, Q=[129,513], KV=[257,1025] | 52.52 | 19.25 | 2.73× |

Measurement contract:
- GB300/SM103, BF16, GQA 16 query heads / 4 KV heads, head dimension 256, causal, 128-token KV pages, packed K/V cache strides, preallocated output, LSE enabled on both sides.
- PyTorch `2.15.0.dev20260909+cu132`, CUTLASS DSL `4.6.2`, Quack `0.6.4`, TVM-FFI `0.1.12`, Triton `3.8.0+gitc01b6774`.
- Same process, GPU, inputs, launch path, and dependencies; separate JIT caches and parent/patched kernel classes. Seed 42, normal-random BF16 inputs, shuffled page mappings.
- CUDA graph containing 32 calls with fixed warm/reused buffers; 25 warmup batches, 100 replay samples, three interleaved rounds (before/after, after/before, before/after), median of round medians. Native clocks/DVFS; telemetry recorded. No locked-clock or cold-DRAM claim.
- Uses Transformer Nuggets' CUDA-graph benchmark helper. Excludes compilation, graph capture, cache updates, model projections, and scheduling. Not an end-to-end model throughput result. Backward performance was not measured because the patch does not touch backward.
- Both implementations passed FP64/low-precision reference checks and produced bitwise-identical outputs for all eight measured workloads.

## Validation

- 14 new output-layout cases passed on GB300.
- 13 existing HD256 layout/paged-KV cases passed.
- Compute Sanitizer memcheck on all seven new BF16 cases: **0 errors**.
- Eight before/after benchmark workloads passed their reference and bitwise-equivalence checks.
- Focused review of the alignment, singleton-stride, and cache-signature contracts found no remaining blocker after the singleton-stride handling was added.
- Repository pre-commit Ruff check/format hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

The full attention suite, SM110 hardware, backward benchmarks, and racecheck were not run. The patch does not address the separate existing NaN-in-unused-V padding behavior.

Targeted new tests:
```bash
pytest -v tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_hd256_varlen_output_alignment tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_hd256_output_singleton_strides
```

title: [CuTe, SM100] Dedicated FP8 E4M3 2-CTA forward kernel (1.2-1.9x on B200/GB300)
body:
Dense E4M3 attention with `head_dim = head_dim_v = 256` on Blackwell runs the generic hd256 2-CTA forward kernel, whose BF16-shaped schedule leaves the FP8 tensor cores waiting on softmax and TMEM traffic. This PR adds a dedicated persistent 2-CTA FP8 forward kernel (`flash_attn/cute/sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_forward_fp8.py`) and dispatches to it from `flash_attn_func` for dense `float8_e4m3fn` inputs on SM100 (B200) and SM103 (B300 / GB300). Its BF16 output and FP32 LSE are **bitwise identical** to the generic kernel.

## What the kernel does differently

- persistent static scheduling; causal tiles are ordered longest-first with alternate waves reversed so trip counts balance across the grid;
- separate three-deep K and V TMA rings, one full-D QK^T MMA per KV block, QK^T issued one KV block ahead of PV;
- SM103: `tcgen05.ld.red` returns the row max together with the score tile; SM100 uses a plain TMEM load and a software max (same result, max is exact);
- the online-softmax correction factor is handed to the correction warps through SMEM, and the accumulator rescale is skipped when every factor in the warp is exactly 1.0.

FP32 accumulation, the softmax reduction order, the EX2 emulation settings and the FP8 P conversion are unchanged from the generic kernel, which is why the outputs are bitwise identical.

## Dispatch

`_hd256_fp8_dispatch()` in `interface.py`: dense inputs only (no varlen, paged KV, local window, descales, qv), `float8_e4m3fn`, `head_dim = head_dim_v = 256`, compute capability 10.x. `ld.red` is used when the DSL compile target is the SM103 family. E5M2 and every other configuration keep the existing kernels. Both choices are part of the JIT cache key. There are no shape-dependent tuning knobs: half-D QK^T tiles and a 2-deep KV ring were measured on both parts and were not better.

## Tests (`tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py`)

- `test_flash_attn_fp8_hd256_output`: reference comparison on 8 shapes (unaligned tails, aligned diagonal, `seqlen_q <= 128`, several persistent rounds, rows without valid keys, E5M2 fallback);
- `test_flash_attn_fp8_hd256_matches_generic`: bitwise equality with the generic kernel on 4 shapes x `return_lse`;
- `test_flash_attn_fp8_hd256_dispatch_rule` (CPU), `..._uniform_scores` (analytic output/LSE), `..._preallocated_graph` (strided output, CUDA graph replay with changed inputs).

`test_flash_attn_fp8_hd256*` is added to the GPU CI filter; the B200 CI runner now exercises the new kernel (SM100 path).

## Performance

Method: for each shape, both arms (upstream generic kernel and this PR) run in one process with separate JIT caches; outputs are checked bitwise; each arm is captured as a CUDA graph of N back-to-back `flash_attn_func` calls (N sized to ~20 ms), warmed up, and replayed in interleaved order for 6 rounds; the table reports the median per-call time. FLOPs = `2 * B * Hq * (Dqk + Dv) * pairs` with `pairs = Q * KV` (non-causal) or the bottom-right causal count. Default clocks. GB300: 152 SMs, PyTorch 2.10.0+cu130, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1. B200: 148 SMs, PyTorch 2.14 (NGC 26.08), CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1.

title: [CuTe, SM100] Add symmetric D512 forward and backward
body:
Add symmetric head dimension 512 (`d_qk = d_v = 512`) to the SM100 CuTe attention path, including FP16/BF16 forward and backward.

### Implementation and scope

- Fused two-CTA dense forward shares QK and online softmax across all 512 output columns, reusing the SM100 MLA pipeline. Generic forward uses two V256 slices for varlen, paged KV, FP8, local masks, softcap and SplitKV; each slice uses the complete D512 QK dot product.
- Separate TCGEN05 dQ/dK/dV kernels keep the working set within shared-memory/TMEM limits. Accumulation and grouped-query partial reduction use FP32, with head grouping and long noncausal tile ordering for reuse.
- Compact layouts keep batch/token extents dynamic, with runtime maximum lengths and scheduling-aware cache keys. Noncompact layouts retain static specialization. Forward, backward and GQA reduction have disk-cache reload regressions.
- Large GQA reduction counts and indices use Int64 from the first multiplication, avoiding overflow at 2^31 output elements.
- Signed window bounds retain their literal meaning. The latest fix also initializes gradients when a negative bound can exclude an entire output tile: for square sequences, those tiles previously skipped their stores and could leave stale gradients. Added tests use nonzero supplied output buffers so allocator reuse cannot hide missing writes.

FP16/BF16: dense/varlen forward and backward, MHA/GQA/MQA, causal/local masks, softcap, LSE gradients and training with SplitKV forward. FP8 E4M3/E5M2 and paged KV are **forward only**. Deterministic backward, learnable sinks, custom score/mask callbacks, block sparsity and sparse gather/scheduler metadata are outside this implementation. Callers must translate external `-1`-means-unbounded conventions to FA4's `None` convention. Validation is on B200; full-graph `torch.compile` integration is not claimed.

Latest follow-up: `71ff336`, retaining the dynamic-cache contribution in `313d646` and the subsequent fixes in `f502aea` and `bed49db`. The diff contains implementation, regression tests and necessary CI wiring; no reports or binary artifacts.

### Validation at `71ff336`

B200, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, quack-kernels 0.6.4:

- A separately installed wheel passed **402 tests: all 394 D512 regressions plus 8 upstream CI-selected smoke cases**, with no skips. All **54 Python modules** match committed source byte-for-byte; interpreter and imported module paths were checked in the controller and workers.
- **56 signed-window cases** cover FP16/BF16, square/rectangular sequences, MHA/GQA, entirely empty and partially empty output tiles, autograd and supplied nonzero gradient buffers. The previous installed wheel failed three sentinel reproductions; the fix also passed 24 independent cases including ordinary-window controls.
- The suite includes cache reuse across batch/token changes, disk reload, output layouts, FP8/paged/SplitKV, independently packed Q/K plus used lengths and LSE gradients, and four checkpoint/autocast/AdamW regressions. The latter exercise a small attention block, not a complete training stack.
- All four large-index reduction cases executed at or above 2^31 output elements, both across and within batches. These require about 40 GiB of buffers and explicitly skip below 48 GiB free memory.
- Compute Sanitizer **memcheck passed four square signed-window MHA/GQA cases with zero errors**. This is targeted sanitizer validation, not a full-suite sanitizer claim.
- The CI driver now selects the D512 file. Local validation used the workflow's filter and the driver's two-stage plan: fake pass **8 passed / 394 skipped**, execution pass **402 passed**. D512 tests require real values and intentionally skip the fake pass. Local execution used four workers; the workflow's default worker count and triggers are unchanged. This is local validation, not a claim that the upstream GitHub Actions workflow has run.
- Ruff on the added kernels/cache helper and `git diff --check` pass. Existing numerical tolerances were not relaxed; comparisons use FP64 and either fixed tolerances or the upstream input-precision error criterion, with finite-value checks.

```bash
python -m pip install -e 'flash_attn/cute[dev]'
pytest -x tests/cute/test_flash_attn_dim512.py
```

### Performance

Fresh measurements from this source on one B200: BF16, B1, Hq8/Hkv2, fixed sequence/mask, changing only D. D128/D256 are the upstream implementations at base `1bda8f9`. Changing D changes the workload; these are not identical-workload regression ratios.

Three interleaved rounds, four independent inputs rotated in a CUDA Graph, median of round medians; each pattern receives at least 150 ms warmup followed by 10 groups of 10 replays. Forward uses `num_splits=1` and `return_lse=True`; complete backward includes preprocessing and required reduction. Compilation and input creation are excluded. No clock settings were changed. Values are milliseconds:

| S / mask | D128 fwd | D256 fwd | D512 fwd | D128 bwd | D256 bwd | D512 bwd |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 / causal | 0.01084 | 0.01441 | 0.01235 | 0.03193 | 0.06617 | 0.07547 |
| 512 / full | 0.01133 | 0.01340 | 0.01298 | 0.03191 | 0.06261 | 0.07533 |
| 2048 / causal | 0.02704 | 0.02928 | 0.05181 | 0.05802 | 0.20128 | 0.22549 |
| 2048 / full | 0.02826 | 0.03288 | 0.07498 | 0.05900 | 0.18427 | 0.35949 |
| 8192 / causal | 0.11830 | 0.25866 | 0.51048 | 0.39751 | 1.03853 | 2.54343 |
| 8192 / full | 0.23055 | 0.43531 | 0.93605 | 0.66360 | 1.78877 | 4.93006 |

The same run interleaved the preceding D512 implementation at `bed49db`: 72 records total (54 current cross-dimension records, 18 preceding-D512 records). Observed complete-backward median differences across the six shapes were **-0.35% to +0.23%**. These measurements are not precise causal estimates of sub-percent overhead. No claim is made that optimization has reached a hardware limit.

The timing harness checks forward against FP64 (all queries through S2048, sampled boundary/interior queries at S8192, against all keys). Backward numerical validation comes from the separate regression suite; timing records are not a full 8K backward numerical proof.

title: Fix Windows builds with CUDA 13 and PyTorch 2.15
body:
## Summary

Fix the Windows CUDA build failures reported in #2832.

- Add sm_121 to the default CUDA architectures.
- Generate native sm_121 code with compute_121f on CUDA 12.9+.
- Emit forward-compatible PTX only for architectures supported by the active toolkit.
- Use C++20 with PyTorch 2.15+, while retaining C++17 for older releases.
- Enable MSVC’s conforming preprocessor with /Zc:preprocessor.
- Define _USE_MATH_DEFINES so M_LOG2E is available under MSVC.

These are build-configuration changes only; no attention kernel logic is modified.

## Motivation

CUDA 13.x CCCL headers reject MSVC’s traditional preprocessor. Additionally, PyTorch 2.15 headers use C++20 features, including designated initializers and std::strong_ordering.

On an SM 12.1 GPU, the existing architecture defaults also produce no native sm_121 cubin. Finally, MSVC does not expose M_LOG2E unless _USE_MATH_DEFINES is set.

Before this change, these resulted in:

  - CCCL C1189, requesting /Zc:preprocessor
  - C7555 for C++20 designated initializers
  - C2039 for std::strong_ordering
  - Undefined M_LOG2E
  - No native sm_121 code

## Compatibility

PyTorch releases before 2.15 continue to use C++17. The gencode helper now tracks architectures supported by the detected CUDA version, preventing unsupported architectures from being selected for the forward-compatible PTX target.

## Validation

  Tested on:

  - Windows 11 ARM64
  - MSVC 14.51
  - CUDA 13.4.46
  - PyTorch 2.15 Windows ARM64 headers
  - NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 12.1

Validation performed:

  - Reproduced all reported failures using the previous flags.
  - Compiled CCCL, PyTorch 2.15, and <cmath> headers together using the new flags.
  - Verified native sm_121 output and compute-121 PTX with cuobjdump.
  - Verified host compilation with the new MSVC flags.
  - Checked gencode output for CUDA 11.7, 12.8, 12.9, and 13.4.
  - Ran python -m py_compile setup.py and git diff --check.

  Fixes #2832

title: [CuTe, SM90] Fix wrong dQ in backward for head_dims padded to a non-multiple of 32
body:
## Description

The SM90 CuTe backward sets `hdim_multiple_of = 64 if dKV_swapAB else 16`. With the default (non-swapped) dK/dV layout, head_dim 72/104 therefore round `tile_hdim` up to only 80/112, while interface.py allocates and zeroes `dq_accum` with head_dim rounded to 32 (96/128), and the preprocess/postprocess steps use the same granularity. The kernel never writes the tail of the padded accumulator (columns 80-95 / 112-127), and the postprocess readback carries that stale data into dQ. Forward, dK and dV are unaffected; dQ comes back silently wrong with a uniform four-mismatches-per-column fingerprint.

### Root cause

The kernel-level tiling granularity (16) disagrees with the interface-level allocation granularity (32) for the non-swapped layout.

Use 32 for the non-swapped layout as well, matching the interface allocation. One-line change; a no-op for head_dims that are already multiples of 32, and the swapAB path is unchanged.

## Examples

Repro cell (bf16, seqlen 512, 8 heads, head_dim 72, non-causal, varlen with a single sequence), dQ checked against an fp32 SDPA reference at atol=rtol=0.05:

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute.interface import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(0)
q, k, v = (torch.randn(512, 8, 72, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") for _ in range(3))
cu = torch.tensor([0, 512], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
out = flash_attn_varlen_func(q, k, v, cu, cu, 512, 512, causal=False)
dq = torch.autograd.grad(out.float().pow(2).sum(), q, retain_graph=False)[0]
```

Affected head_dims: 72, 80, 104, 112 (16-aligned padding that is not a multiple of 32).

## Performance Data

No performance claim: this is a pure correctness fix. The change only alters tile padding granularity for the affected head_dims and is a no-op for head_dims that are already multiples of 32.

## Verification

A/B on H100 (SM90), bf16 inputs against an fp32 SDPA reference, head_dim in {72, 104} x causal in {False, True}, same seed/shapes/tolerances per cell. The stock build fails all four cells: three return dQ with more than half of all elements mismatched (uniform four-per-column fingerprint; fwd/dK/dV exact), and head_dim 104 non-causal additionally fails to compile with an MLIR partition error. With the patch all four cells pass, and every per-tensor max_abs_diff matches the same cells run on stock B100 (SM100), which does not have the bug. The analogous fix for the swapped layout landed upstream as [#2482](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2482).

title: [ROCm/CK] Fix num_splits heuristic, which could never return more than 1
body:
Cause
-----
override_num_splits_if_necessary() passed num_splits_heuristic_ck() two wrong inputs, leaving split-KV dead code: num_splits=0 was bit-identical to num_splits=1 on every shape measured.

1. num_n_blocks was ceildiv(hdim_v, kN1) with kN1 = hdim_v, i.e. a constant 1. It counts the KV-sequence blocks a split is carved from, so it must come from seqlen_k, as set_params_splitkv() does on the CUDA side. Pinned at 1, `max_splits = min(max_splits, num_SMs, num_n_blocks)` clamped to 1 and the heuristic could only ever return 1. seqlen_k was not even a parameter.

2. The parallelism term used nhead. The splitkv kernel packs the query heads sharing a KV head into one workgroup, so the grid is batch * nhead_k * num_m_blocks; using nhead overstated parallelism by the GQA ratio and suppressed splitting where it pays most. At a fixed batch*nhead of 4096 the gain from splitting tracks batch*nhead_k: 1.02x at 4096, 1.29x at 256, 1.95x at 128, 3.21x at 64.

Fix
---
Pass seqlen_k and nhead_k through and derive both quantities correctly. num_splits_heuristic_ck() itself is unchanged: given correct inputs its choices match, shape for shape, the best policy found by fitting occupancy- and blocks-per-split-based alternatives against measured optima.

The heuristic is also capped at 8 splits, and the `num_splits <= 128` checks become `<= 8`. The CK splitkv combine kernel only reduces up to 8 splits correctly: on gfx950 with CK c56c6750, num_splits 1..8 match an fp32 reference to ~5e-3 relative error while num_splits >= 9 diverge (rel err 0.28..2.0), independently of batch, seqlen_k and causal. Callers passing more than 8 get an error instead of silently wrong output. Lifting that limit in the combine kernel is left to a separate change; it is what holds the win to ~2.2x rather than ~7x, since 25 of the 93 shapes measured have their optimum above 8.

varlen fwd calls the same helper and is updated identically.

Correctness
-----------
Changing num_splits changes the split-K reduction, so this was checked against a full rebuild of the extension (2413 instances, gfx950, 0 errors) rather than by reasoning about the heuristic alone.

The existing suite carries the strongest signal. test_flash_attn_kvcache is already parametrized over num_splits=[1, 0] and over mha/mqa/gqa, d in {32, 59, 64, 80, 128, 256}, new_kv, paged and non-paged KV, rotary (fraction 0/0.5/1.0, interleaved or not), causal, local, alibi and batch_idx. Because 0 always collapsed to 1, none of those cases had ever reached the split-KV path. They do now:

| test                                   | result        |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| tests/test_flash_attn_ck.py -k kvcache  | 152064 passed |
| tests/test_flash_attn_ck.py -k varlen   | 56774 passed  |

On top of that, against an fp32 reference:

| check                                          | result                 |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| auto path (num_splits=0), 12 decode shapes      | rel err 0.0019..0.0036 |
| every split count 1..8, same shapes             | rel err <= 0.0041      |
| num_splits of 9, 64, 128                        | rejected, not computed |
| varlen vs the dense kernel on identical inputs  | rel err 0.00000        |

The rejection cases are the reason for the 8-split cap. Before this change the API accepted up to 128 and the combine kernel silently produced wrong output above 8; the divergence is abrupt (rel err ~5e-3 at 8, 2.0 at 9) and does not depend on batch, seqlen_k, num_n_blocks or causal.

The cap itself is measured on gfx950 with CK c56c6750 only. Whether other architectures or CK revisions share the same limit is untested here, so it is a named constant rather than something derived.

Performance
-----------
93 decode/short-q shapes on MI350X (gfx950), bf16, d=128, batch 1..128, seqlen_k 1K..128K, GQA ratios 1:1..64:1:

| metric                              | value  |
| ----------------------------------- | ------ |
| geomean speedup                     | 2.16x  |
| max speedup                         | 7.3x   |
| geomean vs best reachable at ns<=8  | 1.030x |
| shapes made slower                  | 0      |

Per shape, from the end-to-end run against the rebuilt extension (`auto` is num_splits=0, the path this patch changes; `ns=1` is the old behaviour):

| batch | seqlen_k | q/kv heads | ns=1     | auto     | speedup | rel err |
| ----- | -------- | ---------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | ------- |
| 2     | 131072   | 64/8       | 6.435 ms | 0.988 ms | 6.51x   | 0.0029  |
| 1     | 65536    | 64/8       | 3.237 ms | 0.519 ms | 6.23x   | 0.0030  |
| 4     | 16384    | 64/1       | 0.801 ms | 0.138 ms | 5.80x   | 0.0027  |
| 1     | 16384    | 64/8       | 0.815 ms | 0.144 ms | 5.66x   | 0.0028  |
| 16    | 16384    | 64/1       | 0.836 ms | 0.154 ms | 5.43x   | 0.0030  |
| 8     | 32768    | 64/8       | 1.655 ms | 0.354 ms | 4.67x   | 0.0036  |
| 4     | 4096     | 64/4       | 0.217 ms | 0.051 ms | 4.27x   | 0.0030  |
| 64    | 4096     | 64/1       | 0.243 ms | 0.076 ms | 3.18x   | 0.0029  |
| 1     | 4096     | 64/64      | 0.225 ms | 0.071 ms | 3.15x   | 0.0035  |
| 16    | 4096     | 64/8       | 0.247 ms | 0.114 ms | 2.17x   | 0.0019  |
| 128   | 1024     | 64/8       | 0.191 ms | 0.191 ms | 1.00x   | 0.0021  |
| 64    | 4096     | 64/8       | 0.322 ms | 0.325 ms | 0.99x   | 0.0035  |

The last two rows are shapes with enough parallelism already; the heuristic correctly leaves them at one split. rel err is against an fp32 reference.

title: Compile with c++20 for pytorch 2.13+
body:
## Motivation
https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2879 introduced compiling with `c++20` for pytorch2.14+ based on [header guard](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/178150/changes) but pytorch2.13 has `c++20` feature as well.

For example, the first compilation error encountered while building flash attention2 with pytorch2.13 is [here](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/release/2.13/c10/core/AutogradState.h#L88-L89) which is [default member initialisers for bit-fields](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/language/bit_field)
> There are no [default member initializers](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/language/data_members#Member_initialization) for bit-fields: `int b : 1 = 0;` and `int b : 1 {0}` are ill-formed.
(until C++20)


## Changes
- changed to compile the flash attention with `c++20` if pytorch version is greater or equal to `2.13`.

title: [CuTe, SM120] Reject backward configurations that exceed shared memory
body:
SM120 backward with equal head dimensions of 192 requests 115712 bytes of shared memory, exceeding the 101376-byte limit. Forward succeeds, but backward reaches `CUDADialectError(cudaErrorInvalidValue)` during compilation. CUTLASS prints the resource counts separately; they are not in the Python exception.

Check the actual shared-storage declaration before emitting the backward kernel and raise a `ValueError` containing the required bytes, limit, tile, and padded head dimensions. Using the declaration includes P/dS, LSE/dPsum, and alignment padding omitted by the existing, unused `can_implement()` estimate. The change only improves rejection of unsupported configurations; it does not add d192 backward support or change supported kernels.

Validation against upstream `edb5c76ee329b18ed95d1f7ea9aa522a1331ab7d`:

- Actual CuTe shared-storage compilation confirms 115712 bytes for d192 and the new `ValueError`; supported d64, d128, and d192/v128 declarations still compile.
- RTX 5090 / SM120: four rejection tests passed (FP16/BF16 × causal/noncausal), with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 and CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2.
- Python syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- In separate fresh baseline/candidate processes, 12 supported cases each passed output and dQ/dK/dV comparison to FP64 (with a same-input, output-dtype-rounded FP32 reference): d64/d64, d128/d128, d192/v128 × FP16/BF16 × causal/noncausal, B1/S128/H2. The d192/d192 case reproduced the original CUDA error and the new descriptive `ValueError`, respectively.

Reproduce the new regression test with:

```sh
pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k sm120_backward_rejects_smem_overflow
```

Related to #2609, which wires the existing `can_implement()` predicates into the interface. Its SM120 predicate still returns `True` for this d192 configuration because it counts 98304 bytes of Q/K/V/dO tiles but not the complete 115712-byte allocation. This small kernel-local check covers that gap without depending on the broader interface change.

AI-assisted implementation and testing. This is a validation/diagnostic fix, not a performance claim.

title: Fix version comparison, contiguity checks, and IndexPutFirstAxis perf
body:
This PR fixes and optimizes several issues in FlashAttention:

1. **Semantic Versioning & Contiguity checks**:
   - Replaced string comparison with proper `packaging.version.Version` semantic comparisons in `flash_attn_interface.py` to prevent compatibility issues on PyTorch >= 2.10.
   - Added missing contiguity checks for `q`, `k`, and `v` in `flash_attn_varlen_func`.
   - Fixed the `cache_seqlens` contiguous check in `hopper/flash_attn_interface.py` when passed as a `Tensor`.

2. **Input Validation Assertions**:
   - Added checks in `flash_attn_with_kvcache` to ensure that `k` and `v` are either both `None` or both provided, preventing silent failures or crashes.
   - Added similar checks for `rotary_cos` and `rotary_sin` pairs.

3. **IndexPutFirstAxis Optimization**:
   - In `bert_padding.py`, optimized `IndexPutFirstAxis` (used in sequence packing/unpacking) by replacing direct indexing with PyTorch's native `scatter_` and `gather` operations, resulting in a significant performance improvement.

4. **Type Hint Cleanup**:
   - Replaced the non-standard `Union[(int, torch.Tensor)]` type hints with `Union[int, torch.Tensor]` in `README.md`, `flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`, and `hopper/flash_attn_interface.py`.

title: ci: registry-free GPU job (runner-local SIF) + verify the provisioned overlay from a fresh session
body:
Two CI infra fixes that interact, in one PR.

## Registry-free GPU job

The job logged in to Docker Hub on every run to pull a private image. With the credentials rotated, the
unconditional login step fails before any test runs, although the SIF is cached and the pull is skipped.
The image is just Ubuntu + Python + torch; `run_fa4_ci.py` installs cutlass-dsl / quack / FA4 at job time.

- `gpu-test`: new input `fa4_local_sif` — use that SIF, skip pull and prune, fail if the file is missing.
- `ci.yml`: Docker Hub login only when `vars.FA4_LOCAL_SIF` is empty. Unset = unchanged behaviour.
- `tools/ci/docker/build_local_sif.sh`: `docker build` the existing Dockerfile on the runner and
  `apptainer build` a SIF into `CI_WORK_DIR/local-sif/` (registry mode prunes `*.sif` directly under
  `CI_WORK_DIR`, hence the subdirectory).

## Verify the provisioned overlay from a fresh session

All 8 tests failed with `JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ CuteDSLRT_TVMFFISetRaisedCudaError ]`
after a passing floor check. The test session saw the SIF-baked cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 runtime (`lib/`) next to
the installed 4.8.0 (`cu13/lib/`): `apptainer exec` returns before its fuse2fs child has flushed the overlay
image, so the next session can read a stale view, and DSL discovery tries `lib/` first. Intermittent and
load-dependent; latent since #2685, fatal once #2798 moved the pin off the SIF's layout. The floor check
runs in the same session as the install, so it cannot see this.

`tools/ci/run_fa4_ci.py`: wait until nothing holds the overlay image between sessions; verify from a fresh
session (one distribution per package, `flash_attn.cute` from the checkout, runtime owned by the installed
cutlass-dsl), re-provision once, then fail with `OVERLAY VERIFY FAILED: ...`; pin the verified runtime via
`CUTE_DSL_LIBS`.

## Validation

- Action pull step run locally in all three states (local SIF selected / missing file → exit 1 / variable
  unset → old cached-SIF path).
- Verification fails on an `--overlay img:ro` mount (whiteouts ignored, i.e. the leaked state), passes on RW.
- End-to-end with the `ci.yml` filter on the current CI SIF (DSL 4.6.0 baked) and on a
  `build_local_sif.sh` image (4.8.0 baked): verify OK, Pass 1 8/8, Pass 2 8/8 on both.

Related: #2685, #2798. Supersedes #2895.

title: ci: verify the provisioned overlay from a fresh session and pin the DSL runtime
body:
## Problem

Every GPU job on `main` failed on 2026-09-16, all 8 tests at `cute.compile(..., "--enable-tvm-ffi")`:

```
JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ CuteDSLRT_TVMFFISetRaisedCudaError ]
```

right after provisioning had reported `DSL floor check OK: nvidia-cutlass-dsl=4.8.0.dev0`.

Inside the failing test container the SIF-baked cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 runtime (`nvidia_cutlass_dsl/lib/`) was
visible next to the freshly installed 4.8.0 (`cu13/lib/`), although `prepare_overlay()` had deleted it and the
overlay image's upper layer on disk had the correct whiteouts and opaque marker. `apptainer exec` returns
before the fuse2fs that owns the ext3 image has finished flushing, so a session opened right after can read a
stale view. DSL runtime discovery tries `lib/` before `cu{major}/lib/`, so the stale 4.6.0 runtime was linked.
Intermittent and load-dependent. Latent since #2685; fatal once #2798 moved the pin from `==4.6.0.dev0`
(same layout as the SIF) to `>=4.6.2` (new `cu13/` layout).

The floor check runs in the same session as the install, where the in-memory overlay state is always right,
so it cannot see a cross-session inconsistency.

## Change (`tools/ci/run_fa4_ci.py`)

1. `wait_for_overlay_release()`: after every session, wait until no process holds the overlay image
   (60 s cap, then warn). `sync` at the end of provisioning.
2. `verify_overlay()`: a fresh session asserts one visible distribution per runtime package, `flash_attn.cute`
   imported from the checkout, and the `libcute_dsl_runtime` resolved by `get_shared_libs()` owned by the
   installed cutlass-dsl. On failure: recreate + re-provision once, then fail with `OVERLAY VERIFY FAILED: ...`
   naming what leaked, instead of 8 opaque JIT link errors.
3. Pin the verified runtime into the test sessions via `CUTE_DSL_LIBS`.

`tools/ci/README.md` documents the step.

## Validation

- The verification snippet fails on an `--overlay img:ro` mount (read-only mounts ignore whiteouts, i.e. the
  leaked state): 5 duplicate distributions and `flash_attn.cute` resolving to the baked copy. Passes on RW.
- End-to-end with the `ci.yml` filter on the current CI SIF (bakes DSL 4.6.0) and on a fresh

title: ci: add PyTorch 2.14 to the wheel build matrix
body:
## Why

PyTorch 2.14 raised the `ATen/ATen.h` header guard to C++20 (pytorch/pytorch#178150), and FA2's `setup.py` hardcodes `-std=c++17`, so building against 2.14 fails with `#error C++20 or later compatible compiler is required to use ATen` (#2863). Nothing in CI compiles FA2 against any torch newer than 2.10, so the break was only found by users building from source.

Adding 2.14 to the wheel matrix does two things:

1. Moves the failure from the user's `pip install` into the release build: the next time a torch release changes a header requirement, a `v*` tag build fails instead of a user's source build.
2. Gives 2.14 users a prebuilt wheel. `setup.py` derives the wheel name from `torch.__version__` and `torch.version.cuda` and downloads it from the release; today 2.14 users miss (no such asset), fall back to a source build, and that source build then fails on C++17. With this row they hit `+cu13torch2.14cxx11abiTRUE` (or `cu12…`) directly.

## What

- `publish.yml`: add `"2.14.0"` to `torch-version`. Exclude `cxx11_abi: FALSE` for it, same as every torch ≥ 2.7 row (PyTorch wheels ship CXX11 ABI = 1, so a FALSE wheel is unusable and would only double the job count). No CUDA exclude is needed: on the 12.9.1 runner the build picks the `cu126` torch wheel, on 13.0.1 the `cu130` one (see next point).
- `_build.yml`: extend the torch-minor → CUDA-tag map that decides which `download.pytorch.org/whl/cuNNN` index to install from ("highest published tag not above the system CUDA"). A missing key is a `KeyError` before torch is even installed, so the matrix row is useless without it. Entries are copied from what PyTorch actually publishes (checked 2026-09-16):

  | torch | published cu tags |
  |---|---|
  | 2.11.0 | 126 128 129 130 |
  | 2.12.x | 126 129 130 132 |
  | 2.13.0 | 126 129 130 132 |
  | 2.14.0 | 126 130 132 (no 128 / 129) |

  Only 2.14 is added to the publish matrix; 2.11–2.13 are in the map so `build.yml` (manual dispatch) can build them on demand.

Matrix cost: +16 jobs (2 OS × 4 Python × 2 CUDA × 1 ABI), 56 → 72 total. aarch64 `manylinux_2_28` wheels for 2.14.0 exist on all three CUDA tags, so the arm runner needs no exclude.

Wheel naming is unchanged: `_build.yml` produces `+cu{12,13}torch2.14cxx11abiTRUE`, which is exactly what `setup.py::get_wheel_url()` computes on the install side (CUDA major only, torch major.minor).

## Verification

- YAML parses; matrix expansion counted by script: 72 jobs, 16 for 2.14.0. `TORCH_CUDA_VERSION` resolves to `cu126` on CUDA 12.9.1 and `cu130` on 13.0.1.
- Local end-to-end on B200 (from reviewing #2879, now merged as f87af617): main + that setup.py change, torch 2.14.0+cu130, `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=100` — full build 97/97 TUs, 3625-case `tests/test_flash_attn.py` slice passes.
- Suggest one manual `build.yml` dispatch (`ubuntu-22.04`, `3.12`, `13.0.1`, `2.14.0`, `TRUE`) before the next `v*` tag to see a full runner build.

## Not in this PR (maintainer calls)

- Whether to also publish 2.11–2.13 wheels (+16 jobs each) or drop the x86-only 2.6.0 row (−8 jobs) to offset.
- Python 3.14 (torch ≥ 2.10 ships cp314).
- `publish.yml` only runs on `v*` tags, so this catches header changes at release time, not at PR time. A PR-time guard could be a seconds-long CPU job that runs `g++ -fsyntax-only` over `flash_api.cpp`'s torch include set; happy to follow up if wanted.

Related: #2863

title: Build CUDA extension with C++20 on PyTorch 2.13+
body:
## Summary

The NVIDIA CUDA build hardcodes `-std=c++17` for both the host compiler and NVCC. PyTorch 2.13+ requires **C++20** for any extension that includes ATen headers, so building against torch 2.13/2.14 fails at compile time:

```
#error C++20 or later compatible compiler is required to use ATen
```

Because `setup.py` passes an explicit `-std` flag, PyTorch's `cpp_extension` machinery cannot upgrade the standard for us — the hardcoded C++17 forces the failing standard.

Fixes #2863.

## Change

- Select the C++ standard from the installed torch version: `c++20` for `torch >= 2.13`, `c++17` otherwise. Existing toolchains on older torch are unaffected (no regression).
- Applied to both `nvcc_flags` and the host-compiler flags, including the Windows `/std:` variant, so the two stay in sync.
- Renamed `compiler_c17_flag` → `compiler_cxx_flag` since it is no longer always C++17.

The ROCm/HIP build path already uses C++20, so this only aligns the CUDA path.

No kernel implementation or mathematical behavior is changed — this is a build-configuration fix only.

## Testing

- Verified the version-selection logic maps torch `2.12→c++17`, `2.13→c++20`, `2.14→c++20`, `3.x→c++20`.
- The change is confined to the NVIDIA CUDA branch of `setup.py`; `python -m py_compile setup.py` passes.
- Full end-to-end build against torch 2.14 + CUDA 13.2 / SM120 was reported working by the issue author (#2863); I do not have matching CUDA/GPU hardware to re-run the full compile here, so I validated the setup.py logic rather than the produced binary.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

title: [CuTe, SM100] Sparse MLA bwd: in-kernel recompute-P + token-chunked backward
body:
Two composable, opt-in memory features for the sparse top-k MLA (DSA) path. Kwargs-only API; the default path is untouched (same binaries, speed, and memory — sentinel tests pass with and without the flags).

## `gather_bwd_recompute_p=True`

The forward saves only `out` + `lse` — no `p`/`row_max` at all (**508 MiB/1k tokens → 0** of saved activations; train forward 4.43 → 3.77 ms at 8k since the `p` store leaves the softmax critical path; the training forward reuses the inference binary). The backward main kernel reconstructs `P = exp2(scale·log2e·S − lse·log2e)` in-kernel with an extra Sᵀ UMMA over the already-gathered V (+ gathered K_rope for the rope chunk), masking invalid top-k slots on the exponent via the gather bitmask; smem stays at the exact 232448 B SM100 cap (dS merges into sP, sScaleP→sLse, stationary-QvB role swap).

- Forward `out`/`lse`: **bitwise-identical** to the default path.
- Grads: not bitwise (one fewer rounding in P) and measure **more** accurate vs an fp32 reference.
- `retain_graph` is safe: nothing saved is consumed.
- `recompute_P` requires the KV bitmask (asserted — it is the only masking in this mode).

## `gather_bwd_token_chunk=N`

The backward loops its three kernels over token chunks, bounding the p-sized dS transient (~520 KiB/token at H=128, W=2048) by the chunk instead of the sequence. With causal masking the chunked main kernel shrinks its K extent to `seqlen_k − seqlen_q + tok1` per chunk (non-varlen: sliced views; varlen: clamped `cu_seqlens_k` ends) so the recomputed bitmask reproduces the forward's key limit exactly; fully-masked chunks (`k_end ≤ 0`) skip all three kernels and zero their dq/dqv directly. Requires varlen or batch 1; the kwarg is validated at the entry points (positive int; sparse-MLA calls only).

- Chunked dq/dqv: **bitwise-identical** to unchunked (including adversarial non-causal indices under `causal=True`, varlen docs split across chunk boundaries, shared-kv, and rectangular `seqlen_q > seqlen_k`).
- dk/dv: differ only by fp32-atomic accumulation order (≤ the unchunked kernel's own run-to-run noise).

## Results (GB200, B=1, W=2048, bf16, square T=S, train step, median time / peak memory)

All columns H=128 except tilelang finetune, whose backward exceeds SM100 smem at H=128 and runs at H=64 (**half** the head-FLOPs).

| T=S  | FA4 main (H=128)         | tilelang dsv32 (H=128)     | tilelang finetune (H=64)   | this PR (`recompute_p` + `chunk=4096`) | vs main              |
|------|--------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------|
| 4k   | 12.75 ms / 5.14 GiB      | 64.08 ms / 1.08 GiB        | 70.04 ms / 0.55 GiB        | 13.44 ms / 3.08 GiB                    | +5.4% time, −40% mem |
| 8k   | 25.90 ms / 10.28 GiB     | 105.50 ms / 2.16 GiB       | 137.29 ms / 1.09 GiB       | 27.46 ms / 4.15 GiB                    | +6.0%, −60%          |
| 16k  | 53.61 ms / 20.55 GiB     | 188.53 ms / 4.32 GiB       | 272.47 ms / 2.19 GiB       | 56.40 ms / 6.31 GiB                    | +5.2%, −69%          |
| 32k  | 115.58 ms / 41.10 GiB    | 368.55 ms / 8.64 GiB       | 543.30 ms / 4.37 GiB       | 119.68 ms / 10.62 GiB                  | +3.5%, −74%          |
| 64k  | 260.62 ms / 82.20 GiB    | 730.25 ms / 17.27 GiB      | 1094.00 ms / 8.74 GiB      | 262.75 ms / 19.23 GiB                  | +0.8%, −77%          |
| 128k | OOM (186 GiB)            | 1480.45 ms / 34.55 GiB     | 2213.11 ms / 17.48 GiB     | 575.43 ms / 36.47 GiB                  | —                    |

tilelang reference: `tilelang` @ 0.1.13, same machine and methodology, `-1` index tails remapped to 0 (its gathers/scatters are unguarded; identical traffic). dsv32 = `examples/deepseek_v32/sparse_mla_{fwd,bwd}.py` with the head-split backward — same head-FLOPs, the apples-to-apples column: this PR is 4.8× (4k) to 2.6× (128k) faster. finetune = `examples/dsa_sparse_finetune/` at H=64: even at half the head-FLOPs it is ~4× slower than this PR at H=128. Before this PR the tilelang kernels used ~5× less memory than FA4 while being 2.6–5× slower; after it, FA4 matches their memory scaling (285–300 MiB/1k tokens vs dsv32's 270) at the same speed advantage — the remaining ~2 GiB gap at 64k is the chunk-sized dS transient. Full methodology, smem map, and design notes in `AI/SPARSE_MLA_RECOMPUTE_P.md`.

## Robustness hardening included in this PR

- The sV gather stages are zero-filled once at kernel launch: masked top-k slots skip their `cp.async`, so launch-time smem garbage could otherwise reach the dP GEMM as `0 × NaN` (a pre-existing load-p hazard; recompute mode additionally hardens dS against non-finite dP).
- The dV epilogue scatter is bounds-guarded (`0 ≤ idx < seqlen_k`), so chunked-causal runs never write past the sliced dv view (and skip the wasted zero atomics).
- `pipeline_bitmask` gets its `producer_tail` (same invariant the forward documents); the QvB/dO/dOt TMA tx-count invariants are asserted as actually paired; all warps (including the mma warp) use the same static top-k group count.
- One `SharedStorage` struct for all three compile modes via zero-size fields — per-mode layouts byte-identical (verified at 232448 B each).
- The bwd-preprocess compile key distinguishes `lse_log2` presence, so cached binaries can't be reused across mismatched signatures.

## Tests

`tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k mla_sparse` (34 cases): recompute-P vs fp32 reference + bitwise-forward checks; chunked-vs-unchunked (recompute and load-p, non-varlen and varlen with docs split across chunks, for both the rope and shared-KV kernel specializations, checked against per-doc fp32 references); fully-masked rows (all `-1` slots: `out = 0`, `lse = −inf`, NaN-free zero grads, unaffected rows bitwise); rectangular `seqlen_q > seqlen_k` chunking (exercises the skip-chunk path); learnable sink + sparse gather in every mode (out/lse/dsink bitwise-identical across default, recompute-P and chunked; all grads incl. dsink vs the fp32 reference — the sink lives inside `lse`, and dsink depends only on the full-size `dpsum`/`lse`, so neither feature needs sink-specific handling); plus the pre-existing sentinel suites with and without the new flags.

title: [FA2, SM89] Add D512 forward and backward
body:
Gemma4-E4B global attention uses `head_dim=512`. FA2 currently rejects it on RTX 4090 with `FlashAttention forward only supports head dimension at most 256`.

This adds native CUDA D512 forward and backward for SM89. It supports FP16/BF16, dense and varlen inputs, MHA/MQA/GQA, causal attention, and deterministic backward. The tiles use 64 KiB shared memory for forward and 96 KiB for backward. The D512 dQ accumulator layout follows its 64-thread MMA layout.

D512 requires zero attention dropout. Local attention, softcap, ALiBi, paged/split KV, `leftpad_k`, `seqused_k`, and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` remain unsupported. Existing head dimensions keep their current paths.

Validation on RTX 4090 (48 GB, SM89), PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8:
- Reproduced the original error with the unchanged upstream API.
- 105 new tests and 56 existing regression cases passed.
- Compute Sanitizer: 0 memory errors and 0 race hazards.
- Real Gemma4-E4B global-layer inputs passed FP64 output and gradient checks. LoRA backward with checkpointing and HF cached decoding also ran successfully.

For BF16, batch 1, Q/KV heads 8/2, causal attention, scale 1.0:

| Tokens | FA2 forward + backward | PyTorch efficient SDPA |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 0.56 ms | 0.93 ms |
| 2048 | 5.66 ms | 9.00 ms |
| 4096 | 19.11 ms | 22.92 ms |
| 8192 | 73.35 ms | 69.97 ms |

The benchmark includes SDPA KV expansion and gradient reduction. Forward alone is slower. Training uses less extra memory, but the 8192-token case still needs optimization.

Full-model training parity is not established. In a BF16 LoRA probe, the full-model gradient relative L2 difference was about 0.25 against FP32/FP64 global-attention references. FP32 versus FP64 references also differed by 0.245. Deterministic native repeats matched exactly. These are smoke and kernel accuracy checks, not convergence results.

Run `pytest -q tests/test_flash_attn_sm89_d512.py` and `python benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention_d512.py` after building.

Related to #2581. This PR covers the FA2 training path; paged-KV support requested there remains open.

title: [CuTe, SM100, HD256] optimize SM100 HD256 varlen scheduling and epilogues
body:
## Summary

- Bound dedicated SM100/SM110 HD256 varlen forward, dQ, and dK/dV grids by runtime maximum sequence lengths instead of packed total-token extents.
- Preserve packed output alignment for vector stores.
- Use TMA stores for complete 128-row dQ tiles while retaining predicate stores for ragged tails.
- Add targeted MQA correctness coverage for complete and ragged tiles under causal and noncausal masking.

This closes #2521. Thanks to @horakka5 for the original root-cause analysis and reproducer.

## Why

The dedicated HD256 kernels used the packed `total_q` / `total_k` extents to size each batch's grid. For a packed input with `B` equal-length sequences this launches approximately `B` times more M tiles than necessary, with most CTAs exiting after reading `cu_seqlens`.

After fixing the grid, packed-varlen epilogues become visible in short-sequence profiles:

- Forward used `domain_offset` for the runtime packed-row offset, which discarded the alignment proof needed by `autovec_copy`.
- Backward constructed a dQ TMA destination only for fixed-length inputs. Every varlen dQ tile therefore used the predicate global-store path, including complete tiles that cannot cross a sequence boundary.

The change keeps the physical packed tensor extents unchanged. Runtime maximum sequence lengths are used only for grid sizing. Within a sequence, complete dQ tiles use TMA; the final partial tile keeps the bounds-checked path.

## Benchmark protocol

- GPU: NVIDIA GB200, SM100
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- CUDA: 13.0
- CUTLASS DSL: 4.5.2
- dtype: BF16
- packed-varlen layout: `Q=[B*S,Hq,256]`, `K/V=[B*S,1,256]`
- `Hkv=1`, dropout disabled, softcap disabled
- seed: `20260814`
- `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=16`
- 20 warmups per phase
- 5 retained trials; reported latency is the median
- 50 timed iterations per trial for `S <= 8K`, otherwise 20
- FA4 HD256 backward uses `deterministic=False` because the current upstream kernel rejects deterministic mode

The baseline is upstream main before this PR. Commit `0251105` only changes dependency requirements; its HD256 kernels are identical to the measured `145b101` baseline.

MFU uses the repository's historical GB200 roofline:

- compute peak: 2.5 PFLOP/s
- HBM peak: 8 TB/s
- BWD useful FLOPs: `2.5 * FWD FLOPs`
- BWD `exec` is the useful MFU multiplied by 1.4 to reflect the split dQ + dK/dV kernel work

## Forward results

| Shape `(B,S,Hq)` | Mask | Baseline latency | Fixed latency | Speedup | Baseline MFU | Fixed MFU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `(32,1K,8)` | Causal | 1.662 ms | 0.683 ms | **2.43x** | 4.0% | **9.8%** |
| `(32,1K,8)` | Noncausal | 1.699 ms | 0.727 ms | **2.34x** | 6.5% | **15.1%** |
| `(4,8K,8)` | Causal | 1.223 ms | 1.131 ms | 1.08x | 36.0% | 38.9% |
| `(4,8K,8)` | Noncausal | 1.938 ms | 1.994 ms | 0.97x | 45.4% | 44.1% |
| `(1,32K,8)` | Causal | 3.401 ms | 3.389 ms | 1.00x | 51.7% | 51.9% |
| `(1,32K,8)` | Noncausal | 6.259 ms | 6.384 ms | 0.98x | 56.2% | 55.1% |
| `(1,128K,1)` | Causal | 6.468 ms | 6.508 ms | 0.99x | 54.4% | 54.1% |
| `(1,128K,1)` | Noncausal | 12.249 ms | 12.217 ms | 1.00x | 57.4% | 57.6% |

## Backward results

BWD MFU is shown as `useful / exec`.

| Shape `(B,S,Hq)` | Mask | Baseline latency | Fixed latency | Speedup | Baseline MFU | Fixed MFU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `(32,1K,8)` | Causal | 2.033 ms | 0.680 ms | **2.99x** | 6.8% / 9.5% | **20.2% / 28.3%** |
| `(32,1K,8)` | Noncausal | 13.096 ms | 0.922 ms | **14.20x** | 2.1% / 2.9% | **29.8% / 41.8%** |
| `(4,8K,8)` | Causal | 3.312 ms | 3.252 ms | 1.02x | 33.2% / 46.5% | 33.8% / 47.3% |
| `(4,8K,8)` | Noncausal | 14.332 ms | 5.775 ms | **2.48x** | 15.3% / 21.5% | **38.1% / 53.3%** |
| `(1,32K,8)` | Causal | 11.932 ms | 12.000 ms | 0.99x | 36.9% / 51.6% | 36.7% / 51.3% |
| `(1,32K,8)` | Noncausal | 22.180 ms | 22.574 ms | 0.98x | 39.7% / 55.5% | 39.0% / 54.6% |
| `(1,128K,1)` | Causal | 23.535 ms | 23.428 ms | 1.00x | 37.4% / 52.3% | 37.5% / 52.6% |
| `(1,128K,1)` | Noncausal | 42.824 ms | 43.259 ms | 0.99x | 41.1% / 57.5% | 40.7% / 56.9% |

The shape dependence matches the expected mechanism:

- Many short sequences benefit strongly because the old grid multiplies packed totals by batch size.
- At `B=1`, grid sizing is unchanged and attention computation dominates, so differences are within normal run-to-run variation.
- Complete dQ tiles benefit from TMA; only sequence tails retain predicate stores.

## Correctness

The regression test covers:

- sequence lengths `(128, 256)`: complete 128-row tiles
- sequence lengths `(129, 257)`: ragged tails
- causal and noncausal masks
- MQA with `Hq/Hkv=4/1`
- forward output and backward `dQ/dK/dV` against PyTorch SDPA

Result on GB200:

```text
4 passed
```

- [x] Full HD256 packed-varlen benchmark matrix shown above
- [x] `git diff --check`

title: [CuTe, SM90] hdim256 backward: C++ FA3 dQ path and 2-CTA DSMEM dS exchange (373 → 530 TFLOP/s)
body:
## Summary

This PR takes the CuTe SM90 backward at head_dim 256 from 373 to 530 TFLOP/s (dense bf16, S=16k, H200), 1.42x, past the C++ FA3 kernel (480 TFLOP/s on the same GPU), with unchanged numerics. It is the follow-up to #2888, which fixed the swapped postprocess layout and moved hdim 256 to a 2-stage 64x48 config (302 → 373 TFLOP/s). The two optimization commits are independently useful:

1. **C++ FA3's hdim256 dQ path** (`BwdConfig.dQacc_use_TMA=False`). No smem staging of dQ: the MMA warp groups reduce the dQ accumulator straight into `dQaccum` with `red.global.add.v4.f32`, partitioned by the same R2S tiled copy as the smem path, so the gmem layout and the postprocess are unchanged. dQ is computed in two hdim halves into the same registers (C++ `Slice_dQKV_Mma`; with two accumulators ptxas hoists the second WGMMA above the atomics and dV spills at tile_n=80). The freed 64 KB is what lets the C++ tile (64x80, 2-stage Q) fit. 373 → 471 TFLOP/s, C++ FA3 is 480 on the same GPU.
2. **FA4's 2-CTA dS exchange, on Hopper via DSMEM** (`BwdConfig.cluster_size=2`). With the atomics compiled out the 1-CTA kernel runs at 747 TFLOP/s, so what remains is the fp32 reduce traffic into dQaccum (`S² · d · 4 B / tile_n` per head; a single SM sustains only ~30 GB/s of `red.add`). The two CTAs of a cluster take KV blocks n and n^1 of one head, walk the union of their m-block ranges in lockstep and exchange their dS tiles through distributed shared memory (`cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster`, mbarrier full/empty handshake with remote arrive/expect_tx). CTA r then computes `dQ[:, 128r:128r+128] = dS_own @ K_own[:, half] + dS_peer @ K_peer[:, half]` (K = 2·tile_n) and reduces only its half: half the atomics and half the dQ registers at the same tile_n. Splitting by head-dim halves rather than query rows (FA4's Blackwell variant) needs only the peer's K half (20 KB) in smem, which is what makes 64x80 fit exactly (232,448 B). Q and dO are TMA-multicast to the pair. Odd block counts use a "ghost" partner that participates in every barrier with fully masked columns (dS = 0), flushes its dQ half, and skips the dK/dV epilogue. 471 → 530 TFLOP/s.

The pair's fixed cost only pays off once the m-block loop is long enough, so `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` selects the 2-CTA kernel for `seqlen_q >= 2048` (max_seqlen_q for varlen) and keeps the 1-CTA 64x80 config below (measured crossover, table below). Deterministic and block-sparse backward keep the semaphore-ordered smem-staged path, matching the C++ restriction `Deterministic && kHeadDim < 256`. Forward and hdim ≤ 192 are untouched.

A third commit rounds `seqlen_k_rounded` straight to `n_block_size * cluster_size` instead of fixing up the parity of the n-block count. The old form branched on `max_seqlen_k`, which callers may pass as a device tensor (HF/TE varlen): that synced, and raised `DataDependentOutputException` in the FakeTensorMode compile pass. The rounding is the same value and does not branch. The SM100 2-CTA backward has the same issue; the SM90 cluster config added here reaches it from the varlen path.

New surface: two `BwdConfig` fields (`dQacc_use_TMA`, `cluster_size`) and two `FlashAttentionBackwardSm90` constructor arguments of the same names, both selected in `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` (which gains `deterministic` and `seqlen_q` keyword arguments). No public API change.

## Results

H200 (132 SMs, 227 KB smem; CUDA 12.8, torch 2.10, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1), bf16, backward, ms · TFLOP/s:

| | `main` (before #2888) | #2888 | commit 1 (1-CTA) | commit 2 (2-CTA) | C++ FA3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense S=16384 H=16 D=256 | 36.5 · 302 | 29.5 · 373 | 23.3 · 471 | **20.8 · 530** | 22.9 · 480 |
