title: fix(attention): accept non-contiguous index tensors in plan()
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`plan()` passes user-supplied index tensors (`indptr` / `indices` / `last_page_len`) to the C++ planner and the kernels as raw data pointers without checking contiguity. A strided view (e.g. `indptr_full[::2]`) is therefore misread, in two ways:

- **CUDA inputs**: in non-CUDA-graph mode, `self._*_buf = indptr.to(self.device)` is a no-op for a strided CUDA view, so the kernel buffers stay strided. `indptr.to("cpu")`, on the other hand, returns a *contiguous* host copy for the planner. The plan and the kernel then disagree about the layout.
- **CPU inputs**: `.to("cpu")` is a no-op, so the strided host tensor goes straight into the C++ planner.

Measured on H200 (SM90) with stride-2 views holding identical values (fp16, 8/2 heads, head_dim 128, page_size 16, 4 requests):

| wrapper / backend | strided metadata on CUDA | strided metadata on CPU |
|---|---|---|
| Ragged prefill, fa2 | illegal memory access | `PrefillSplitQOKVIndptr` check fails |
| Ragged prefill, fa3 | OK | `PrefillSM90Plan` check fails |
| Paged prefill, fa2 | illegal memory access | `PrefillSplitQOKVIndptr` check fails |
| Paged prefill, fa3 | wrong output (max abs diff 3.3) | `PrefillSM90Plan` check fails |
| Paged decode, CUDA cores | wrong output (max abs diff 3.0) | wrong output (max abs diff 4.6), no error |
| Paged decode, tensor cores | wrong output (max abs diff 2.6) | `PrefillSplitQOKVIndptr` check fails |
| `BlockSparseAttentionWrapper` (auto) | fails (not isolated: ran after an IMA in the same process) | wrong output (93% of elements mismatched) |

**Fix:** call `.contiguous()` on the index tensors at the top of `plan()` in:
- `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.plan`: `qo_indptr`, `paged_kv_indptr`, `paged_kv_indices`, `paged_kv_last_page_len`
- `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.plan`: `qo_indptr`, `kv_indptr`, and the optional `o_indptr` / `v_indptr`
- `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper._plan_impl` and `fast_decode_plan`: `indptr`, `indices`, `last_page_len`
- `BlockSparseAttentionWrapper.plan`: `indptr`, `indices`
- `seq_lens` (when given) in the paged prefill `plan()` and decode `_plan_impl`: it is copied to the host with `seq_lens.cpu()`, which is a no-op for a strided CPU view, and the host copy goes to the native planner. With fa3 paged prefill a strided CPU `seq_lens` was an illegal memory access.
- `workspace_size()` on the paged prefill and decode wrappers, which mirrors `plan()`'s host copies: the same tensors, including `seq_lens`. Without it, strided CPU indptrs failed the native size query's `PrefillSplitQOKVIndptr` check (tensor-core decode, fa2 prefill). Thanks to the CodeRabbit review for flagging this one.

These tensors are tiny, and `plan()` already copies them between host and device. `.contiguous()` returns `self` for contiguous inputs, so the usual path is unchanged. The CUDA-graph paths `copy_()` into preallocated buffers and were already correct.

Out of scope:
- The MLA planner already rejects non-contiguous metadata (`mla/_batch_mla/_planning.py`).
- `VariableBlockSparseAttentionWrapper` builds its own indptr via `cat`/`cumsum`, so it is always contiguous.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #5260

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New file `tests/attention/test_plan_noncontiguous_metadata.py` (28 cases): ragged and paged prefill (fa2/fa3), paged decode (with and without tensor cores), and block-sparse, with metadata on CUDA and on CPU, and with and without `seq_lens` for paged prefill and decode. Each case plans the same problem with contiguous metadata and with stride-2 views of the same values, then compares outputs. A `workspace_size()` case checks that strided and contiguous metadata give the same sizes.
- Before the fix: every case that uses strided metadata in a path that reads it raw fails (IMA / planner error / mismatch).
- After the fix: 28/28 pass (H200, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.14).

Regression check on H200: a sampled subset of `tests/attention/test_batch_prefill_kernels.py`, `test_batch_decode_kernels.py`, `test_block_sparse.py`, and `test_batch_prefill.py`. All cases of functions with ≤300 parametrizations (including CUDA-graph decode, `fast_plan`, custom mask, and multi-item scoring), plus every 25th case of the large sweeps, for 1,648 cases in total: **1,240 passed, 408 skipped, 0 failed** (rebased on `2268a1ae`). After the follow-up commit, the same subset plus `tests/attention/test_workspace_size.py`: **1,251 passed, 407 skipped, 0 failed**.

## Reviewer Notes

- I chose to normalize rather than raise (`ValueError`, like the MLA planner) so that callers that currently pass strided views keep working. Ragged fa3 with CUDA metadata happened to be correct before this change. Happy to switch to rejecting if maintainers prefer a strict contract.
- The C++ launchers still don't check contiguity (`CHECK_INPUT`) on indptr. This PR keeps the change at the Python boundary. Adding C++ checks would also cover direct callers of the low-level modules, and could be a follow-up.

title: fix(attention): pre-scale P by 2^8 before e4m3 quantization in SM120 prims FP8 prefill
body:
## 📌 Description

The SM120 `cute-dsl-prims` FP8 prefill kernel converts the softmax matrix P
(values in (0, 1]) directly to e4m3 for the PV MMA, while the softmax
denominator `row_sum` is accumulated from the **unquantized fp32** P. In e4m3,
values below 2^-10 round to zero and values below 2^-6 land on the subnormal
staircase (2^-9 absolute steps). As a result, diffuse softmax mass silently
vanishes from the **numerator only**: the output is biased toward the hot
tokens, while the LSE stays exact — the bug is invisible to both random-input
tests and LSE-based correctness checks.

The SM100 cute-dsl backend already guards against this with a P × 2^8
pre-scale (`p_fp8_prescale_log2 = floor(log2(448))` in
`flashinfer/cute_dsl/attention/fmha/fmha.py`). This PR ports the same scheme
to SM120:

- Add `P_FP8_PRESCALE_LOG2 = 8.0` to
  `flashinfer/cute_dsl/attention/fmha/sm120/fmha_prefill_fp8_tma.py`.
- Add the offset to the exp2 exponent in both softmax implementations
  (`online_softmax`, `online_softmax_single_buffer`), so both the PV MMA
  operand and `row_sum` pick up the same 2^8 factor. It cancels in
  `O = acc / row_sum`, so the epilogue is unchanged.
- Subtract the offset at the (single) LSE writeout to keep the LSE exact.

Safety notes (audited against the kernel structure):
- Masked entries: `-inf * scale + 8 = -inf` → `exp2` still yields 0.
- `old_scale` (running-max rescale) is a ratio of exponentials of maxima and
  is unaffected by the constant offset.
- No saturation: `P <= 1` → `P * 256 <= 256 < 448`, so `cvt.rn.satfinite`
  never clamps.

## Evidence

**1. V=1 regression** (all values set to 1, so the correct output is exactly
1; tail-hot plateau, N=32768, 4 hot tokens, tail at 7.07-nat deficit — every
tail weight is exp(-7.071) = 8.49e-4 < 2^-10, i.e. exactly on the flush
boundary):

| | output (should be 1) | LSE error |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0.1257 (= 4 / (4 + 32764·e^-7.071), the analytic no-prescale value) | 0.0 (bit-exact) |
| after  | 1.0049 | 0.0 |

Before the fix the kernel returns the analytic no-prescale value to fp16
precision — 87.4% of the softmax mass is dropped from the numerator while
`row_sum` keeps it, and the LSE is bit-exact, which is why every existing
check passed.

**2. Structured (tail-hot) attention, N=32768** (4 hot tokens at the KV tail
+ diffuse correlated tail; relative rms output error. The kernel walks KV
tiles right-to-left, so tail-hot is the worst case):

| logit deficit | before | after | reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.07 | 100% | 0.6% | ~164x |
| 9.19 | 88% | 1.0% | ~39x |
| 6.36 | 13% | 0.8% | ~17x |
| 5.66 | 12% | 2.2% | ~5x |

**3. Random inputs** (gaussian / production-style per-tensor-quantized):
relative rms error ~1–3% both before and after — dominated by e4m3's
normal-range 3-bit mantissa, i.e. the pre-scale neither helps nor hurts
there. This is why the existing random-input tests cannot catch the defect
and why the new regression tests use structured inputs.

## 🔍 Related Issues

None.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Added `tests/attention/test_sm120_prims_prescale.py` — two structured-input
regression tests (SM120 + cutlass-dsl>=4.7.0 gated, like the existing SM120
tests):

- `test_tail_hot_all_ones_values`: V=1 tail-hot plateau; asserts output ≈ 1
  (atol 2e-2; reads 0.365 before the fix) **and** LSE against an fp32
  reference (guards the −8 LSE correction).
- `test_tail_hot_correlated_values`: correlated-V tail-hot plateau; asserts
  relative rms error < 3% (93% before the fix).

Verified on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), CUDA 12.8, torch 2.14.0,
nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1:

```
pytest -v tests/attention/test_sm120_prims_prescale.py
# 2 passed, 4 warnings in 1.14s

pytest -v tests/attention/test_sm120_fmha.py \
          tests/attention/test_sm120_fmha_paged.py \
          tests/attention/test_sm120_prims_prefill_backend.py
# 53 passed, 50 warnings in 60.13s
```

## Reviewer Notes

- The regression tests deliberately avoid random inputs: the defect only
  manifests when a few hot tokens sit ~7 nats above a long, diffuse,
  value-correlated tail, which random tensors do not produce.
- Numerics were cross-validated with an independent chunked-online-softmax
  simulation of the kernel (right-to-left tile order, 128-token tiles): on
  the structured configs the pre-fix kernel output matched the no-prescale
  simulation elementwise, and the post-fix output matches the pre-scale
  simulation. Full investigation write-up (all measurement tables, analysis
  script) available on request.

* **Tests**
  * Added regression coverage for FP8 attention precision, including concentrated, distributed, and tail-focused softmax value patterns.
  * Verified attention outputs and log-sum-exp results against FP32 reference calculations.

title: [PrimsTS] MxFp8-MMA backed blockscale FP8
body:
## 📌 Description

Adds an explicit PrimsTS recipe for running DeepSeek FP8 checkpoints with
native MXFP8 block-scale MMA while retaining compact FP32 checkpoint weight
scales. FC1 fuses SwiGLU and MXFP8 quantization, and FC2 consumes the MXFP8
interstage directly. Existing true DSFP8 and true MXFP8 paths remain unchanged.

On B200 with the DeepSeek EP=4 shape, MX-backed DSFP8 is faster than true
DSFP8 at all eight measured token counts: 1.038x-1.999x, with a 1.3704x
geometric mean. It remains slower than true MXFP8 in every measured bucket.

Note: 
- FC1 weights require the recipe-specific gated-row reorder followed by `shuffle_matrix_a(..., epilogue_tile_m=128)`
- FP32 checkpoint scales are approximated as UE8M0 and still require model-quality validation.

## 🔍 Related Issues

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used my preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] The applicable commit hooks, Ruff checks, formatting checks, and `git diff --check` pass.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] The focused host, trace, and B200 device tests pass.

Device validation used B200/SM100. The focused host and trace suites pass 742
tests. The focused device suite passes 11 tests covering staged scale loading,
partial K and K512, tile-N256 equivalence, logits and pre-routed public entry
points, and end-to-end comparison with true DeepSeek FP8. Host coverage also
verifies that capacity-invalid tactics are rejected before autotuning.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE=$PWD/.cache
export MAX_JOBS=8

python -m pytest -q -n0 \
  tests/prims_ts/test_moe_compile_cache.py \
  tests/trace/test_trtllm_mxfp8_moe_trace.py \
  tests/trace/test_fi_trace_template_consistency.py \
  tests/prims_ts/test_moe_fp8_block_support.py \
  tests/prims_ts/test_moe_runner_ffi_tensors.py \
  tests/prims_ts/test_moe_api_signature.py

python -m pytest -q -n0 \
  tests/prims_ts/test_batched_gemm_dsfp8_mxfp8.py \
  tests/moe/test_prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_moe.py::test_prims_ts_deepseek_native_mxfp8_tile8_stays_close_to_true_dsfp8 \
  tests/moe/test_prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_moe.py::test_prims_ts_deepseek_native_mxfp8_tile256_matches_tile128 \
  tests/moe/test_prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_moe.py::test_prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_routed_modes_match_logits
```

For identical seeded inputs, weights, and routing, comparison with true
DeepSeek FP8 measures relative L2 `0.0742` when checkpoint scales are exactly
UE8M0-representable. With ordinary FP32 checkpoint scales, it measures relative
L2 `0.370858`, cosine similarity `0.947360`, and output-norm ratio `1.134513`.

## Reviewer Notes

### Implementation details

- Add the keyword-only `use_mxfp8_backed_dsfp8` option to logits-based and
  pre-routed PrimsTS FP8 block-scale MoE entry points, including trace support.
- Load compact FP32 checkpoint weight scales through staged SMEM-to-TMEM
  conversion with partial-K predication. Native activation scales support
  LINEAR, R8c4, and R128c4 layouts.
- Use independent one-warp SFA/SFB loaders and four-warp copy groups that
  publish into separate TMEM scale rings with independent lifetimes.
- Fuse FC1 SwiGLU and MXFP8 output quantization so FC2 directly consumes E4M3
  values with UE8M0 K32 scales. No pre-expanded weight-scale workspace or
  standalone activation-conversion kernel is required.
- Add complete same-tile FC1/FC2 tactics for tile-N 8 through 256, including
  2-CTA/MMA-M256 variants. Routing metadata and both GEMMs use the tile-N
  selected for the complete tactic.
- Validate FC1 and FC2 schedule capacity before compilation or timing, and fix
  tile-N256 warp realization and accumulator lifetime.
- Register every tactic in the ordinary JSON catalog. Generated tactic indices
  use the standard cache and routing path without recipe-specific IDs or
  token-count overrides.
- Remove the environment selector and the pre-expanded GMEM recipe. Static
  weight preparation and execution use the same explicit recipe contract.

Recipe selection is explicit because it changes the activation-scale and FC1
weight-shuffle contracts.

### Usage

Prepare FC1 input as E4M3 with token-major UE8M0 K32 scales. For each FC1
expert, apply `reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm` to the logical `[gate; up]`
rows, then apply `shuffle_matrix_a(..., epilogue_tile_m=128)` to the byte view.
Keep the compact FP32 FC1 scale tensor in checkpoint order.

```python
from flashinfer.fused_moe import prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_moe
from flashinfer.tllm_enums import Fp8QuantizationType

output = prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_moe(
    routing_logits=routing_logits,
    routing_bias=routing_bias,
    hidden_states=hidden_states_mxfp8,
    hidden_states_scale=hidden_states_scale_ue8m0,
    gemm1_weights=gemm1_weights,
    gemm1_weights_scale=gemm1_weights_scale_fp32,
    gemm2_weights=gemm2_weights,
    gemm2_weights_scale=gemm2_weights_scale_fp32,
    num_experts=256,
    top_k=8,
    n_group=8,
    topk_group=4,
    intermediate_size=2048,
    local_expert_offset=0,
    local_num_experts=64,
    routed_scaling_factor=None,
    use_shuffled_weight=True,
    fp8_quantization_type=Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8,
    use_mxfp8_backed_dsfp8=True,
)
```

`prims_ts_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe` exposes the same option for packed and
unpacked precomputed routing inputs. The option cannot be combined with
`Fp8QuantizationType.MxFp8`.

### Detailed performance

Measurements cover routing, FC1, fused activation and quantization, FC2, and
finalization on one exclusive 1000 W B200. The DeepSeek shape uses hidden size
7168, intermediate size 2048, 256 global and 64 local experts (EP=4), and top-k
8. Each token bucket uses a complete-tactic autotuner winner with one shared
tile-N. Timings use CUDA graphs, cold-L2 eviction, 10 warmups, 50 samples per
round, and the median of five order-balanced round medians. The full sweep used
Python 3.12, Torch 2.12, and CUDA 13.2. Lower latency is better.

| Tokens | MX-backed DSFP8 (us) | True DSFP8 (us) | True MXFP8 (us) | Speedup vs DSFP8 |
|-------:|----------------------:|----------------:|----------------:|------------------:|
| 8 | 29.947 | 32.106 | 26.374 | 1.072x |
| 64 | 43.574 | 45.213 | 31.901 | 1.038x |
| 128 | 46.798 | 51.152 | 35.992 | 1.093x |
| 256 | 54.434 | 67.432 | 44.992 | 1.239x |
| 512 | 73.326 | 103.888 | 60.352 | 1.417x |
| 1024 | 107.669 | 164.922 | 79.522 | 1.532x |
| 4096 | 241.664 | 460.130 | 177.507 | 1.904x |
| 8192 | 442.730 | 884.838 | 311.294 | 1.999x |

| Tokens | FC1 kernel | FC2 kernel |
|-------:|------------|------------|

title: fix(benchmarks): benchmark the CUTLASS ragged prefill backend eagerly
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Since #5133, `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper` refuses `backend="cutlass"` with `use_cuda_graph=True`, because `fmha_varlen_plan` allocates its plan buffers on every `plan()` call and a captured graph would replay against a stale plan. The ragged-prefill benchmark routine still built the CUTLASS wrapper with the routine-wide graph flag, since only `fa2` was special-cased. As a result, any `--backends` list containing `cutlass` stopped during wrapper preparation with:

```
the cutlass backend allocates its plan buffers per plan() call and is not CUDA-graph safe; use backend='auto' to get a graph-safe backend, or an explicit 'cudnn'/'fa2'
```

No backend in the run produced results, not just `cutlass`.

This PR keeps the wrapper's guard and changes only the benchmark. In `testBatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, `cutlass` now joins `fa2` in a small `eager_only_backends` set:
- its wrapper is created with `use_cuda_graph=False`;
- `bench_gpu_time` times it without graph capture;
- an `[INFO]` line says so, when graph mode is on and `cutlass` is in the list.

The other backends in the same run still use graph replay. `--no_cuda_graph` behaves exactly as before. Other routines are unaffected: the MLA routine's `cutlass` path has no equivalent guard, and the paged routine doesn't offer `cutlass`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #5284

1. **The DeepSeek-R1 command from the issue** runs to completion with and without `--no_cuda_graph` and reports `fa2`, `fa3`, and `cudnn` results. On SM90, `cutlass` and `trtllm-native` are filtered out by compute capability, so this shows the routine is intact but doesn't exercise the CUTLASS branch.
2. **CUTLASS control flow, exercised on SM90 with a stand-in.** A small harness disables the compute-capability filter and substitutes the `cutlass` wrapper with a subclass. The subclass records the requested `use_cuda_graph`, raises the same `ValueError` as the real wrapper when graph mode is requested, and otherwise runs fa2. The harness also records the `use_cuda_graph` flag passed to each `bench_gpu_time` call. Command: `--backends fa2 fa3 cutlass`, bf16, causal, 4×512 tokens, 16 heads, head_dim 128.

| this PR, graph mode | False / True / **False** | False / True / **False** | all three timed |
| this PR, `--no_cuda_graph` | False / False / False | False / False / False | all three timed |

title: Test Pruning Infrastructure to Separate Regular/Full Test Suites
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

This change introduces regular and full modes for large Cartesian pytest parameter matrices:

- A normal `pytest` invocation runs a reduced, deterministic selection of cases.
- Passing `--full` restores the complete Cartesian parameter matrices.
- The nightly test script passes `--full`, so nightly coverage remains complete.

The implementation adds a shared `parametrize_product` helper and registers the `--full` pytest option through the existing test configuration. The helper also supports grouped parameters, such as `(num_q_heads, num_kv_heads)`, that must remain coupled rather than being expanded as independent axes.

To run full test suites manually, set `PYTEST_ADDOPTS="--full"` before launching tests.

Also to tune memory-aware JIT parallelism for parallel workers and retain lightweight timing and resource telemetry.

This is a clone of PR#5313 to introduce the regular/full pruning mechanism without the change to the test suite yet.

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

## 🔍 Related Issues

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5313

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below with your targets.
     Do not delete the fence or change its `experimental-tests` tag — the experimental-track
     watcher reads it verbatim to decide which targets to ask CI for. -->

```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.
#
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

The regular cases are selected independently for each test using deterministic pairwise coverage (a strength-2 covering array). They are not sampled globally from the complete set of test nodes.

A full Cartesian product covers every higher-order interaction across all parameter axes, but grows exponentially. Selecting only one occurrence of every individual value is much cheaper, but can leave parameter values correlated and miss important two-parameter interactions. Pairwise coverage is the compromise:

> For every pair of parameter axes, every combination of their values appears in at least one regular case.

For example, three binary axes have eight full combinations. The following four cases cover every pair of values across `A/B`, `A/C`, and `B/C`:

```text
A0 B0 C0
A0 B1 C1
A1 B0 C1
A1 B1 C0
```

The selector:

1. Builds the set of all required value-pairs across every pair of axes.
2. Generates deterministic candidate rows containing each required pair.
3. Fills the remaining positions deterministically without materializing the complete Cartesian product.
4. Repeatedly selects the candidate covering the most uncovered pairs.
5. Stops when every required pair has appeared.

This greedy algorithm is deterministic and reproducible, although it does not guarantee the mathematically smallest possible covering array. Grouped parameter values remain atomic, preserving the valid combinations from the original tests.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- **New Features**
  - Added an optional full parameter-matrix test mode for comprehensive validation.
  - Added configurable JIT build parallelism to better manage host resource usage during testing.
  - Expanded test artifacts with telemetry, metadata, CPU, load, process, and memory details.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated testing guidance to distinguish regular and full test suites.
  - Documented the new JIT parallelism configuration option.

- **Tests**
  - Improved parameterized test coverage while reducing unnecessary combinations in regular test runs.

title: ci(docs): never deploy a release candidate to the stable docs site
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The docs deploy job fires on any non-empty `release_tag`, which includes `vX.Y.ZrcN`. `docs.flashinfer.ai` is the **stable** documentation site, so an rc would publish an unreleased API surface to every reader.

This guards the deploy on the tag not being a release candidate:

```yaml
if: inputs.release_tag != '' && !contains(inputs.release_tag, 'rc')
```

Docs still **build** for an rc — only the publish step is skipped — so a broken doc build is still caught before the final tag, which is what that job is most useful for.

### Why this has not bitten us yet — and the other half of the problem

The deploy job has never actually run. It declares `environment: github-pages`, whose deployment branch policy permits `gh-pages` and `main`, while the Release workflow is dispatched against `release-vX.Y.Z`. A called workflow inherits the **caller's** ref, so GitHub refuses the job before allocating a runner: **0 steps, no runner, no log**. Fetching that job's log returns an Azure `BlobNotFound`, which reads like a storage error but is just the missing log of a job that never started.

Evidence from the v0.7.0rc3 release run:

- deployment created with `ref=release-v0.7.0`, sha `03296170`, at `10:22:45Z`
- job `deploy-docs / Deploy Docs` failed at `10:22:46Z` — 1 second, 0 steps
- `deploy-docs / Build Docs` immediately before it: success
- `docs.flashinfer.ai` currently serves **0.6.18** (last modified 2026-09-08); no 0.7.0 docs exist, across rc1/rc2/rc3

Unblocking that is a **repository settings change**, not a workflow change: permit `release-v*` in the `github-pages` environment's deployment branch policy. That does not widen who can deploy — `deploy-docs` is already gated `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, so it is reachable only by someone who can dispatch the Release workflow.

This PR is the other half: once the deploy is unblocked, make sure the first thing it publishes is not an rc.

## 🔍 Related Issues

None filed. Happy to open one for the environment policy side if that is preferred over a settings change.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

CI-only change with no test surface. Verified by parsing the workflow and checking the resolved condition:

```
deploy.if: inputs.release_tag != '' && !contains(inputs.release_tag, 'rc')
```

Condition truth table for the tags this repo produces:

| `release_tag` | builds docs | deploys |
|---|---|---|
| `""` (push to main / PR) | yes | no (unchanged) |
| `v0.7.0rc3` | yes | **no (new)** |
| `v0.7.0` | yes | yes |
| `v0.6.18.post1` | yes | yes |

## 🔬 Experimental Track

N/A — not an experimental API or backend.

title: feat(cake_fmha): add BF16 head-dim-256 small-M speculative decode route
body:
## 📌 Description

Add the Cake FMHA route `decode_native_bf16_hd256_smallm_v1` to the `cake_fmha` package: BF16 Q/KV/O paged GQA decode with head_dim 256 and 17..64 packed (speculative token × head) rows per KV head in a 32- or 64-row tile (rows above the packed count are padding; the Q tensor-map box always fills the tile), selected through the existing `backend="cake"` entry points (`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache`, `cake_batch_decode_with_kv_cache`).  Target workload: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 2× B200 with TP=2, batch 1, ISL 60k, 7 draft tokens — per rank 8 query rows × 8 heads over one KV head.  Before this change that shape had no optimized Cake route and ran on `cake_fmha_compat_v1`.

Kernel (generated Cake kernel; upstream source and harness are tracked in the Cake kernel repository):
- all (token, head) pairs of a KV head are one swapped-AB MMA N tile, so K/V stream once per KV head;
- one resident wave of Split-KV CTAs (`NUM_SPLIT = min(#SMs // (batch·kv_heads), max(kv_blocks, rows), 256)`), BF16 partial `O` + FP32 base-2 LSE per row;
- fused distributed in-launch merge after a GPU-scope rendezvous (counters live in the caller workspace and are reset per launch, CUDA-graph safe);
- softmax reductions are in-thread after an SMEM transpose of the score tile.

Package changes:
- `csrc/cake_fmha/cuda/decode_native_bf16_hd256_smallm_n{32,64}_p{16,32,64}/{sm_100a,sm_103a}/default.cu` and their `bindings/*_binding.cu` (six generated structural instances);
- `csrc/cake_fmha/jit/cake_fmha_decode_native_bf16_hd256_smallm_jit_binding.cu`: packed 4-D query and 5-D HND KV tensor maps, partial/counter/LSE workspace layout, one-wave launch; unsupported options (sinks, windows, device scales, NHD, block scales, block-sparse) fail closed;
- `csrc/cake_fmha/manifest.json` gains the six components, the route and their artifact digests; `include/cake_fmha.h` declares the six launch bindings; `flashinfer/jit/cake_fmha.py` manifest/bindings digests updated;
- `flashinfer/cake_fmha.py`: route selection (`decode_native_bf16_hd256_smallm`, `16 < q_len·group ≤ 64` with the GQA group dividing the tile, page 16/32/64, HND, shared page table, `batch·kv_heads·NUM_SPLIT ≤ SMs`), loader, registry tables; `flashinfer/jit/cake_fmha.py`: JIT spec generator/loader (`-DQ_LEN -DGROUP -DQ_BOX_ROWS -DNUM_SPLIT -DCAKE_FMHA_SMALLM_N_ROWS`).
- Pinned FlashInfer main-matrix accounting moves 6 cells from compatibility to this route (1,798 → 1,804 optimized / 55,482 → 55,476 compatibility; the pinned corpus digest is updated). The SGLang NEXTN verify batch for 7 draft tokens has 7 query rows per request (56 packed rows), which is why the tile is padded instead of requiring exactly 32 or 64 rows.

Kernel-level measurements (B200, cold-L2 CUPTI medians from the Cake benchmark harness; correctness against the paged-attention torch reference, BF16 `atol=rtol=1e-2`):

| Shape | trtllm-gen backend | `cake_fmha_compat_v1` | this route |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| batch 1, kv 60,007, q 7, Hq 8 / Hkv 1, page 64 (SGLang verify shape, 56 rows) | 43.3 µs | — | **26.9 µs** |
| batch 1, kv 60,008, q 8, Hq 8 / Hkv 1, page 64 | 40.8 µs | 123,645 µs | **26.4 µs** |
| same, page 16 | 40.9 µs | 123,515 µs | 26.9 µs |
| batch 1, kv 8,200, q 8 | 15.0 µs | 16,896 µs | 14.0 µs |
| batch 1, kv 1,032, q 8 | 10.0 µs | 2,091 µs | 15.1 µs |
| batch 1, kv 60,004, q 4, Hq 16 / Hkv 2 | 41.8 µs | 115,874 µs | 33.5 µs |
| batch 1, kv 60,004, q 4, Hq 8 / Hkv 1 (32 rows) | 34.8 µs | 123,805 µs | 25.0 µs |
| batch 1, kv 60,003, q 3, Hq 8 / Hkv 1 (24 rows in the 32-row tile) | 37.4 µs | — | 24.9 µs |

**Correctness fix in the regenerated bodies (latest two commits):** the kernel's shared-memory `P^T` tile was single-buffered with no consumer-release barrier. The MMA warp issues `QK(n+1)` ahead of `PV(n)`, so the softmax warps could overwrite block n's probabilities with block n+1's before `PV(n)` had read them; whenever a KV split streams more than one 128-token block (the 60k target streams 3–4) whole packed rows accumulated the wrong probabilities. A one-hot FP32-reference check (one planted key per packed row so `|O| ≈ |V|`) found 81 of 744 rows wrong across 15 shape/seed cases before the fix and 0 after, bit-exact; random-input `atol=1e-2` checks never caught it because diffuse attention keeps `|O| ≈ 5e-3`. The fix is a consumer-release mbarrier (MMA commits after the PV pair, softmax waits before its P store). The earlier commit's double-buffered O-rescale factor (same hazard class) stays but did not change the numerics on its own. Latency is unchanged (60k q 7: 26.8 µs vs 43.4 µs trtllm-gen). Validated from this branch on B200 (sglang:26.07 container, JIT from source): the six GPU small-M tests pass, and the same one-hot sweep through `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(backend="cake")` is bit-exact at 1, 2, 3 and 3–4 blocks per split (kv 18,944 / 37,888 / 56,832 / 60,007 with q 7; kv 60,003 q 3; kv 8,200 q 8), with diffuse-input rel-L2 0.0027 at every length (0.16–0.28 before the fix).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to the `cake_fmha` product integration; target workload: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B speculative decode on B200 TP=2.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added as needed.
- [x] All focused tests passed on the intended hardware.

Validated on NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13 container `nvcr.io/nvidia/sglang:26.07-py3`, this branch head (bodies regenerated from the rebased Cake source) built from source (`pip install -e .`, JIT only, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0`):

- `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha.py -k "manifest or registry or smallm_jit or smallm_num_split or pinned_capability_corpus or q257"`: **17 passed** — manifest digest, registry/component accounting, pinned capability corpus replay (unchanged 1,798 / 55,482 split and digest), small-M JIT spec selection.
- `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha.py -k "smallm and (matches_flashinfer_reference or route_is_selected)"`: **6 passed** — five `_test_trtllm_batch_decode(backend="cake", head_dim=256)` shapes (batch 1 / q 7 / Hkv 1 / page 64 / kv 60k; batch 1 / q 8 / Hkv 1 / page 64 / kv 60k; page 16 / kv 8k; TP=1-style Hkv 2 / q 4; 32-row batch 2) plus the route-selection test that runs `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(backend="cake", q_len_per_req=8, return_lse=True)` on the 60k target and checks O and LSE against dense causal attention.
- Existing Cake decode tests (`test_cake_decode_bf16_matches_flashinfer_reference`, fully-masked row, fp16 NHD, fp16 hd512; `-k "test_cake_decode_bf16_matches_flashinfer_reference or fully_masked or fp16_nhd or hd512"`): **12 passed**.
- Not run here: full `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha.py`, compute-sanitizer. Repository CI needs maintainer authorization (`@flashinfer-bot run`).

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] `pre-commit` check passes on the PR head (`ruff format` fix applied to the two Python files it flagged).

## Notes

- This PR carries the focused six-component merge; the Cake product lane regenerates the whole `cake_fmha` export/manifest from its release head and re-runs its final gates (sanitizer, full job matrix) separately. The bodies here were regenerated after the upstream Cake change was rebased onto its current main (the generated warp/lane prelude changed); generated bindings were byte-identical, only the six kernel bodies and their manifest digests moved.

title: refactor(kda): unify the two recurrent_kda facades onto one decode dispatcher
body:
## What this does

FlashInfer exports two public functions named `recurrent_kda` —
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda` and `flashinfer.kda_decode.recurrent_kda` — which shared a trace
label, defaulted to different backends, and each carried their own copy of the decode
contract. This puts one dispatcher underneath both and deprecates the older facade.

Step 8's *removal* half is not here: deprecate-then-remove spans two releases by
construction.

## Issues 

#4936 

## Commits

Each is independently revertible, so a contested piece can be dropped without restructuring
the rest.

| | Commit | Step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Factor one shared decode dispatcher | 4 |
| 2 | Explain why the decode facade rejects `backend="cudnn"` | 4 |
| 3 | Trace the two facades under distinct names | 6 |
| 4 | Deprecate `flashinfer.kda_decode.recurrent_kda` | 5 |
| 5 | Point KDA tests and benchmarks at the canonical facade | 7 |
| 6 | Stop exporting the `kda_kernels` noun aliases | 8 |
| 7–8 | Correct and consolidate the KDA docs | 8 |

## Notes for reviewers

**The dispatcher extraction is mechanical, not a semantic reconciliation.** The decode facade's
parameter set is a strict subset of the top-level facade's, and both shared exits already
passed byte-identical arguments — 21 kwargs to `_run_frozen_recurrent_kda` and 22 to
`_run_recurrent_kda`. Every dispatcher parameter is keyword-only *without a default*, so a
caller that forgets to forward one raises `TypeError` rather than silently taking a default
the other facade would not have used.

**One deliberate behaviour change and one error-message reordering.** `test_recurrent_kda.py`'s
47 calls never named a backend, so retargeting them to the canonical facade moves them from
`"cute-dsl"` onto `"auto"` — intended, since that is what callers get and #5037 made `"auto"`
a decode superset. Separately, when a `disable_state_update=True` call also passes
prefill-only arguments, the top-level-only guard now runs before the shared three, so a call
violating both rules reports a different one of the two. No test pins either message.

**The `backend` default becomes `None`.** *Omitting* it still resolves to `"cute-dsl"`, so no
working call changes meaning, but `None` records "not requested" in a way an explicit value
cannot — which is what lets a later release converge omitted calls onto `"auto"` without
overriding callers who named `"cute-dsl"`.

One accepted consequence: an explicit `backend=None` now resolves here rather than raising,
while `flashinfer.recurrent_kda` still rejects it. Python cannot distinguish `f()` from
`f(backend=None)`, so this follows from the sentinel rather than being a choice, and it lasts
only until the two defaults converge. Removing the divergence means widening the top-level
facade to accept `None` as "not specified" — a public-API change this PR does not otherwise
need, so it is deliberately left out.

**The trace fixture's diff is larger than this change.** The checked-in
`recurrent_kda_q8_v16_d128.json` predated the template's checkpoint and frozen-verify fields.
Regenerating through the *decode* facade on unmodified `main` produces the same additions, so
that drift is pre-existing rather than introduced here.

**The docs merge moves prose verbatim.** A word-level diff of the three original pages against
the merged page shows nothing dropped. The `apikda_decode` and `apikda_prefill` labels are kept
at their new sections so cross references still resolve.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/kda/` — **1184 passed, 154 skipped**, run after every commit.
- `pytest tests/trace/` — no new failures; the `*_reference_correctness` failures reproduce on
  a clean tree.
- All pre-commit hooks pass, including mypy.
- The consolidated docs page was built locally with Sphinx; that build is what caught a missing
  version argument on the `deprecated` directive.

title: feat: [PrimsTS] Add distribution-aware tuning and kernel selection to PrimsTS MoE
body:
# Add distribution-aware tuning to PrimsTS MoE

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

PrimsTS MoE now tunes against representative expert-load distributions and publishes a plan for
each operation shape. A DA plan maps normalized expert-load profiles to complete MoE tactics.
`ddist:x` is a deterministic Dirichlet-derived profile whose larger `x` values produce more
concentrated expert loads:

```text
ddist:1.1 --+
            |
ddist:1.3 --+--> body 0: (tile_n=8,  tactic=A)
            |
ddist:1.5 --+
ddist:1.7 ------> body 1: (tile_n=16, tactic=B)
ddist:2.0 --+
            |
ddist:2.5 --+--> body 2: (tile_n=32, tactic=C)
            |
ddist:4.0 --+
```

A multi-body plan pays both the inherent conditional-graph switch cost and the DA selector-kernel
cost. These overheads may outweigh tactic specialization, in which case the guard selects a
single body or falls back to the ordinary path.

The retained bodies determine capture behavior:

- `da_single_body` captures one fixed tactic without selector overhead.
- `da_switch` captures a device selector, routing preamble, and conditional body graphs.
- `da_fallback` captures the matched ordinary path when the guarded DA plan does not win.

Plans are immutable and shareable. Mutable routing metadata, selector state, and typed body
workspace are owned per concurrent CUDA Graph replay lane.

Eager calls use the `ddist:1.1` distribution winner for the same token bucket. Because the
kernel tactic heuristic (cosine similarity of distribution spectrum) and data all happen on
device, transferring back tactic to host or compute tactic on host is costly.

### Changes

- Extend DA tuning, caching, diagnostics, capture, replay, and teardown to PrimsTS MoE.
- Profile ordinary and DA tactics through complete `(inputs, kwargs)` invocations while preserving
  tensor aliases and stable native addresses.
- Filter nonlocal IDs before exemplar and runtime histogram sorting, including nonzero EP shard
  offsets and routing buffers that retain remote assignments.
- Extend the shared DA selector and fused routing preamble to 1024 global experts and top-k 32.
- Enable DA for PrimsTS by default while keeping TRTLLM DA opt-in. PrimsTS DA uses the empirical
  two-times balanced EP workload by default, while ordinary tuning ignores the DA workload policy.
- The `ValueProfileArena`, `prepare_tactic_profile()`, and former `profile_tactic()` contracts
  introduced in #4106 are removed and simplified by the complete-invocation profiling API.

### Usage

Leaving `FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE` unset enables DA for PrimsTS and disables it for TRTLLM.
Set it explicitly to override both backend defaults:

```bash
export FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0  # Disable DA.
export FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=1  # Enable DA.
```

No MoE call-site change is required. The matched baseline guard is enabled by default and can be
disabled explicitly:

```bash
export FLASHINFER_DA_BASELINE_GUARD=0
```

## Related Issues

<!-- Link any related issues here -->

- #4361

## Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Validation uses CUDA 13.2.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/autotuner
python -m pytest -q tests/moe
python -m pytest -q tests/prims_ts
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Repository-wide pre-commit passed. SM100 and SM103 validation covers ordinary and DA MoE,
1024 experts, top-k 32, packed and unpacked routing, and CUDA Graph replay. The balanced-workload
checks pass 17 tuner tests and both routed and FromLogits NVFP4 graph-lifecycle cases on B200.

## Performance

These measurements use cache-only CUDA Graph replay on an exclusive, non-oversubscribed 1000 W
B200; tuning and cache persistence are outside the timed interval. The DeepSeek-V3 EP8 shape has
256 global experts, 32 local experts, top-k 8, hidden size 7168, and intermediate size 2048. This
table predates the two-times default and used 1x balanced DA profiling. Replay is 1x balanced for
both graphs. Each cell is the minimum-maximum NoDA/DA speedup across `uniform` and five `ddist`
profiles; values above 1.0 favor DA.

Both graphs occupy both timing positions in ABBA order. A separate buffer larger than twice L2 is
zeroed before every replay, outside the timed interval. A separate cache-only process confirms the
same plan and capture topology selected during fresh tuning.

| Precision\Tokens | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 | 8192 | Overall |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | 1.0381x-1.1465x | 0.9942x-1.0027x | 0.9974x-1.0018x | 1.0014x-1.0095x | 0.9966x-1.0032x | 0.9969x-1.0017x | 0.9975x-1.0023x | 0.9978x-1.0003x | 0.9961x-1.0006x | 0.9975x-1.0026x | 0.9942x-1.1465x |

| BF16 | 0.9947x-1.0023x | 0.9982x-1.0027x | 0.9985x-1.0020x | 0.9977x-1.0012x | 0.9976x-1.0021x | 1.0006x-1.0032x | 0.9991x-1.0028x | 0.9971x-1.0019x | 0.9961x-1.0045x | 0.9952x-1.0014x | 0.9947x-1.0045x |
| FP8 per-tensor | 0.9914x-1.0185x | 0.9936x-1.0239x | 0.9975x-1.0047x | 0.9981x-1.0022x | 0.9994x-1.0079x | 0.9987x-1.0015x | 0.9935x-0.9974x | 1.0023x-1.0063x | 0.9984x-1.0062x | 0.9969x-1.0058x | 0.9914x-1.0239x |
| FP8 block | 1.0012x-1.0176x | 0.9991x-1.0070x | 0.9956x-1.0064x | 0.9975x-1.0036x | 0.9969x-1.0024x | 0.9952x-1.0019x | 0.9979x-1.0017x | 1.0457x-1.1287x | 0.9986x-1.0015x | 0.9987x-1.0013x | 0.9952x-1.1287x |
| MXFP8 | 0.9973x-1.0144x | 0.9984x-1.0021x | 1.0007x-1.0453x | 1.0000x-1.0028x | 0.9929x-1.0017x | 0.9991x-1.0043x | 0.9953x-1.0027x | 0.9968x-1.0034x | 0.9988x-1.0020x | 0.9960x-1.0001x | 0.9929x-1.0453x |

The guard admitted no `da_switch` plan in this matrix. Every token and precision domain resolved to
`da_single_body` or `da_fallback`.

`da_switch` is useful only when distribution-specific tactics save more time than the selector,
routing preamble, and conditional-graph switch cost. The guard currently budgets 12 us for that
cost. At the [B200 peak of 8 TB/s](https://docs.nvidia.com/enterprise-reference-architectures/hgx-ai-factory/latest/components.html), 12 us is a 96 MB bandwidth opportunity cost. For this
7168-by-2048 gated MoE shape, whose FC1 and FC2 contain `3 * H * I` parameters per expert, that is
about 1.1 BF16, 2.2 FP8, or 4.4 FP4 experts' raw weight payload. Scale metadata is excluded.

title: [SM120] Add W4A8 CuTeDSL MegaMoE backend

## Summary

This PR adds an SM120 CuTeDSL MegaMoE backend for:

- **Weights:** MXFP4 / E2M1
- **Activations:** MXFP8 / E4M3
- **Block scales:** E8M0 with K32 granularity
- **Accumulator:** FP32
- **Output:** BF16

The implementation extends the split MegaMoE backend introduced by #4387 and preserves its communication/computation overlap, ready-queue scheduling, CUDA Graph support, symmetric workspace management, and top-k reduction path.

## Dependency

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This PR depends on and is stacked on top of [#4387](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4387).
>
> It should not be merged before #4387. After #4387 is merged, this branch will be rebased onto the latest `main` so that the final diff contains only the incremental SM120 W4A8 changes.

## Implementation

The main W4A8 changes include:

- Use packed `Float4E2M1FN` weights and `Float8E4M3FN` activations.
- Use the SM120 mixed block-scaled QMMA path:
  - `E2M1 × E4M3`
  - `m16n8k32`
  - E8M0 block scales
- Add packed MXFP4 weight preprocessing and workspace sizing.
- Add the SM120 packed-E2M1 TMA/LDSM path.
- Keep FC1 output quantized as MXFP8 E4M3 with per-K32 E8M0 scales.
- Reuse the split K1/K2 Green Graph execution and independent K3 top-k reduction.
- Support CUDA Graph capture/replay and uneven token counts across ranks.
- Add a FlashInfer-facing W4A8 configuration and frontend independent of the benchmark runner.

The initial FlashInfer frontend supports single-rank and same-NUMA multi-rank `p2p_direct`. Cross-NUMA IBGDA frontend integration is left as follow-up work.

## Correctness

Validated on RTX Pro 5000 / SM120 with public CUTLASS DSL 4.6:

- Single-rank eager execution and repeated replay.
- Single-rank CUDA Graph capture and replay.
- Four-rank uneven tail-wave execution.
- Four-rank CUDA Graph capture and 16 repeated replays.
- Deterministic eager/replay outputs.
- Relative L2 error below `0.03` against the Torch reference.

body:
## What

Enables the fused gated MXFP8 quantization kernel — `silu_and_mul_mxfp8_quantize` and its backward (SwiGLU + MXFP8 rowwise/colwise quantization) — on SM107 (Rubin). One commit.

| gate | change |
|---|---|
| `flashinfer/gated_act_mxfp8.py` `(major, minor) not in ((10, 0), (10, 3))` | add `(10, 7)` |
| `csrc/gated_act_mxfp8/gated_act_mxfp8.cu` `TVM_FFI_ICHECK(major == 10 && (minor == 0 \|\| minor == 3))` | add `minor == 7` |
| `tests/utils/test_gated_act_mxfp8.py` `_supported()` | add `(10, 7)` |

The `_sm103`-specific backward variants stay selected by `minor == 3` only; SM107 takes the SM100-tuned generic backward kernels, which is functionally correct. Whether Rubin wants its own selection rule is a perf follow-up.

## Why it is safe

The kernels use TMA bulk copies, mbarriers (CTA and cluster scope) and packed `bf16x2`/`f32x2` math — nothing Blackwell-exclusive, no tcgen05/TMEM, no `__CUDA_ARCH__` branches. The JIT module (`flashinfer/jit/gated_act_mxfp8.py`) compiles with `supported_major_versions=[10]` and `map_sm107_to_100f=False`, i.e. it **already emits native `sm_107a` code** on a Rubin build; only the three checks above kept the op from being called.

## Validation

GR100 (cc 10.7, driver 620.05), image `flashinfer-ci:cu134-nightly-py3.67144516-whl-amd64` with the CI job's `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0.dev0` override, against an `upstream/main` baseline on the same tree/image:

## 📌 Description

@humansand

Add `Sm100_Bf16_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig` through the existing `MegaConfig` / `MoEEpLayer` API. One persistent kernel stages BF16 inputs, dispatches tokens, executes FC1/SwiGLU and FC2, returns route outputs, and performs deterministic FP32 combine.

- **Weight contract:** canonical gate-then-up packed E2M1 weights and E4M3 scales; prepared `(weight, scale)` pairs match NVFP4 W4A4's gate16/up16 and blocked-scale layout. Existing `fc1_alpha`/`fc2_alpha` config or runtime fields provide FP32 per-expert scales after GEMM accumulation. Weights decode directly into TMEM for BF16 MMA; decoded weights never materialize in global/shared memory.
- **Pipeline:** five warp groups, including two dequantization groups, retain the 61,440-register CTA pool and one CTA per SM; existing CuTe MegaMoE backends use three or four groups. Alternate receive-counter banks allow clearing the previous generation during GEMM work. Existing readiness fences, accumulator ownership, and outgoing-copy completion waits remain.
- **Fusion:** input staging and deterministic FP32 top-k combine execute inside MegaMoE, replacing the separate staging operations and reduction launches used by existing deterministic paths. One dispatch group stages inputs through the existing publication protocol. Four retired compute groups, including both dequantization groups, perform ordered combine after the cross-rank drain; mapping/score preparation overlaps the producer tail.
- **Numerics:** default FC2 route values round to BF16, then ordered FP32 routing multiplication/FMA produces one final BF16 output. `apply_topk_in_fc1=True` instead multiplies the FP32 SwiGLU result before its BF16 handoff, then combines using ordered FP32 additions. The modes have separate rounding contracts and cache identities; the default remains false. Neither deterministic mode uses atomic/TMA reduction. Existing opt-in `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` allows the distinct BF16 atomic reduction path.
- **Interface/lifetime:** preserve BF16 activations, int32/int64 routing IDs, FP32 scores, empty/uneven ranks, strided views, and graph replay. Public forward always stages inside MegaMoE. Collective warmup prepares all four ID/layout signatures before capture; source tensors stay owned through tuning and launch. Runtime expert scales retain their stable workspace buffers. Inputs cannot alias private staging storage.
- **Autotune:** eight deterministic M256/C2/K256 tactics: `group_hint=512/1024` × N128/N64 × epilogue/dispatch return, communication flag batch 4, epilogue flag batches (2, 4), and scheduler depth 2. Explicit IKR permission adds four dispatch-return reduction tactics, for twelve candidates total. Grouping uses the existing compile-time scheduler. Existing knob-cache entries remain valid; explicit AUTO retuning discovers the new candidates. Routing-weight placement is session configuration, not a tuning dimension. Candidate timing includes fused staging and combine. Preserve manual geometries/stage counts and collective EP-group tuning; failures abort the sweep.

The vendored `kernel_src/**/src` drop and other MegaMoE kernels remain unchanged. SM100/SM103, SwiGLU, EP, H divisible by 32, I divisible by 64, and top-k at most min(32, total experts).

Focused EP1/EP2 deterministic checks require finite BF16 bit equality with zero tolerance; IKR uses a separate rounding-band contract.

**Environment/source:** `7100e0d16dd306e6fd2a8d734bdb03981d477901`; B300 SXM6 AC (SM103), 4 GPUs for EP4 and 8 for EP8; `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3`, driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13.2, Torch `2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.5.50603568`, CuTe DSL 4.7.1/cu13, NVSHMEM 3.6.5, CUPTI Python 13.2.0/library 13.2.86. MegaMoE uses O3 and ordinary staging preparation. Each EP comparison uses one host/boot; EP4 and EP8 use separate nodes.

**Workload:** H7168/I2048/E256/top-k8, global tokens 1–512 plus 4096/8192/16384. BF16 activations, NVFP4 weights, FP32 routing scores, default FC2 routing placement, deterministic finalize (`--no-fused-finalize`). MegaMoE uses its eight-tactic AUTO catalog; Split uses its native autotuner.

**Timing:** cold-L2 CUDA graph replay with CUPTI, three warmups and 100 samples per sweep. Each sample is the maximum across ranks of the span from first to last GPU activity, including gaps and overlap. Two final-source Split/Mega sweeps provide 200 samples per row; report their pooled median without trimming. cat > "$benchmark_dir/run_deferred.py" <<'BENCH_PY'
```bash
"""Experiment-only CUPTI session lifetime; native measurement code is unchanged."""
from cupti import cupti


class DeferredFinalize:
    def __init__(self):
        self.callbacks = []
        self.finalize_calls = 0
        self.original_register = cupti.activity_register_callbacks
        self.original_finalize = cupti.finalize
        cupti.activity_register_callbacks = self.register
        cupti.finalize = self.defer

    def register(self, *callbacks):
        self.callbacks.append(callbacks)
        return self.original_register(*callbacks)

    def defer(self):
        self.finalize_calls += 1

    def finish(self):
        # Every native measurement has already synchronized, flushed activity
        # buffers and disabled all five activity kinds. Keep callback ownership
        # through the single detach after the workload and process group drain.
        self.original_finalize()
        cupti.activity_register_callbacks = self.original_register
        cupti.finalize = self.original_finalize
        return dict(deferred_finalizes=self.finalize_calls, registrations=len(self.callbacks))


import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd() / "benchmarks"))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "frozen_benchmark", Path.cwd() / "benchmarks/bench_cute_dsl_moe_distributed.py"
)
native = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[spec.name] = native
spec.loader.exec_module(native)
lifecycle = DeferredFinalize()
result = native.main()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
lifecycle.finish()
raise SystemExit(result)
BENCH_PY
for ep in 4 8; do
  export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$(seq -s, 0 "$((ep - 1))")
  for repeat in 1 2; do
    sweep_dir="$benchmark_dir/ep${ep}-${repeat}"
    mkdir -p "$sweep_dir"
    export FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE="$sweep_dir/knobs.json"
    python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node="$ep" \
      --master-addr=127.0.0.1 --master-port=30317 \
      "$benchmark_dir/run_deferred.py" --num-gpus "$ep" \
      --parallel-modes ep --variants w4a16,w4a16_megamoe \
      --num-tokens 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,4096,8192,16384 \
      --warmup 3 --iters 100 --timing cupti --cuda-graph \
      --precomputed-routing --no-fused-finalize --megamoe-knobs auto \
      --log-timing-samples | tee "$sweep_dir/benchmark.log"
  done
done
```

The wrapper retains callback ownership and detaches CUPTI once after all measurements; native timed callables, graph capture, sampling and rank aggregation remain unchanged. After each timed graph helper returns, the observer makes two untimed eager calls and checks finite, bit-exact repeat outputs; old/new MegaMoE hashes are compared separately. It does not check every timed graph replay output. Native graph tests are covered above. Frozen helper `f156f69cfa49` SHA-256 identifiers:

```text
bench_cute_dsl_moe_distributed.py: 7e2beb4a2e1a57364e4e54de4dcd028e9d2eacb99f3feed5a2ca886861b41d7d
worker.py: 70ef12cf9edaace79f219e5da9a594ca7311113aab5c6c2c1f1a7538940a8706
cupti_lifecycle.py: 6d11d36d6e8a4fde1d88d55f900067fcc18c9a39b747c0283ef6757e292ae3a7
```

Each sweep uses a fresh knob cache. Only support-library build artifacts are reused; no persistent CuTe device-compilation cache is claimed. Pool the 100 raw rank-MAX samples from each final sweep and take their median. Split and MegaMoE have different reduction-rounding contracts; their outputs are not a numerical acceptance comparison.

title: fix(prefill): packed LSE and default sm_scale for the paged cuDNN backend
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn").run()` has two bugs at the same call site, and fixing the first exposes a known cuDNN kernel bug that needs a guard.

**1. `return_lse=True` raises (#5258).** The wrapper allocates the packed `[num_tokens, num_qo_heads]` LSE that every other backend writes, but the paged cuDNN call passes no stats ragged offset, so the low level only accepts the padded `(num_sequences, max_token_per_sequence, h_qo)` layout and raises `ValueError`. Fix: pass the token-unit `qo_indptr` as `batch_offsets_stats` when `return_lse=True`, which is what the ragged wrapper already does, so cuDNN writes the packed layout directly.

**2. Silently wrong output when `plan()` gets no `sm_scale` (not previously reported).** `run()` computes a defaulted local `sm_scale = 1/sqrt(head_dim)`, but the paged cuDNN call passed `self._sm_scale`, which is `None` in that case, so cuDNN applied no softmax scaling. This does not depend on `return_lse`. The ragged wrapper passes the local value and was fine. `tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill.py` always passes `sm_scale` explicitly, so nothing caught it.

Paged cuDNN vs fa2 on H200 (bf16, 8/2 heads, head_dim 128, page_size 16, q_lens `[17, 1, 64, 33]`, kv_lens `[40, 90, 64, 70]`, causal):

| case | out max abs diff | LSE max abs diff |
|---|---|---|
| `sm_scale=None`, before | 3.48 | `ValueError` |
| `sm_scale=1/sqrt(128)` explicit, before | 0.016 | `ValueError` |
| `sm_scale=None`, after | 0.016 | 0.0017 |
| `sm_scale=None`, MHA 8/8, after | 0.016 | 0.0021 |

**3. Guard for the single-token GQA LSE bug (NVBug 6783545).** With the packed LSE enabled, the paged kernel shows the same bug the ragged wrapper already guards against: when every q_len is 1 and `num_qo_heads != num_kv_heads`, the LSE is only correct for the first head of each kv group. Per-head LSE max abs diff vs fa2 with 8/2 heads: `[0.001, 7.5, 6.9, 7.2, 0.0, 7.4, 7.1, 7.2]`; the output itself is correct, and MHA is fine. I observed this on cuDNN 9.24, so it is not limited to 9.26/9.27. This PR mirrors the ragged guard: that combination raises `NotImplementedError` instead of returning a wrong LSE. Before this PR it raised `ValueError`, so no working call is lost.

All code changes are inside the `backend == "cudnn"` branch of the paged `run()`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #5258

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Test changes:
- `tests/attention/test_lse_base.py`: removed the strict xfail on `test_paged_lse_base[cudnn]`. The test also handed cuDNN an NHD-shaped cache, while the paged cuDNN path reads `shape[1]` as the kv head count (the `[pages, H_kv, page_size, D]` view that `test_cudnn_prefill.py` builds). The xfail had been hiding that, so the cuDNN case now passes the transposed view.
- `tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill.py`: added `test_cudnn_paged_prefill_return_lse` (output and packed LSE vs fa2; GQA 8/2 and MHA 8/8; causal and non-causal; no explicit `sm_scale`, so it covers bug 2 as well) and `test_cudnn_paged_prefill_single_token_gqa_lse_rejected` (the guard; the same call without LSE still works). These are not gated on SM100, so they also run on SM80/SM90 CI.

Results on H200 (SM90, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.14, cuDNN 9.24, cudnn-frontend 1.29):
- The 5 new tests fail on `main` (5/5) and pass with this PR (5/5).
- `test_lse_base.py`, `test_cudnn_prefill.py`, `test_cudnn_prefill_large_page.py`, `test_cudnn_prefill_token_indptr.py`: **443 passed, 578 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `test_paged_lse_base[cudnn]` is gated on SM100, so CI on H200 skips it. I ran it on H200 with the gate relaxed locally: all paged cases pass, including `lse_base` log2/ln and `lse_layout="HN"`. It has not been run on SM100.

## Reviewer Notes

- I could not test on cuDNN 9.26/9.27 or on Blackwell. The guard in item 3 is based on cuDNN 9.24 behavior plus the existing ragged guard. If the paged kernel is fixed in a later cuDNN release, the guard can become version-conditional.
- The cuDNN paged wrapper takes `kv_layout="NHD"` but expects `[pages, H_kv, page_size, D]`-shaped views over token-major memory. That convention is unchanged here; it is what tripped the `test_lse_base` case and might deserve a docstring note or a shape check in a follow-up.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved cuDNN paged prefill support for returning log-sum-exp (LSE) values in packed token-and-head format.
  * Calls that omit the softmax scale now use the correct default automatically.
  * Added clearer handling for unsupported single-token grouped-query attention requests when LSE output is enabled; these requests now report an explicit limitation instead of producing incorrect results.
  * LSE-enabled results now align with the alternative attention backend, while calls without LSE continue to behave consistently.

title: feat(cake_kda): deterministic chunked KDA training backward (SM100a/SM103a)
body:
## Deterministic chunked KDA training backward (SM100a / SM103a)

Adds a bit-deterministic backward pass for the chunked KDA training algorithm (`chunk_kda` with in-kernel Q/K L2 normalization, the lower-bound safe gate, sigmoid beta and `dt_bias`; chunk 64, K = V = 128), generated by the Cake compiler and exported as ten device/binding source pairs per architecture.

### What is included
- `csrc/kda/chunk_train/{sm_100a,sm_103a}/` — generated device sources and TVM-FFI bindings for the ten backward stages: gate prefix scan + WY inputs, WY recompute, forward state recurrence, dAv, adjoint state recurrence, fused dq/dk/dg, intra-chunk backward, gate epilogue, q/k-norm epilogue, and the fixed-order `dA_log` / `d(dt_bias)` finalize. Bindings encode TMA descriptors on the host on every call into a caller-owned device workspace, so tensor addresses may change between calls.
- `flashinfer/jit/cake_kda_chunk_train.py` — mechanically filled module registry (argument plans, launch geometry, sources) and a `NativeKernel` wrapper that maps named bindings onto the exported argument plan.
- `flashinfer/kda_chunk_train.py` — `chunk_kda_backward(...)`: consumes the chunked forward's saved set (normalized q/k with inverse norms, sigmoid(beta), per-chunk `Aqk`/`Akk`) and returns `dq`, `dk`, `dv`, `dbeta`, `dg`, `dA_log`, `d(dt_bias)`. `dbeta` is returned with respect to the raw beta when `beta_logits` is passed, or with respect to the already-sigmoided beta when it is omitted (the form the Kimi K3 layer in radixark/miles produces). Fixed layouts with `T % 128 == 0` and packed layouts of one shared 128-multiple length; grouped value heads (HV a multiple of H).
- `tests/kda/test_chunk_kda_backward.py` — elementwise parity (atol = rtol = 1e-2) against flash-linear-attention v0.5.2 `chunk_kda` on fixed, grouped-head and packed shapes, plus bit-determinism of repeated backward calls. Skips when the reference package is not installed.

### Numerics and determinism
The kernels reproduce the reference chunked dataflow stage by stage with fp32 inter-chunk state carriers and bf16 hand-offs at the reference's rounding points; all reductions are fixed-order (no atomics). On the kimi-k3 production rows (B in {1, 4}, T in {2048, 4096, 8192}, H = 16, HV in {16, 32}, packed 4 x 2048) every gradient and the output pass the elementwise gate against the reference and repeated backward passes are bit-identical.

### Performance (backward only, CUPTI, cold L2, vs flash-linear-attention v0.5.2 Triton backward)
| row | B200 | GB300 |
|---|---|---|
| b1 t2048 h16 | 2.55x | 1.90x |
| b1 t4096 h16 | 1.48x | 1.63x |
| b1 t8192 h16 | 1.29x | 1.29x |
| b4 t2048 h16 | 1.40x | 1.33x |
| b1 t4096 h16 hv32 | 1.39x | 1.40x |
| packed 4x2048 h16 | 1.37x | 1.35x |

At T = 2048 the reference's 18 Triton launches are host-bound while the ten launches here enqueue in about 0.4 ms; at T = 8192 both sides are GPU-bound and the margin is kernel time (1.28 vs 1.56 ms on B200). compute-sanitizer synccheck and memcheck report 0 errors on the full backward.

### Validation of this branch
Built from source on B200 (SM100a) inside an NGC container and run against flash-linear-attention v0.5.2:

- `tests/kda/test_chunk_kda_backward.py`: **11 passed** (elementwise parity of all seven gradients on b1 t256, b1 t512 grouped-heads, b2 t384, packed 2x256 and b1 t2048 h16; the post-sigmoid `dbeta` mode; bit-determinism of repeated backward calls; shape validation).
- `benchmarks/bench_chunk_kda_backward.py` (`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`, CUPTI, cold L2; the reference arm is the v0.5.2 Triton backward through `torch.autograd.grad` on a retained graph):

| row | reference ms | this PR ms | speedup | parity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b1_t2048_h16 | 1.372 | 0.380 | 3.61x | pass |
| b1_t4096_h16 | 1.383 | 0.685 | 2.02x | pass |
| b1_t8192_h16 | 1.573 | 1.307 | 1.20x | pass |
| b4_t2048_h16 | 1.283 | 0.994 | 1.29x | pass |
| b1_t4096_h16_hv32 | 1.338 | 1.046 | 1.28x | pass |
| packed_4x2048_h16 | 1.199 | 1.062 | 1.13x | pass |

- Inputs follow the model-init regime (`A_log = log(U(0,1) + 1)`, i.e. decay rates in [1, 2)). `d(dt_bias)` is returned with the reference's bf16-sum rounding; far outside that regime (e.g. `A_log ~ N(0, 1)`) single elements can differ from the reference by one bf16 ulp at |x| > 2, which the elementwise 1e-2 check reports as a mismatch while the error RMS ratio stays at 0.004.
- SM103a sources are generated from the same builds; the compiler-side contract run on GB300 passes the same gate on all six production rows (table above). The generated SM103a modules were not rebuilt through this repository's JIT path in this validation.

### Scope note
This is the training-side sibling of the Cake KDA inference kernels already in `csrc/kda`. Training-side KDA kernels have recently been routed through the cuDNN Frontend `kda_cake` engine rather than FlashInfer; this PR is opened as a draft so the maintainers can decide whether the chunked training backward should live here or be exported to that engine instead. The forward pass is not included: the API consumes the forward's saved set.

Downstream consumer: radixark/miles#3582 adds `--kda-backend flashinfer` to the Kimi K3 trainer (FLA forward, this backward, per-call fallback to FLA outside the kernel domain) and was validated against this branch.

title: feat(prims-ts): support QK-BF16/PV-FP8 in FMHA decode
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds QK-BF16/PV-FP8 support to the prims-ts decode kernel. V can be kept in `float8_e4m3` while Q and K stay `bfloat16`. This is the decode counterpart to [#4879](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4879) and stacks on top.

Most of the change is removing the assumption that Q, K, V share one dtype. `qkv_dtype`/`kv_dtype` are split into per-operand `q_dtype`/`k_dtype`/`v_dtype` and threaded through the public API, TMA descriptors, SMEM tile sizing, and MMA-kind and P-quantization selection. Note that most of the old `use_fp8_qkv`  gates were asking whether a given operand is one byte wide, so they now ask that per operand. For all-BF16 and all-FP8 configs, every one of those predicates evaluates as before (see reviewer notes for correctness and perf verification).

Mixed K/V dtypes take the split-resource path with one K ring and one V ring shared by both instances, i.e. K and V are each staged once. To allow this, `SmemKvTileResource` takes the instance from the calling `load_k0`/`load_k1`. Note that this does not affect existing modes.

Changes public API for .plan() to support the new mixed QK-BF16/PV-FP8 types for KV. See below for changes.

Stacks on [#4879](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4879) (context-side QK-BF16/PV-FP8), which is merged.

**No performance regression for QKV-BF16 decode.**
[qkvbf16-decode-b200.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32128842/qkvbf16-decode-b200.md)

**Average of 3-32% performance gain with QK-BF16/PV-FP8 quantization over QKV-BF16 baseline, positive across all 86 configs measured.**

title: fix(prefill): support host-side `qo_indptr` in cutlass ragged plan
body:
## 📌 Description

`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.plan()` accepts host (CPU) `qo_indptr`/`kv_indptr` for every backend except cutlass (SM100/SM110), which derived the FMHA module-selection device from `qo_indptr.device` (raising `ValueError: device must be a cuda device` for CPU tensors) and passed the raw indptr tensors to `fmha_varlen_plan`, which requires CUDA tensors.

Use `self.device` for module selection and the already-materialized device-side buffers `self._qo_indptr_buf`/`self._kv_indptr_buf` for `fmha_varlen_plan`, so callers holding host-side offsets (e.g. vLLM) can plan without a synchronizing D2H copy.

For callers that already pass CUDA indptr tensors on the workspace device this is a no-op: `.to(self.device)` returns the same tensor object, so `fmha_varlen_plan` receives the identical tensor as before.

Downstream motivation: vLLM threads host-side query offsets through its MLA prefill metadata to avoid a GPU→CPU sync (vllm-project/vllm#52657); this fix unblocks that path on B200/GB200.

title: fix(prefill): avoid device sync for cutlass ragged _max_qo_len
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.plan()` on the `cutlass` (SM100/SM110) ragged prefill backend computes `_max_qo_len` via `torch.max(...).item()` on the device-side `_qo_indptr_buf`, forcing a GPU→CPU sync on every `plan()` call.

`plan()` already derives the identical value sync-free from the `qo_indptr` host mirror (`max_qo_len`, computed for the fmha_v2 path a few lines earlier), and `_qo_indptr_buf` is a pure device copy of the same data, so the two are always equal. This change reuses the host-side value.

This completes the no-sync story for callers passing host-side indptrs (e.g. vLLM): with this change, every value the cutlass plan/run path consumes is either a host scalar or an async H2D copy — the removed `.item()` was the last GPU→CPU sync on the path.

No benchmark numbers attached: the win is one eliminated blocking sync per `plan()` call, and I don't have SM100/SM110 hardware available locally to measure it.

Multi-token decode, ragged prefill, split-KV, and eager planning retain their existing scheduling.

The single-token restriction is intentional: an initial broader uniform-query variant showed a small multi-token latency regression on H100. This version leaves that path unchanged. Public APIs and the plan/FFI layout are unchanged.

The review follow-up also makes `workspace_size()` reject non-positive `q_len_per_req`, matching `plan()` and `fast_decode_plan()` before native sizing.

The subsequent validation-only commit leaves the kernel and valid-input sizing logic unchanged; these timings were not rerun on that commit.

| 1 | FP16 | 2 | cold | 6.259 → 6.139 | 6.259 → 6.146 |

| 3 | BF16 | 129 | hot | 8.514 → 8.514 | 8.515 → 8.515 |

Tiny-KV latency improves about 3.7% hot / 1.8–1.9% cold; long-KV hot results are essentially flat to sub-1%, and cold results improve about 1.4–1.6%. These are kernel microbenchmarks for callers already using `disable_split_kv=True`, not end-to-end serving gains or a reason to disable split-KV generally. Other GPUs remain unmeasured.

A second shape (BF16, Q=1, KV=128, 32 query heads / 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, page size 16, regular planner) showed larger gains. I repeated each pair twice more, reversing execution order. | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| 16 | cold | 10.712–10.726 | 8.788–8.790 | 17.9–18.1% |

For these shapes, grid-x changes from 33 to 1 or 16. Gains are shape-dependent; the nearly-flat cases in the first table are just as relevant.

```bash
python benchmarks/bench_fa2_no_split_cuda_graph.py --dtype bfloat16 --kv-len 2
```
