title: perf(quantization): parallelize long segment packing
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`segment_packbits` assigns one CUDA block to each segment, so a long mask in a small batch is processed serially by very few blocks. Both paged and ragged prefill `plan(custom_mask=...)` use this path. For example, packing a single 4096 × 4096 boolean mask takes about 1.36 ms on RTX 4090 before attention planning can continue.

Split each segment into independent, byte-aligned tiles across a bounded number of CTAs, using the input size already known by the host. The original single-CTA specialization is retained for short segments and large batches. This adds no scratch buffer or device-to-host metadata read, preserves per-segment tail padding, and keeps existing C++ calls valid through a defaulted size hint.

**Measured complete ragged-prefill `plan(custom_mask=...)` latency:**

| GPU | batch × Q × KV | main (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX 4090 | 1 × 128 × 32768 | 414.55 | 132.42 | 3.13× |
| RTX 4090 | 1 × 4096 × 4096 | 1380.91 | 141.26 | 9.78× |
| RTX 4090 | 16 × 128 × 8192 | 173.87 | 139.29 | 1.25× |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 1 × 128 × 32768 | 658.04 | 126.81 | 5.19× |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 1 × 4096 × 4096 | 2411.11 | 136.27 | 17.69× |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 16 × 128 × 8192 | 248.00 | 131.04 | 1.89× |

FP16 Q/KV, 8 query heads / 2 KV heads, head dimension 128, FA2. These are mask-preparation/plan-call improvements, incurred whenever a caller replans with an unpacked mask; they are not model-throughput measurements.

**Packing kernel, one segment, big bit order:**

| GPU | 16 MiB input, warm (µs) | rotating inputs > L2 (µs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| RTX 4090 | 1360.28 → 7.88 | 2443.68 → 19.84 |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 2217.60 → 17.46 | 5017.55 → 26.40 |

Measured against main `975f90583d9ac8896db14cf0f26e99a853c2f136`, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8. Separate JIT caches, A/B/A runs, shuffled case order (seed 42); table baseline is the mean of the two baseline medians. Kernel timings use CUDA events around graph replay; API/plan timings use synchronized wall time with fixed CPU affinity. The matrix covers both bit orders, batch sizes 1–1024, 17–16,777,216 elements per segment, and warm/rotating-input conditions. Additional interleaved same-process comparisons confirm the retained single-CTA cases have matching kernel timings.

Reproduce on each revision with the benchmark script from this PR:

```bash
FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE=/tmp/packbits-main python benchmarks/bench_segment_packbits.py --include-plan
FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE=/tmp/packbits-main python benchmarks/bench_segment_packbits.py --cold-l2
# Repeat on the PR revision with a separate /tmp/packbits-pr cache, then main again.
```

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related to the custom-mask preprocessing discussion in #724.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).


Validation on both RTX 4090 (SM89) and A100 80GB PCIe (SM80):

- `pytest tests/utils/test_quantization.py -q`: **142 passed per GPU**. New cases use an independent NumPy oracle and cover byte/tile boundaries, long and uneven segments, empty segments/batches, input offsets, both bit orders, int32/int64 indptr, output guards and allocation-free kernel graph capture. The baseline passes the 126 cases applicable to its nonempty-batch launcher.
- **70 existing custom-mask attention combinations per GPU**, comparing with causal attention: paged/ragged, MHA/GQA, ROPE/ALIBI, soft cap, page sizes 1/16, short/long context.
- Python suite under Compute Sanitizer **synccheck/racecheck: zero errors/hazards** on both GPUs.
- Standalone C++ header harness: **160 independent CPU-reference cases per GPU**, including original/defaulted C++ calls and int32/int64 pointers; **memcheck/racecheck/synccheck all report zero errors/hazards**.
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files` and `git diff --check` pass.

Python memcheck also executes all tests successfully, but exits nonzero for one `cuKernelGetFunction` / `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` API report on both baseline and patch. The standalone CUDA checks above avoid that runtime path and pass memcheck; the Python invocation is not counted as a clean memcheck result.

title: test(sampling): add seeded correctness fuzz coverage
body:
## 📌 Description

Stream 1a of #3605: a seeded fuzzer for the existing probability-sampling entry points, following the MoE / GEMM fuzzers (`FuzzLedger`, env-var case count and seed, single-seed repro on failure). Test-only; no kernel or API changes.

Covered: `sampling_from_probs`, `top_k_sampling_from_probs`, `top_p_sampling_from_probs`, `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs` (`joint` and `top_k_first`), with scalar and per-request thresholds, `indices` (including `len(indices) != probs.size(0)`), and `seed`/`offset`/`generator` replay. `min_p`, chain speculative sampling and the logits entry points are left for a follow-up.

Oracle: a float64 PyTorch reference written from the documented semantics. It does not call FlashInfer or mirror the rejection loop. Each row gets two masks rather than one answer:

- may-draw: classes a correct kernel may return. For top-k this is everything at least as likely as the k-th largest, compared exactly on the float32 values passed in (top-k is a rank test, so no tolerance). For top-p the cumulative-mass threshold is loosened by `vocab * 2^-24`, since the kernel accumulates in float32.
- must-draw: classes every implementation allowed by the docs has to keep. "Keep the top-k probabilities" is read the way `test_sampling.py` reads it (at least k classes, at most everything tied with the k-th), so a tie at the pivot is only required when there is no freedom in choosing among the tied classes. For `top_k_first` the bounds also account for which tied classes the top-k stage kept, because that changes the renormalized row the top-p stage sees.

A draw outside may-draw fails. A must-draw class whose expected count, computed from a lower bound on its probability, is at least 64 has to show up (miss probability at most e^-64 per class). The first version of this PR loosened the top-k pivot with the top-p tolerance, which dropped the k-th class from the must-draw side, so a kernel keeping only k-1 classes would have passed; there is now a CPU test for exactly that.

Cases: each seed fixes API, vocab (1–257), 1–4 distributions drawn from sparse / one-hot / bimodal / long-tail / near-uniform / strictly-decreasing / plateau shapes, k ∈ {1, 2, vocab−1, vocab}, and top-p either from a fixed grid or placed just below / at / just above one of the row's cumulative masses. ~4096 draws per case.

Distribution check: 12 frozen configs (including the no-op thresholds `top_k = vocab`, `top_p = 1`), 32768 draws each, Pearson χ² with low-expectation bins merged. Targets are built from the float32 probabilities actually handed to the kernel. A config fails only if `p < 1e-5 / 12` and the effect is large (TVD > 0.02 or max standardized residual > 6). The 1e-5 is a nominal budget (asymptotic χ², Bonferroni split), not a finite-sample guarantee. Thresholds were fixed before looking at FlashInfer output. As an observation: 0 / 4800 gate firings on `torch.multinomial` and 0 / 2400 on FlashInfer; an injected bias of TVD 0.01 is caught 200 / 200 times, TVD 0.005 62 / 200.

Known issue tracked through the ledger: per-request `top_k` combined with `indices` uses the wrong row's `k` (#5339, fix in #5340). Those cases are generated and run with one output per probs row, so the wrong read stays inside the threshold tensor on an unfixed build, and they are recorded in `FuzzLedger` as a tolerated wrong answer. `test_per_request_top_k_follows_indices` is the probe for it. On current `main` that gives 6 xfails. Once #5340 is in, the probe passes and the ledger's xpass rule fails on purpose; the only change needed then is deleting the `Finding` entry (271 passed with it removed on the fixed kernel). Whichever of the two PRs lands second, I'll do that in the same PR.

The reference, generator and statistics tests (18 of them) run without CUDA; only the tests that call FlashInfer are skipped on a CPU-only machine.

Cost: 271 tests, 1.85 s warm on one RTX 4090 D (first run JIT-compiles the sampling module). Registered next to `test_sampling.py` in `scripts/task_jit_run_tests_part3.sh`.

```
FLASHINFER_SAMPLING_FUZZ_NUM_CASES   number of seeded cases (default 240)
FLASHINFER_SAMPLING_FUZZ_SEED        base seed (default 0)
FLASHINFER_SAMPLING_FUZZ_ONLY_SEED   comma-separated seeds to replay
```

title: perf(sampling): defer last-valid-index reduction until fallback
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Probability sampling currently performs an integer block-max reduction for the last valid token on every scanned vocabulary tile, although that index is only consumed if the CDF scan fails to select a token. Retain each thread's candidate across tiles and reduce it only when the scan ends without a selection. This removes the fallback collective from the normal path while preserving the probability accumulation, CDF, RNG progression, predicates, and final shared-storage barrier. Each rejection round starts with a fresh candidate; the speculative residual scan does the same.

The included benchmark measures the sampler alone and Torch softmax followed by sampling (FP32 Gaussian logits, std=1, seed=42, top-k=50). Results below use the revised benchmark: an independent Python RNG shuffles all 10 sampler/softmax combinations per shape with `--order-seed 42`, and every row records its execution index. Each A/B/A run uses the same permutation, matching inputs within each mode, and separate JIT caches. These are same-GPU CUDA-graph medians; “before” is the mean of the two baseline medians. Five warmups and 30 timed replays; compilation and input creation are excluded.

| GPU | B | V | top-k + Torch softmax, before | after | latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX 4090 | 1 | 151936 | 311.65 us | 287.54 us | 7.7% |
| RTX 4090 | 16 | 151936 | 370.33 us | 342.94 us | 7.4% |
| RTX 4090 | 128 | 151936 | 619.65 us | 589.52 us | 4.9% |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 1 | 151936 | 537.34 us | 474.11 us | 11.8% |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 16 | 151936 | 553.83 us | 486.71 us | 12.1% |
| A100 80GB PCIe | 128 | 151936 | 1023.59 us | 902.40 us | 11.8% |

These are sampling-stage latencies. The affected probability APIs can run at each non-greedy decoding step; gains depend on the sampler and shape. Model-forward and serving-throughput measurements are outside this benchmark.

Reproduce with the same benchmark file on both revisions, each installed from source with its pinned submodules and its own `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`:

```bash
python benchmarks/bench_sampling_fallback.py --vocab-sizes 111 4096 151936
python benchmarks/bench_sampling_fallback.py --cold-l2
python benchmarks/bench_sampling_fallback.py --vocab-sizes 111 4096 151936 --non-deterministic
```

Cold-L2 runs rotate enough input buffers to exceed the device's cache and visit every buffer before replay. For the six top-k + softmax rows at V=151936, cold-L2 latency reductions ranged from 3.7% to 12.4%. title: feat(attention): FA2 per-(token, head) FP8 KV scale
body:
Add a per-(token, head) FP8 K/V cache scale to the FA2 attention kernels. The scale is a separate float32 tensor mirroring the KV layout minus head_dim, following the NVFP4 block-scale design:

- kernel: one float32 scale per (KV row, head), staged into smem and applied in compute_qk (K scale on the S accumulator) and compute_sfm_v (V scale on the P fragment). Single/ragged derive the scale strides in-kernel from the KV strides (scale stride = KV stride / head_dim, as the NVFP4 path derives its SF strides); the paged path takes host-computed strides (GetFP8ScaleStrides) because its scale may be a non-contiguous view of an inline slot (last dim head_dim + 16).
- API: the scale is passed via the existing kv_cache_sf parameter (no signature change). single_prefill_with_kv_cache derives the feature from is_float8(kv) and kv_cache_sf is not None (mirroring the NVFP4 derivation); the ragged/paged prefill and paged decode wrappers take an explicit use_token_head_sf at plan time. The fa2 backend is required.
- decode: no CUDA-core kernel; the tensor-core (fa2 prefill) path is forced, reusing the prefill kernel.
- smem: the scale buffer (one float per KV row, K and V) is added to the shared-memory budget; on tight-smem configs (e.g. SM75 head_dim 256) the KV repack staging is disabled to make room.
- tests/bench: end-to-end coverage for single/ragged/paged prefill and paged decode, HND/NHD layouts, inline-slot views, the mirror-stride contract, and the negative validation paths.

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

vLLM implements a fine-grained, dynamic, inference-time FP8 KV cache quantization method known as `fp8_per_token_head`.
Compared to per-tensor FP8 quantization, it offers several advantages:
1. It eliminates the need for pre-calibration of per-tensor scales.
2. It employs a finer quantization granularity with dynamic scaling, resulting in superior quantization precision.
3. It calculates scales dynamically for each head, entailing lower computational overhead during quantization.

However, the current implementation relies on Triton and suffers from poor performance; a specially optimized native CUDA implementation is required.

title: feat(comm): add a PCIe/RDMA Ulysses all-to-all backend
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds `UlyssesCommunicator(backend="pcie")`: an experimental single-node all-to-all transport for PCIe-connected GPU groups without NVLink (e.g. 8x RTX PRO 5000), targeting Ulysses sequence parallelism in video/image diffusion serving. Being experimental, it is reachable from `backend="auto"` only where NVLink is unavailable and `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1` is set identically on every rank; naming it explicitly never needs that variable. Either way it warns once.

**Why.** The existing NVLink backend lets SM threads store into peer-visible staging buffers; across a PCIe host bridge that degenerates into small transactions (measured 5-13x slower than copy engines during bring-up, see `docs/design_docs/ulysses_pcie.md`). NCCL works but leaves bandwidth and stability on the table on this fabric (see numbers below).

**What.**

- Routes: world size 1 is an identity path; 2 uses all-pairs CUDA P2P copy engines (`cudaMemcpy2DAsync` writes land directly in the peer's final layout, no pack/unpack); 4/8 prefer an all-RDMA route (per-rank mlx5 RC QP, interleaved-UMR MKeys, GPUDirect RDMA) and fall back to all-P2P with a `RuntimeWarning`; an eight-rank 4+4 NUMA hybrid (same-NUMA P2P, cross-NUMA mlx5) is available via `FLASHINFER_ULYSSES_PCIE_ROUTE`.
- Transforms: `scatter_heads` / `gather_heads` interleave the head axis; `exchange_chunks` takes `[1, 1, world_size, chunk]` to the same shape (`all_to_all_single` over a payload a preceding pack already laid out destination-major) and interleaves nothing. On the RDMA routes it configures no MKey, which is what frees it from the 16-bit `bytes_count` that caps the head-axis transforms at 65535 B per peer.
- Synchronization: full-group epoch barriers in device memory (release/acquire, sticky abort half for the RDMA routes); the all-P2P route is CUDA-graph capturable, the RDMA routes refuse capture and bound NIC stalls with a 10 s deadline plus a group-wide abort/quiesce protocol.
- Lifecycle: explicit `allocate_output` registration (collective, lives until `close()`); `input_buffer()` exposes the RDMA landing buffer so producers can write operands where the NIC reads them, removing the largest device-to-device copy on the path (measured ~6% per call at layer scale). The backend has no staging workspaces: `workspace=`, `create_workspace` and the head-chunk primitives from #5027 are refused at world size above one with a message that names `allocate_output()`.
- Failure envelope: a rejection before native code runs (bad operand, refused capture, second stream) is decided from the call's own arguments, so under the SPMD contract every rank rejects it -- the RDMA routes raise the ordinary error and stay usable, the all-P2P route (no abort protocol) poisons teardown and enters BROKEN. A failure inside the transport is fail-stop on every route: on the RDMA routes the failing rank publishes the sticky abort, the peers leave the barrier and `close()` completes; on all-P2P `close()` refuses to synchronize and the process must exit. The design note has the table.
- The element type is per-call (`dtype=` on the collectives), decoupled from the communicator: the transport moves opaque bytes, so FP8/INT8 payloads ride a BF16-sized communicator within the same byte budget. The constructor's capacity is therefore `max_bytes`, replacing main's element-count `max_elems`: the other communication workspaces in `flashinfer.comm` are sized in bytes as well (`buffer_size_in_bytes`, `workspace_size`), and an element count has no single meaning once the element type varies per call. #4924 already targets `max_bytes`. The staging-buffer API from #5027 (`UlyssesWorkspace(max_elems=...)`, `create_workspace(max_elems=...)`) keeps its element count, since those buffers hold one dtype.
- Docs: design note (`docs/design_docs/ulysses_pcie.md`), `docs/api/comm.rst`, env-var reference; fi_trace templates for all three transforms (`scatter_heads` / `gather_heads` gain `trace=` decorators).
- Housekeeping: six `flashinfer.comm` re-exports of JIT module helpers with no users in the repository (`gen_trtllm_comm_module`, `gen_vllm_comm_module`, `gen_pcie_ipc_comm_module`, `get_pcie_ipc_comm_module`, `gen_ulysses_a2a_module`, `get_ulysses_a2a_module`) are dropped; the helpers stay importable from their own modules and from `flashinfer.jit`.

**Changes since the approved revision (a481f1d3).** The branch was rebased onto main (#5027 workspace API, #5263 generated NVLink kernels) and the following landed on top, in this order:

1. `fix(comm): finish the max_bytes rename in the head-chunk tests, benchmark and export example` -- four `max_elems=` constructor calls that arrived with #5027 / #5263 (`_destination_passing_body`, `_head_chunk_body`, `bench_ulysses_head_chunk.py`, `examples/pytorch/ulysses_a2a_export/interface.py`) raised `TypeError` on any 2+ GPU host.
2. `format: format code style by pre-commit` -- the two hooks CI flagged.
3. `test(comm): share the Ulysses test helpers and gloo fixture` -- one FileStore `gloo_pg` fixture in `tests/comm/conftest.py`, `full_mesh` / `forbid_ipc_and_jit` / rendezvous helpers in `tests/test_helpers/ulysses.py`.
4. `fix(comm): check the group's CUDA all-to-all support before arming NVLink` -- the check ran only for `backend="nccl"`, after the NVLink IPC exports were armed.
5. `fix(comm): reject cross-rank FLASHINFER_ULYSSES_PCIE_NICS disagreement` -- the NIC override is now compared across ranks like the route and GID overrides.
6. `feat(comm): warn at garbage collection when a Ulysses communicator was not closed` -- `ResourceWarning` from `__del__` for an armed communicator; no teardown from the finalizer.
7. `fix(comm): refuse workspaces and the head-chunk primitives on the multi-rank PCIe backend` -- see Lifecycle above.
8. `fix(comm): publish the abort when the RDMA routes reject an operand natively` -- the RDMA routes' per-call operand checks run inside the native abort envelope, so a rank whose operand native rejects releases its peers instead of leaving them in the opening barrier (the only native change: the checks moved into `ValidateExchangeOperands`, protocol and wire format untouched); the caller's stream is bound only after a call passes validation; the Python-side envelope is unchanged and documented.
9. `refactor(comm): route Ulysses output validation through the shared helpers` -- `_output_geometry` is the single source of the output shape; the overlap test reuses `_storage_ranges_overlap`.
10. `docs(comm): update Ulysses PCIe prose for auto selection, the failure envelope and follow-ups`.

**Performance** (8x RTX PRO 5000, dual-NUMA 4+4, PCIe Gen5 x16, one 400G mlx5 per GPU; `benchmarks/comm/bench_ulysses_pcie.py`, seq 37888 / heads 56 / head_dim 128 / bf16; median of host-clock loops, max-reduced across ranks, vs the `all_to_all_single`+permute reference; PCIe-side sd ≤ 8%, mostly < 1%, while the NCCL reference jitters up to 50-104% at eight ranks):

| world | route (auto's pick in bold) | scatter | gather | qkv layer | per-rank remote BW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | **all-P2P** | 2.02x | 2.00x | 2.01x | 50.5 GB/s |
| 4 | **all-RDMA** | 1.97x | 1.97x | 1.97x | 42.3 GB/s |
| 8 | **all-RDMA** | 1.49x | 1.43x | 1.48x | 42.6 GB/s |
| 8 | 4+4 hybrid | — | — | 1.27x | 36.4 GB/s |
| 8 | all-P2P (correctness fallback) | 0.81x | 0.43x | 0.30x | 8.8 GB/s |

The transport moves opaque bytes, so the element type should change how long a call
takes but not how fast the link runs. Same node, ws8 all-RDMA, seq 37888 / 56 heads /
head_dim 128, only the dtype varies:

| dtype | bytes/elem | scatter ms | qkv layer ms | remote BW (scatter) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 2 | 1.389 | 5.583 | 42.8 GB/s |
| fp8_e4m3fn | 1 | 0.695 | 2.871 | 42.7 GB/s |
| int8 | 1 | 0.696 | 2.870 | 42.7 GB/s |

Halving the element size halves the time (1.389 -> 0.695 ms) and leaves bandwidth put;
the two 1-byte types are within noise of each other. ws2 P2P saturates ~95% of the
effective Gen5 x16 link; the RDMA route reaches ~85% of the 400G NIC.

Re-measured at this head on the same node (ws8 all-RDMA, same shapes, 5 trials x 200 iterations, other tenants idle) to confirm the round changed nothing on the hot path: scatter 1.427 ms at 41.6 GB/s remote bandwidth (table above: 1.389 ms / 42.8 GB/s), gather 1.554 ms at 38.2 GB/s, both with trial-to-trial sd below 2%; the q/k/v layer loop read 6.93 ms with sd 9.2%, which is inside its own noise band on a shared node and is not re-plotted here. The `rnr_nak_retry_err` counters on all eight NICs did not move during the run.

**Limitations.** Experimental; single host; world sizes 1/2/4/8 (the copy scheduler's `rank ^ step` order needs powers of two); the RDMA routes require batch 1 and refuse CUDA-graph capture, and bound the head-axis transforms at head-row pitch `H*D*elem <= 65535` B (`exchange_chunks` registers no MKey and is not bounded); the JIT module links libibverbs/libmlx5 even when topology picks all-P2P, so it is JIT-only and deliberately absent from AOT; a transport failure is fail-stop as described above, and an all-P2P failure leaves the process to be terminated by the launcher. Validated on one topology (4+4 NUMA, one mlx5 per GPU); no work-request-level mlx5 unit tests yet — the RDMA data path is covered end to end. No CI lane exercises the PCIe wire path (the CI images carry no rdma-core and the GPU lanes are single-GPU); the host-mock and single-rank halves of the suite run there, the multi-rank half runs on the reference node.

Planned follow-ups, prepared on a branch and deliberately kept out of this PR to leave the approved protocol untouched: publish the abort from Python on every route (the all-P2P route already imports every peer's signal buffer), so a Python-side rejection on a rank that broke the SPMD contract releases the peers too; publish a geometry word with the opening epoch so ranks that call with different shapes at the same position break the group instead of writing a misdescribed layout; post the RDMA receive before the opening barrier (closes the window in which a peer's write can arrive before the receive is posted; no RNR retries were counted during this round's benchmark, so this is hygiene rather than a measured stall); build the all-P2P route without rdma-core; `out=None` with lazy registration; per-output `capacity_bytes`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

N/A

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Ran on the 8-GPU reference node (8x RTX PRO 5000, dual-NUMA 4+4, one mlx5 per GPU, rdma-core 63, CUDA 13.4, torch 2.13) at the pushed head: `tests/comm/test_ulysses_communicator.py` 132 passed / 22 skipped / 0 failed, `tests/comm/test_ulysses_topology.py` 112 passed / 0 skipped (244 passed / 22 skipped in one run), `tests/trace/test_ulysses_trace.py` + `tests/trace/test_template_registry.py` 10 passed. The 22 skips are the forced-NVLink family on this NVLink-less machine; every PCIe case ran (p2p, all-RDMA and 4+4 hybrid routes at world sizes 2/4/8, the chunk exchange, the landing-buffer producer path, the p2p fail-stop pair, and the new two-rank RDMA case in which rank 0's native dtype rejection publishes the abort, rank 1 leaves the barrier with "peer 0 aborted the exchange", and both ranks close). Correctness is bit-exact against the `all_gather`-based reference for fp16/bf16/fp32 and byte-exact for int8/uint8/fp8 across all three routes, including non-power-of-two head dims on the UMR path, CUDA-graph capture+replay of a q/k/v/out layer on the P2P route, and `backend="auto"` with the experimental opt-in selecting PCIe on this node.

On a single-GPU host the same files give 186 passed / 90 skipped (host-mock and single-rank halves), `pre-commit run --all-files` is green, and `scripts/check_pr_api_diff.py` / `scripts/check_pr_document.py` report no findings.

## Reviewer Notes

- The riskiest pieces are the epoch-barrier protocol (`include/flashinfer/comm/ulysses_pcie.cuh`) and the mlx5 transport (`csrc/ulysses_pcie_transport.cuh`): QP bring-up, interleaved-MKey geometry (pitch ≤ 65535), completion accounting with per-exchange immediate tags, and the abort/quiesce teardown ledger.
- `_validate`'s byte-budget capacity math after the per-call dtype change (`flashinfer/comm/ulysses.py`) is worth a close read; the rescale rationale is in the commit message of the dtype commit.
- The failure envelope is route-dependent on purpose, and the design note's "Failure envelope" table is the contract to review against. Python-side rejections are rank-uniform under the SPMD contract, so the RDMA routes keep the communicator usable (the multi-rank tests rely on refusing capture and a batch > 1 operand recoverably); the all-P2P route poisons teardown because its barrier has no abort protocol at all. Native failures on the RDMA routes publish the abort (now including the per-call operand checks) and `close()` completes. Publishing the abort from Python on every route is the first follow-up above.
- Things that are correct but will draw a question: (1) full-group CUDA IPC is required even on the RDMA routes, because the barrier signals are always IPC-mapped -- RDMA removes the P2P *data* requirement, not the P2P requirement; (2) `batch == 1` on the RDMA routes comes from mode 0's flat `rank * payload` remote offset, not from the NIC; (3) `input_ready` is deliberately reused between `RunHybridBarrier` and `EnqueueCopies` so the side streams inherit the post-barrier state; (4) the copy-engine writes are ordered against the closing barrier's release store through the `copy_done` event join, i.e. through `cudaMemcpyAsync` completion semantics; (5) the per-call `dtype` is really per-`allocate_output`: the registered buffer pins it and native re-checks every call against it.
- Placement: the backend uses the experimental machinery (warn-once, gated `auto`, no AOT) but lives in `flashinfer/comm/` with tests in `tests/comm/`, because it extends the stable `UlyssesCommunicator` class and the routing shares its decision layer; there is no precedent for an `@experimental_backend` in core. If the maintainers prefer the Experimental Track layout, the code splits at the `_pcie_*` seam (the methods touch only `rank`, `world_size`, `device`, `dtype`, `max_bytes`, `backend`, `transport`, `decision`, `_state` and the `_gather` / `_require_open` / `_validate` / `_output_geometry` helpers) and we will move it.

title: MUSA: add packed-varlen Mamba2 SSU provider for Nemotron MTP6
body:
## Summary

Add a MUSA packed-varlen Mamba2 selective-state-update provider for the vLLM Nemotron MTP6 contract.

The vLLM path supplies packed rank-3 `x/dt/B/C`, device-resident `cu_seqlens` and `num_accepted_tokens`, and source/destination state-slot tables. The provider keeps metadata on device, selects the source slot from `max(accepted - 1, 0)`, processes every token in each sequence interval, and writes each recurrence state to its destination slot. It supports MUSA Triton 3.2, broadcast parameter views, int32/int64 metadata, and graph replay without host synchronization.

The earlier SGLang-specific CAKE raw MTP gate change was reverted because its fixed 4-D/intermediate-buffer contract does not match vLLM and its CUDA implementation is not a MUSA provider.

## Validation

- MUSA S5000, Torch `2.11.0.post1+musa5.2.0`, Triton `3.2.0`.
- `160 passed` in the Mamba varlen/MTP/public API test slice.
- Two-sequence eager oracle plus MUSA graph replay passed with changing accepted-token metadata; replay output/state max differences were `0.0`.
- Nemotron 3.5 MTP6 with `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` completed a real HTTP request and the `_musa_varlen_ssu_kernel` specialization was generated.
- Consumer integration pin: `a1c69c8ebef07f2632707f96b4f2785f773ecf1c`.

title: [SM120] sparse MLA prefill: dispatch support for extra_page_block_size 128/256
body:
**Repo**: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer (PR against `main`; base file `csrc/sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu`)

## Title
`[SM120] sparse MLA prefill: dispatch support for extra_page_block_size 128/256`

## Body

### Motivation
DeepSeek-V4.1 inference with the DeepSeek-V4 attention backend on SM120
(RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) dispatches sparse MLA prefill with
`extra_page_block_size` in `{128, 256}` (dual-path KV: main pages + extra
indexer pages; the values come from the V4.1 fp4-indexer / DSPARK speculative
decoding configuration). The SM120 prefill dispatcher only accepts
`{64, 2}`, so `dispatch_dsv4_dual()` falls through to `return false` and the
prefill launch fails at runtime (engine crash / missing kernel selection).

### Change
- Extend the `extra_page_block_size` validity guard from `{64, 2}` to `{64, 2, 128, 256}`.
- Add `128`/`256` template dispatch branches in both dispatch families inside
  `dispatch_dsv4_dual()` (`DISPATCH_FULLTILE_BY_NH_PBSX` and `DISPATCH_BY_NH_PBSX`).

The kernel templates themselves already accept these values as the `PBSX`
template parameter (verified on the same code family in flashinfer 0.6.18 —
see Notes).

### Verification
- Production-verified on flashinfer **0.6.18** (identical dispatch family):
  8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm120), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8+EP8,
  DSPARK speculative decoding, 262144 context, ~48h serving, >200K-token
  prefills: without the patch the prefill fails to dispatch; with it,
  0 failures (bench: 95 tok/s single-stream, 546 tok/s agg@16).
- The patch was mapped 1:1 onto `main`'s current `dispatch_dsv4_dual()`
  (same macro names and anchors). CI hardware validation on `main` requested;
  if main's `sparse_mla_sm120` headers constrain `PBSX` differently, happy to
  adjust.

### Notes
- First observed on sglang dsv4.1 line (sgl-project/sglang, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash).
- The `== 2` leg is kept as the final `else` to preserve existing behavior.

title: feat(cake_nvfp4_attn): add experimental NVFP4 attention on SM103
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add experimental NVFP4 attention on SM103 through
`flashinfer.prefill.prepare_nvfp4_attention(q, k, v, out, backend="cake")`.
Preparation quantizes contiguous BF16 Q/K/V once and returns an
`NVFP4AttentionRunner`. Calling the runner executes QK, softmax and PV attention
and writes into the caller's BF16 output without CUDA allocation. Prepare a
new runner when input values or bindings change. The initial backend supports
noncausal attention with D=128 and S divisible by 512.

The API emits the standard experimental warning and hands off to the feature
package. Preparation bounds E4M3 block scales to their finite range before
conversion, including on PyTorch versions that do not saturate finite overflow.
Preparation, JIT registration, and generated CUDA are contained under
`flashinfer/experimental/nvfp4_attention/`.

On all three validated shapes, export latency is within 3% of both source
launch policies. The largest measured increase is **0.2228%** versus
selected source and **0.3008%** versus the original pointer-argument
policy, both rebuilt with the current compiler. These are prepared-submit
measurements; input quantization and preparation are outside timing. The
generated CUDA and exported launch code are unchanged.

## Generated-program export evidence

**Updated on 2026-09-19: NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), 2386.7–3099.3 achieved TFLOP/s.**
The complete three-shape campaign now passes in **one process**, with the real
PyTorch CPU/CUDA allocation profiler running **before each row's timing**.
Correctness, zero allocation/free, strict CUPTI cold-L2 timing, and the
unchanged per-shape 3% performance gates all pass.

The original absolute readings were invalid because allocation profiling
replaced process-global CUPTI activity-buffer and timestamp callbacks.
Restoring only activity-buffer callbacks recovered records but could leave
CPU clock ticks interpreted as nanoseconds. The benchmark collector used for
this validation re-registers its activity callbacks and restores a native
nanosecond timestamp callback for each collection session. Its native lifetime
also permits clean CUDA context teardown. It does not rescale old results or
fall back to another GPU timer.

This removes the earlier fresh-process/profiler-after-timing workaround.
The exported kernel was not changed to obtain these numbers. The selected
source uses grid-constant TMA arguments and PDL; the original policy uses
pointer arguments without PDL. Both policies are rebuilt from unchanged
kernel source using the current compiler. The historical compiler snapshot
was unavailable, so this is not an exact frozen-compiler rerun.

## Hardware and protocol

- One exclusively allocated NVIDIA GB300, SM103 / capability 10.3;
  driver 580.159.03, PyTorch 2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c.nv26.07, CUDA 13.3.
- Unchanged target revision: `034bb09742566ff991abad1a56dd28f5e8efac2f`.
- CUPTI activity timing, cold L2, fallback disabled; symmetric external
  CUDA Graphs, three counterbalanced groups, 100 ms warmup and 1000 ms
  reportable budget per arm/group. SM clock threshold: 1900 MHz.
- Selected source, original source policy, and export share the same physical
  input/output buffers within each row. All three pass independent GPU SDPA
  checks over quantized Q/K/V before and after timing at `atol=1, rtol=0.1`.
  Independently prepared packed inputs match byte-for-byte and remain unchanged.
- Every warmed export submit records zero device allocations/frees and zero
  allocation/free API events, with the expected native launch and kernel present.

## Per-shape results

| Shape (B,H,S,D) | Selected source ms | Export ms | Source / Export | Original source policy ms | Original / Export | Correctness and gates |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| (4,8,4096,128) | 0.114913 | **0.115169** | 0.997777x | 0.115553 | 1.003334x | pass |
| (1,8,32768,128) | 1.437610 | **1.440234** | 0.998178x | 1.439690 | 0.999622x | pass |
| (8,32,8192,128) | 2.833268 | **2.838066** | 0.998309x | 2.829555 | 0.997001x | pass |

## Absolute attention throughput

Using the dense-attention FLOPs convention, QK and PV count two FLOPs per
multiply-add:

`FLOPs per call = 4 * B * H * S^2 * D`

`TFLOP/s = FLOPs per call / (latency_ms * 10^9)`

The numerator excludes softmax, scaling, and quantization operations. The
measured attention latency includes softmax and internal kernel work; input
Q/K/V quantization and preparation are outside timing. These are achieved
useful TFLOP/s with no sparse-operation multiplier.

| Shape (B,H,S,D) | FLOPs per call | Selected source TFLOP/s | Export TFLOP/s | Original source policy TFLOP/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (4,8,4096,128) | 274,877,906,944 | 2392.1 | **2386.7** | 2378.8 |
| (1,8,32768,128) | 4,398,046,511,104 | 3059.3 | **3053.7** | 3054.9 |
| (8,32,8192,128) | 8,796,093,022,208 | 3104.6 | **3099.3** | 3108.6 |

Geomeans over all three correct, timed rows: selected source **0.776425 ms**,
export **0.777912 ms**, source/export **0.998088x**;
original source policy **0.777898 ms**, original/export
**0.999983x**. All shapes carry the aligned,
noncausal, and owner-required tags, so those tag denominators are also 3/3.
No shape or gate-failing row was dropped. Correctness and both 3% performance
comparisons pass on **3/3 shapes**, along with the 2% direction/drift gates.

## Timing and isolation evidence

All three rows use the same worker PID, with allocation profiling before
each row. All **36 CUPTI collections** pass positive/nonoverlapping interval,
independent physical-envelope, and synchronized-completion checks. The
benchmark process exits normally, including interpreter teardown. Host
durations are consistency diagnostics, not substitutes for CUPTI GPU timings.

The approximately 1 Hz GPU/process census contains **276 samples**, with no
query errors and no observed process other than the expected worker on the
measured GPU. Samples at GPU utilization of at least 90% report **2070 MHz**.
These are sampled NVML clocks/processes, not continuous CUPTI clock measurements.
Before/after GPU reports, allocation profiles, and full CUPTI activity intervals
are retained with the validation results.

## Validation turnaround

The successful three-row validation took **297.075 s** managed end to end,
including **285.163 s** in the runner. Including source/environment setup and
preflight repairs, turnaround from the first setup attempt to successful
validation was **1836.306 s**. Completed native builds were reused. GPU kernel
latencies are reported separately above.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Tracking issue: [#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254).
Owner: @yyihuang. The tracker records the use case, experimental rationale,
and proposed graduation target of v0.7.0, subject to maintainer review.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

The checked test result applies to the declared experimental test scope:

Latest naming and scale-range repair (`034bb09742566ff991abad1a56dd28f5e8efac2f`):

- `NVFP4AttentionRunner` names the execution object; calling it runs QK, softmax
  and PV attention on its bound inputs.
- `python -m pytest tests/experimental/test_cake_nvfp4_attention.py -q`:
  **6/6 passed** on B300 (SM103), including the original three shapes and
  CPU/CUDA checks for zero, normal values, the E4M3 scale limit, and signed
  BF16 finite extremes. The example and targeted Ruff checks also passed.
- Validation used PyTorch `2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c.nv26.07` / CUDA 13.3. This build
  already saturates the old quantizer on CPU and CUDA; the explicit scale bound
  also covers supported builds whose FP8 conversion can produce NaN on finite
  overflow.
- Test and example processes took **34.731 s** together. The successful managed
  validation took **95.666 s** end to end. Including two setup failures and
  their repairs, the validation campaign took **300.956 s** from first submission
  to successful completion. Those setup failures occurred before testing.

The corrected performance tables above measure this revision. The naming and
scale repair changes preparation-side behavior, with no generated CUDA or
launch-path changes.

Earlier export and packaging validation:

- `python -m pytest tests/experimental/test_cake_nvfp4_attention.py -q`: **4/4 passed**, covering the three shapes, output reuse, reference correctness, and rejection of an unknown backend.
- `python examples/cake_nvfp4_attention.py`: **passed**.
- The test and example processes import the target implementation without the source implementation on their Python import path.
- Canonical export validation: **3/3 passed**, including native build and package-data discovery, zero-allocation/free submit checks, and both per-row performance gates.

The successful tests/example workload took **16.490 s**; its managed turnaround
was **36.337 s**. This duration is separate from the export campaign above.

- [x] Formatting checks completed.
- [x] Wheel packaging and archive-content verification completed.

Wheel inspection verified eight members, including both generated CUDA translation
units and required headers, with source bytes matching the checkout. This checks

**222.754 s**, including **222.630 s** of packaging. The combined pre-commit and
wheel workload took **284.323 s**, with **287.694 s** managed turnaround.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

(Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)

title: feat(moe): CUTLASS unified runners consume the TRT-LLM canonical activation packs
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Unified CUTLASS runners now consume the same `MoEActivationPack` as TRT-LLM / CuTe-DSL / Cake for each MMA pair, so mixed candidate sets like `(TrtllmFp4Config(), CutlassNvfp4Config())` work on one pack. No kernel / `core.py` changes.

- **NVFP4**: packed `uint8 [M, H/2]` + linear E4M3 `[M, H/16]` scale (was BF16, in-kernel quant). `hidden_size % 64 == 0` required (kernel reads the linear scale with a 64-padded row stride); `prepare_cutlass_nvfp4_weights` rejects other H at load time.
- **MXFP8 / MXFP4×MXFP8**: linear `[M, H/32]` scale by default; `QuantConfig(swizzled_scale_factors=True)` selects the flat swizzled 1-D `input_sf` (CUTLASS MXFP8 runners only; CUTLASS NVFP4, TRT-LLM and CuTe-DSL reject it in `check_support`). `Cutlass*Mxfp8*Config.prepare_activations(x, quant=config.quant)` reads the layout from the same `QuantConfig` the layer declares.
- `Cutlass*Config.prepare_activations` produce the canonical packs via the shared `prepare.py` helpers (`CutlassNvfp4Config.prepare_activations` is `TrtllmFp4Config.prepare_activations`); `MoEActivationPack` docs one row per pair; design doc drops #4914's singleton-candidate guidance and describes the shared pack in an undated "One activation pack per MMA pair" bullet instead of a changelog section; `unified_moe` benchmark quantizes for CUTLASS NVFP4.
- New mixed-candidate tests run one pack through TRT-LLM + CuTe-DSL + CUTLASS (NVFP4, MXFP4×MXFP8) and TRT-LLM + CUTLASS (MXFP8); candidates that decline the pair on the test device (CuTe-DSL W4A8 on SM107) are dropped, not failed. The NVFP4 reference now models the kernels' GEMM2-input NVFP4 requantization, which halves its error against every backend (VR200 CI had crossed the unchanged 0.3 tolerance by one element).
- CUTLASS runners reject `QuantConfig(per_token_scale=True)` and a pack carrying `per_token_scale`; the flat ABI has no such input and packing silently dropped it (pre-existing, surfaced in review).

TODO: `activation_prequantized` knob for a CUTLASS BF16-in-kernel path, if a framework needs it.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- Follow-up to #4610 / #4914 (unified CUTLASS runners) and #5061 (three-axis `QuantConfig`); reverts #4914's "choose one singleton candidate set" guidance.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

On SM100 (B200):
- `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_cutlass.py` — all pass, including new mixed-candidate tests that build one `MoELayer` over TRT-LLM + CuTe-DSL + CUTLASS (NVFP4, MXFP4×MXFP8) and TRT-LLM + CUTLASS (MXFP8) on a single pack.
- `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py -k cutlass` — CUTLASS contract handlers moved onto the canonical packs.
- `tests/moe/test_unified_moe.py -k "cutlass or swizzled or Backend"` — pass.
- `benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine unified_moe --quant-variant nvfp4 --backends cutlass --refcheck` — pass.

## Reviewer Notes

- User-visible changes:
  - `CutlassNvfp4Config` takes the pre-quantized NVFP4 pack, not BF16 (b12x / cuTile still take BF16).
  - `CutlassNvfp4Config.prepare_weights` rejects `hidden_size % 64 != 0` at load time; on `main` such shapes ran via in-kernel quantization.
  - `CutlassNvfp4Config.prepare_activations` is an alias of `TrtllmFp4Config.prepare_activations` (same default, optional `quant=`); `CutlassMxfp8Config` / `CutlassMxfp8Mxfp4Config.prepare_activations` take `quant=` (the layer's `MoEConfig.quant`) instead of a `swizzled_scale_factors` bool.
  - CUTLASS runners reject `QuantConfig(per_token_scale=True)` instead of ignoring it.
- `_DEFAULT_BACKEND` unchanged.

title: perf(prims_ts): mask partial last K/V tile outside softmax loop to prevent register spills in dense context fmha
body: ## 📌 Description For dense query-paired context FMHA with S % 128 != 0, the softmax loop ran a masked row-max variant on every iteration. The tail size was a compile-time constant, so each tail value produced a different cubin and some tail sizes spilled heavily in the softmax warps. The build at S=147600 (with a tail size of S % 128 = 16) spilled 4.7x more than the tile-aligned build, evicted K/V from L2 and took 21% more cycles than ideal self attention scaling of S^2. The problem is exacerbated at large S. With these changes, the softmax loop now runs N_tiles-1 unmasked iterations and a tail block masks the last tile once. Specifically, the softmax task now loops over only the floor(S / 128) full K/V tiles with the plain unmasked row max. Then, a separate block after the loop handles the one partial tile and mask its zero-filled keys to -inf. The mask code is no longer in the loop body, so now the loop's register allocation is the same for every S. **Measured on B200 ncu elapsed cycles (B=2 H=40 D=128 bf16; lower is better):** S=147600: 1283M -> 1037M (-19.2%), spill stores 764 GB -> 55 GB S=75600: 289M -> 274M (-5.3%) S=111600: 613M -> 593M (-3.3%) S=147456 (aligned, path untouched): unchanged PV-fp8 S=147600: 740 ms -> 650 ms Correctness vs SDPA passes at S=4112, 4176, 4096, 1040. **Test on Wan2.2-T2V-A14B E2E workloads shows improvement on both QKV-BF16 and QK-BF16/PV-FP8 modes:** Across three prompts P1, P2, P3 over different number of output tokens, which is controlled by number of frames and resolution. | prompt | S | S mod 128 | |---|---|---| | P1 | 75600 | 80 | | P2 | 111600 | 112 | | P3 | 147600 | 16 | ## 🔍 Related Issues ## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! For both PV-BF16 and PV-FP8. ## 🔬 Experimental Track - [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: # - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release. - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff). - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included. - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. title: perf: optimize CuTe DSL W4A4 and W4A16 unfused finalize
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

@humansand

Reduce the cost of deterministic CuTe DSL MoE finalize for W4A4 per-tensor/per-token NVFP4 activation scaling and W4A16 BF16 activations when `use_fused_finalize=False`.

- **Reduction:** replace the native standalone finalizer with a shared CuTe kernel. Reduce top-k slots in ascending order using FP32 round-to-nearest FMA with flush-to-zero behavior matching native `--use_fast_math`, then convert once to BF16. Negative routes are skipped before loading expert output; all-masked tokens write zero.
- **Layouts:** preserve W4A4 expanded rows (`token * top_k + slot`) and W4A16 permuted rows selected by the routing map. `input_is_expanded` specializes address selection at compile time; permuted row zero remains valid. Both paths use contiguous, aligned BF16 vectors of eight elements.
- **PDL:** issue FC2's dependent-launch hint after its input dependency wait, allowing the standalone finalizer to prepare early. It preloads already-completed routing metadata, then waits before all FC2-output reads. W4A16's previous FC2 tail hint moves to this point for unfused output; the fused hint remains unchanged.
- **Launch geometry:** 32 threads for at most eight tokens, otherwise 128; four vectors per thread above 1024 tokens, otherwise one. The private helper accepts FP32/BF16/FP16 routing scales and int32 maps; input/output are separate contiguous BF16 matrices with hidden size divisible by eight and 16-byte-aligned storage. Zero tokens return without a kernel launch.
- **Benchmark fix:** forward `--no-fused-finalize` to CUTLASS, where it was previously ignored. `True` permits fused tactics; it does not force one. The performance campaign below measures CuTe DSL only.
- **Scope:** five CuTe DSL files plus benchmark flag wiring; no C++ changes or new tests. Public MoE defaults and fused-finalize arithmetic remain unchanged.

### Uniform performance comparison

- **Source:** base CuTe files `eb5f05be1f8e3ef8aa017a66dcbd5d80119b1095`; head CuTe files `f9dd3c10541e087b716772245a9d033499745048`. Both are overlays on official nightly `0.7.0.dev20260917`, source `d233e27ddddbcfdc24eec38ab4dffda1f43ff49c`, with the same exact-head `benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py`. These are source overlays on the pinned runtime, not whole-repository builds. The baseline includes the PR-base W4A16 host/kernel files so unrelated nightly-to-base changes are held fixed.
- **Matrix:** W4A4 per-tensor, W4A4 per-token, W4A16 × base/head × fused/unfused: 12 independent forward sweeps, 15 token counts each, 180 rows. Each arm uses its own autotune cache. There is no reverse sweep or aggregation across sweeps.
- **Workload:** H7168/I2048, 256 global experts, top-k8, groups8/top-groups4, routed scaling2.5, SwiGLU, seed42 and routing-bias scale0.01; simulated EP8 (32 local experts, offset0), TP1. Routing and W4A4 input activation quantization are timed; W4A16 consumes BF16 directly. Inter-GPU communication is excluded.
- **Timing:** native benchmark medians from 10 warmups and 100 CUDA-graph CUPTI samples, cold L2, PDL enabled, ordinary autotuning, `FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0`, JIT enabled. Compilation, allocations and tuning are outside measured latency.
- **Environment:** `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3`; one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) GPU0 of an eight-GPU devbox, UUID `GPU-e32ead05-f360-d139-903a-f38cf17eecb8`, 275040 MiB, 1100 W power limit; driver 590.48.01, CUDA toolkit 13.2.78, Python 3.12.3, Torch `2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.05`. Matching FlashInfer python/cubin `0.7.0.dev20260917` and jit-cache/SM103 cache `0.7.0.dev20260917+cu130`; CuTe DSL 4.6.2, TVM FFI 0.1.11, cupti-python 13.4.0 and CUDA CUPTI 13.4.92. All 180 rows used native CUPTI without fallback. Native helpers absent from the nightly cache were built once and shared across both overlays; subsequent kernel specialization uses CuTe DSL JIT.
- **Result:** W4A4 per-tensor: 15/15 token counts improve; W4A4 per-token: 15/15 token counts improve; W4A16: 15/15 token counts improve. No measured unfused regression in this single sweep.

### Reproduce performance

Run in Bash inside the explicit image above. Keep one pinned installed runtime, construct fresh base/head overlays from the four/five changed CuTe files, and use one canonical unchanged nightly `flashinfer/jit` directory for both arms. Use the exact-head benchmark for both. The normal CLI cannot select an individual CuTe precision for timing, so the external launcher calls the unmodified native `run_benchmark` with `profile_cuda=False` and the appropriate `profile_backend` selector.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Run inside nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3; use a fresh task directory.
export TASK_ROOT=${TASK_ROOT:-$PWD/fi-finalize-rerun}
export BASE_REV=eb5f05be1f8e3ef8aa017a66dcbd5d80119b1095
export HEAD_REV=${HEAD_REV:-f9dd3c10541e087b716772245a9d033499745048}
export NIGHTLY_REV=d233e27ddddbcfdc24eec38ab4dffda1f43ff49c
mkdir -p "$TASK_ROOT/artifacts"
cd "$TASK_ROOT"
export TASK_ROOT=$PWD
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git source-repo
git -C source-repo fetch origin "$BASE_REV" "$HEAD_REV" "$NIGHTLY_REV"
unset PIP_CONSTRAINT PYTHONPATH FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK
python -m pip install --no-deps \
  flashinfer-python==0.7.0.dev20260917 flashinfer-cubin==0.7.0.dev20260917 \
  flashinfer-jit-cache==0.7.0.dev20260917+cu130 \
  flashinfer-jit-cache-sm103a==0.7.0.dev20260917+cu130 \
  --index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl/nightly \
  --extra-index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl/nightly/cu130
python -m pip install nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2 apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11 \
  cupti-python==13.4.0 nvidia-cuda-cupti==13.4.92 pytest==9.1.1
python - <<'PYSETUP'
import os, shutil, subprocess
from pathlib import Path
import flashinfer
from flashinfer import _build_meta
root = Path(os.environ['TASK_ROOT']).resolve()
assert flashinfer.__version__ == '0.7.0.dev20260917'
assert _build_meta.__git_commit__ == os.environ['NIGHTLY_REV']
installed = Path(flashinfer.__file__).resolve().parent
files = [
    'flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/fused_moe.py',
    'flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell/blockscaled_contiguous_grouped_gemm_finalize_fusion.py',
    'flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell/moe_w4a16.py',
    'flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell/moe_w4a16_kernel.py',
    'flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell/moe_finalize.py',
]
for arm in ('shared-nightly', 'base', 'head'):
    target = root / 'overlays' / arm / 'flashinfer'
    shutil.copytree(installed, target, symlinks=True,
                    ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('__pycache__', '*.pyc'))
    if arm == 'shared-nightly':
        continue
    shutil.rmtree(target / 'jit')
    (target / 'jit').symlink_to(root / 'overlays/shared-nightly/flashinfer/jit')
    rev = os.environ['BASE_REV' if arm == 'base' else 'HEAD_REV']
    for path in files[:4 if arm == 'base' else 5]:
        data = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(root / 'source-repo'), 'show', f'{rev}:{path}'])
        (root / 'overlays' / arm / path).write_bytes(data)
data = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(root / 'source-repo'), 'show',
                                os.environ['HEAD_REV'] + ':benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py'])
(root / 'bench_moe_deepseek.py').write_bytes(data)
PYSETUP
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0
for MODE in w4a4-per-tensor w4a4-per-token w4a16; do
  for ARM in base head; do
    export MODE ARM PYTHONPATH="$TASK_ROOT/overlays/$ARM"
    mkdir -p "artifacts/$ARM"
    for FINALIZE in fused unfused; do
      export FINALIZE
      python - <<'PYBENCH' 2>&1 | tee "artifacts/$ARM/$MODE-$FINALIZE.log"
import dataclasses, inspect, json, math, os, runpy, warnings
from pathlib import Path
from cupti import cupti
from flashinfer import CuteDslMoEWrapper
import torch
assert torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) == (10, 3)
assert inspect.signature(CuteDslMoEWrapper.__init__).parameters['enable_pdl'].default is True
warnings.filterwarnings('error', message=r'.*Falling back to CUDA events for benchmarking.*')
root, arm, mode, finalize = (os.environ[k] for k in ('TASK_ROOT', 'ARM', 'MODE', 'FINALIZE'))
bench = runpy.run_path(root + '/bench_moe_deepseek.py')
results = bench['run_benchmark'](
    token_counts=[2**i for i in range(15)], warmup=10, iters=100,
    ep_config=8, tp_config=1, do_autotune=True, verbose=True,
    use_cuda_graph=True, use_cupti=True, use_wrapper=True,
    routing_bias_scale=0.01, include_activation_quant=True,
    use_per_token_activation=(mode == 'w4a4-per-token'),
    use_fused_finalize=(finalize == 'fused'), profile_cuda=False,
    profile_backend='cute-dsl-w4a16' if mode == 'w4a16' else 'cute-dsl',
    backends=('cutedsl',),
    autotune_cache=f'{root}/artifacts/{arm}/{mode}-{finalize}-tactics.json',
)
assert [r.tokens for r in results] == [2**i for i in range(15)]
assert all(r.backend == ('CuteDSL W4A16' if mode == 'w4a16' else 'CuteDSL W4A4') for r in results)
assert all(math.isfinite(r.latency_ms) and r.latency_ms > 0 for r in results)
Path(f'{root}/artifacts/{arm}/{mode}-{finalize}.json').write_text(
    json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(r) for r in results], indent=2) + '\n')
PYBENCH
    done
  done
done
```

| SM100 | BF16 remote-Q/owner-O distributed FA4 adapter; O-TMA, peer-layout checks and disposable-padding query scheduling; **complete** external FA4 patch | Requires explicit full-NVLink/NVSHMEM, B=1/H=56/D=128 and U2/U4/U8 shape allowlist. Not FP8 FA4 or a general varlen backend. B200 reruns pending. |
| SM90 | BF16-to-E4M3 per-head quantization fused with destination-major QKV packing; complete examples using in-tree FA3 BF16/FP8 | Native FA3 compute is now connected in the example with BF16 wire. The separate per-head FP8 pack is not an FP8 transport pipeline. Hopper execution pending. |
| SM120 | Grouped QKV projection producer across all destination ranks; benchmark-local head pipeline; shape-stable full-head K-mean helper | Complete native BF16/FP8/Sage examples now reuse existing in-tree kernels. Includes a correctness fix to existing BF16/FP16 and CuTe-DSL Sage BSA kernels. Native BF16/Sage U4 validation is recorded below; grouped-producer multi-GPU validation remains pending. No CE transport or SGLang-specific norm/RoPE-to-wire. |

Public functions are thin, explicitly called `@flashinfer_experimental_api` wrappers; implementation stays in `flashinfer/experimental/ulysses`. No AOT or auto routing. Frameworks continue to own TP/EP/CP/SP groups, stream scheduling, scale agreement, valid-prefix semantics and fallback selection before launch. Prepared storage is reusable, single-stream/non-reentrant, and outputs alias workspace. Small-head configurations need not benefit.

FA4 setup is explicit and reproducible: the cumulative patch targets public FlashAttention commit `c2006099f3ff03de187f4e1b27e756fe6df482ba`, includes the original distributed kernel rather than depending on a private intermediate commit, retains the BSD license, and is never applied at import/runtime. Whether that kernel patch should instead land in FlashAttention needs maintainer agreement.

Details, safety contracts, runnable commands and graduation gates: [`docs/design_docs/ulysses_architecture_experiments.md`](https://github.com/tiffany940107/flashinfer/blob/feat/ulysses-architecture-backends-20260917/docs/design_docs/ulysses_architecture_experiments.md).

### Native-kernel integration update (2026-09-18)

Commit `0f2c6433` adds a complete `bench_ulysses_native_attention.py` example: QKV -> input Ulysses -> existing FlashInfer kernel -> output Ulysses -> local O. It compares ordinary, whole-QKV fusion, chunk-serial and chunk-overlap using the same selected compute/quantization recipe. The producer benchmark also accepts these native backends.

- SM90: native FA3 BF16 / E4M3 FP8.
- SM100: native TRT-LLM Gen BF16 / E4M3 FP8, **separate from the external distributed FA4 experiment**.
- SM120: native all-active-block BF16 BSA, FP8 FMHA, and Sage QK-INT8/PV-FP8. No external FA4/Sage package is needed for these examples.

All examples use **BF16 communication**. Quantization/layout conversion is timed; setup/JIT is not. One valid non-causal prefix is supported; tail output is zero/disposable, not a second packed sequence. FP8 uses a fixed scalar recipe shared across ranks/heads, not model-calibrated per-head scales. This does not wire the separate per-head FP8 quant-pack primitive into FP8 transport.

Initial single-rank smoke (S256/used193/H4/D128, groups=[1,3], 8 samples) passed numerical comparisons. Ordinary -> overlap medians: BF16 **0.377456 -> 1.018512 ms**, FP8 **0.265920 -> 0.774944 ms**, Sage **0.623744 -> 1.475248 ms**. These small U1 cases are slower with chunking and exercise **no inter-GPU A2A**. Relative RMSE versus BF16 SDPA was 0.001835 / 0.051096 / 0.036461 respectively; lossy checks do not imply model-quality acceptance. Those U1 smoke numbers do not claim a multi-GPU speedup; see the separate U4 follow-up below.

[Backend mapping, runnable U2/U4/U8 commands, boundaries and raw smoke samples](https://github.com/tiffany940107/flashinfer/blob/feat/ulysses-architecture-backends-20260917/docs/design_docs/ulysses_native_attention_examples.md).

### Four-GPU PRO 6000 BSA correctness and performance update (2026-09-19)

Fix commit: `b1f3a95a`. Measurements were collected on 2026-09-18.

**Correctness fix:** concurrent memory traffic exposed a K/V shared-memory stage-reuse race in the existing SM120 BF16/FP16 and CuTe-DSL Sage BSA kernels. The failure reproduces on a single GPU with unrelated copy traffic, without NCCL. Add `cute.arch.fence_view_async_shared()` before K/V `consumer_release` to order generic-proxy LDSM reads before the next async-proxy TMA overwrite (four fence sites across two kernels). No global synchronization, overlap disablement, compiler optimization downgrade, or relaxed tolerances.

**Measured configuration:** 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, PCIe/no NVLink; GPU 0/1/2 pairwise PIX and GPU 3 to the others NODE. B=1, physical S=37888, valid prefix=37807, H=56, D=128; non-causal, all-active BSA mask (dense semantics). Q/K/V/O communication is BF16, including Sage compute (QK INT8 / PV FP8).

| Native backend / per-rank head bands | Ordinary Ulysses (ms) | Whole QKV fused (ms) | Chunk serial (ms) | Chunk overlap (ms) | Ordinary / overlap | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 BSA / [7,7] | 42.89 | 43.53 | 44.18 | 36.91 | **1.162x** | **13.94%** |
| Sage BSA / [5,5,4] | 32.22 | 32.82 | 32.78 | 23.50 | **1.371x** | **27.06%** |

Both baseline and overlap use the **same corrected native kernel**. Timing covers input A2A + required layout/quantization + attention + output A2A, not a single CUDA kernel or model E2E. Setup/JIT/warmup is excluded. Each figure is the arithmetic mean of two independent runs' p50s; each run has 10 warmups and 40 max-rank CUDA-event samples per mode, with rotating mode order. Clocks were not locked. Torch 2.15.0.dev20260917+cu134, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.0, NCCL 2.30.7, driver 595.58.03.

**Correctness evidence:**

- New concurrent-copy regression: removing only the new fences causes BF16, FP16 and Sage to fail; restoring them makes all three pass (20 rounds, atol=rtol=0).
- U4 BF16 [7,7], Sage [5,5,4], and Sage [7,7]: 100 changed-input rounds each, with padding perturbation and output poisoning; max absolute difference versus same-backend ordinary is **0**.
- Single-GPU BF16/Sage stress: 100 rounds each, 1000 independent 64 MiB copies per round; bit-exact versus idle execution.
- Selected regression + existing native tests: **70 passed, 12 hardware-gated skipped, 1 performance sweep deselected**. The skips require SM90/SM100.
- Pre-fix BSA overlap timings that failed correctness are invalid and are not used as accepted speedups. This update does not claim FP8 wire support, model quality, model E2E, other card counts, or SM90/SM100/SM121 validation.

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/attention/test_bsa_sm120_concurrent_memory.py \
  tests/attention/test_vsa_block_sparse_sm120.py \
  tests/attention/test_vsa_block_sparse_sm120_sage.py \
  tests/experimental/ulysses/test_native_attention.py \
  -k 'not perf_sweep' -q

python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 \
  benchmarks/comm/bench_ulysses_native_attention.py \
  --attention sm120-bf16 --sequence 37888 --used 37807 \
  --heads 56 --schedule 7,7 --warmup 10 --iterations 40

python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 \
  benchmarks/comm/bench_ulysses_native_attention.py \
  --attention sm120-sage --sequence 37888 --used 37807 \
  --heads 56 --schedule 5,5,4 --warmup 10 --iterations 40
```

The new core-kernel regression is outside the `experimental-tests` fence and needs the normal SM120 attention test lane in addition to the declared experimental tests. The PR remains Draft.

title: fix: give concurrent streams disjoint row_states buffers in multi-CTA top-k
body:
## Description

Fixes #3618.

The multi-CTA radix top-k kernels keep histograms and inter-CTA barrier counters in `RadixRowState` scratch. The Python entry points previously obtained that scratch from device-keyed `_get_cache_buf` entries, so unsynchronized launches on different CUDA streams could share the same state and corrupt results or wedge the barrier.

The original PR covered seven producers. Current main subsequently added two supported `top_k_varlen` producers (`radix` and `radix_cutlass`), so this rebuild covers all nine current Python call sites.

## Fix

Allocate zero-initialized row-state scratch per call with `torch.zeros` instead of sharing a device cache entry. PyTorch's stream-ordered caching allocator gives concurrent live launches disjoint storage, reuses it after stream work completes, and handles CUDA graph capture without a custom ring or lifetime registry.

The `top_k_varlen` radix backend preserves its existing SM-count-based allocation size and `int32` view shape; the other eight paths retain their existing 1 MiB byte-buffer contract.

## Validation

Validated on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120, 96GB with CUDA 13:

- concurrent public API regressions: 5 passed (`top_k`, page-table transform, ragged transform, and both `top_k_varlen` backends)
- public-API pointer probe: distinct row-state allocations on two streams for both `top_k_varlen` backends
- focused sampling/logits selection: 1,104 passed, 123 skipped
- focused top-k/page-table/ragged selection: 163 passed
- exact-file pre-commit, compileall, and `git diff --check`: passed
- fresh independent outcome verification: confirmed

The earlier maintainer-triggered GPU pipeline `57443299` also succeeded on the previous converged per-call-allocation head. The current push only rebuilds that design on current main and extends it to the two newly landed producers.

## Disclosure

AI-assisted (Codex); reviewed and validated on real SM120 hardware by the submitter.

title: fix(jit): quote -ccbin host compiler path so it works with spaces
body:
## Description

On Windows, when `CC` points at a host compiler whose path contains spaces
(e.g. `C:\Program Files\...\cl.exe`), JIT compilation fails with:

```
nvcc fatal : A single input file is required for a non-link phase
```

**Root cause:** `build_cuda_cflags` appends the host compiler as a raw
`-ccbin <CC>` pair (`flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py`), and `join_multiline`
performs no quoting when it flattens the flag list into the `cuda_cflags`
ninja variable. The `cuda_compile` rule expands `$cuda_cflags` directly into
the command line, so the shell splits the unquoted path — nvcc then receives
`-ccbin C:\Program` plus `Files\...\cl.exe` as a stray second input file.

**Fix:** strip any surrounding single or double quotes already supplied by the user, then quote the value once — `["-ccbin", f'"{cc_env}"']`. This is shell-agnostic
(both `cmd.exe` and POSIX `sh` strip the outer quotes before nvcc sees the
argument) and a no-op for space-free paths, so existing behavior is unchanged.

**Scope:** limited to the reported `-ccbin` argument. The `cxx`, `nvcc`, and
`cuda_home` ninja variables share the same latent unquoted-path issue; I left
them untouched to keep this focused on the reported failure — happy to extend
if maintainers prefer a single broader pass.

## Related Issues

Fixes #3515.

## Tests

Added `test_ccbin_host_compiler_path_with_spaces_is_quoted` to
`tests/test_jit_cpp_ext.py` (GPU-free): generates the ninja build with bare, single-quoted, and double-quoted spaced `CC` values and asserts the `-ccbin` value is quoted exactly once. Verified it **fails on
the pre-fix code** (the bare path is emitted) and **passes with the fix**.

- `pytest tests/test_jit_cpp_ext.py` → 9 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py tests/test_jit_cpp_ext.py`
  → mypy / ruff-check / ruff-format all pass.

I don't have a Windows box; the fix is verified on Linux by inspecting the
generated `build.ninja` (a `CC` with spaces is now quoted), and the reporter
already confirmed a manually-quoted `-ccbin` path compiles.

---
AI-assisted (Claude).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed build argument generation for `-ccbin` so host compiler paths containing spaces are correctly quoted. Also ensures any user-supplied quotes are handled safely to avoid double-quoting.

* **Tests**

title: feat(topk_varlen): windowed (prefill) mode for gvr_2: row_starts, register-family routing (max_seq_len), absolute_indices (TRT-LLM #18702 port)
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds windowed (prefill) top-k to `top_k_varlen` for the gvr_2 backend, in three commits that together form the prefill API: `row_starts` (window mode, port of NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#18702), `max_seq_len` (register-family routing for windowed rows) and `absolute_indices` (fused absolute-column output). They were opened as three stacked PRs (#5304, #5307, #5310) and are consolidated here so the prefill path is reviewed as one unit; #5307 and #5310 are closed in favour of this PR.

**Stacked on #5288** (hint-free engines); the last three commits are new here, one per part below.

### Part 1: windowed mode via `row_starts` (commit `feat(topk_varlen): windowed (prefill) mode via row_starts`)

Row `r` ranks `logits[r, row_starts[r] : row_starts[r] + seq_lens[r]]` and returns window-local indices (`-1` padded, identity for windows shorter than K). This is the DSA prefill-indexer layout: every request's keys packed along the column axis, one query row per prompt token with a causal window into its own request's slice. Columns outside a row's window are never read. Until now the only FlashInfer path for that layout was the radix `top_k_ragged_transform(row_starts=)`.

#### What changed

- **Device**: `GvrMainKernel(prefill=True)` variant of the streaming `main` family. The window is read from a float4-aligned base (`ks & ~3`) with the `ks & 3` lead lanes masked in sampling, histogram, tail and emit, and indices shifted back by the lead, so the row base stays 16-byte aligned for any `ks`. ABI: the `pre_idx` slot carries `row_starts`, `seq_lens` keeps its per-row *length* meaning (upstream passes ks/ke), so callers never materialize row ends. Hint-free only; `next_n == 1`, `compress_ratio == 1`.
- **Host**: `run_varlen(..., row_starts=)` → `_launch_prefill`, one engine per (row-count tier, K, pow2 envelope bucket), rows slabbed at 32768. `warmup_prefill(top_k, max_cols)` compiles the set (≤ 6 engines per K) for CUDA-graph capture; the reference engine copies each window into an aligned `-inf`-padded row.
- **Main kernel, all varlen modes**: rows with `n <= K` now skip the body outright and go straight to the identity epilogue (block-uniform `short`). Upstream runs the body as a zero-work pass (every barrier and the sample scan still execute, ~1 µs per CTA on B200). In a causal prefill staircase the first K rows of every request are short, so this matters (25% of rows at L = 8192, K = 2048; all rows at L ≤ K). The diff of `gvr2_topk_decode.py` is large only because the body is re-indented one level; `git diff -w` shows the real change. Also, the hint-free identity bracket now samples from the first in-window lane (`base = lead`) instead of the float4-rounded row base, whose ≤ 3 lead lanes belong to the previous request; sampling them cost 50% on misaligned windows at K = 512.
- **API**: `row_starts` validated (contiguous 1-D int32 CUDA, one entry per row, no `pre_idx`, `next_n == 1`, `compress_ratio == 1`). Only gvr_2's checker admits it, so `auto` picks gvr_2 and an explicit other backend is refused at validation. The trace template gains the optional input with a window-aware reference/check.

#### Perf

SGLang-shaped staircase: R requests x L prompt tokens, causal windows, fp32, graph replay, 3 interleaved repetitions, min, every column on the same node in the same job. `radix_win` = `top_k_ragged_transform(row_starts=)` (FlashInfer today), `sgl_v2` = SGLang's default `topk_transform_ragged_v2`, `proxy` = the gvr_2 decode engine on a column-0 layout of identical per-row work (control column).

### Part 2: register-family routing via `max_seq_len` (commit `perf(topk_varlen): route windowed (prefill) rows to the register-resident gvr_2 family`)

Part 1's window engines existed only for the streaming `main` slab, so every prefill row ran the slab, while the decode router sends rows of the same length to the register-resident `reg` kernels, which are 1.6-2x faster on windows up to 4K tokens. SGLang's prefill top-k kernel picks its path per row by window length, which is exactly where it was still ahead of us.

#### What changed

- **Device**: `GvrTopkRegKernel(prefill=True)`. The row is read from the float4-rounded window base; the `ks & 3` lead lanes (thread 0's first float4) are excluded from the bracket fold, the identity hint positions, the histogram classify, the key-space escape and every emit by a 4-bit lane mask; indices are shifted to the window frame. A row whose scan extent exceeds the rung's register capacity (the caller's bound was violated) is reported as all `-1`, never as a truncated ranking. The slab engine is unchanged.
- **Host**: `_prefill_reg_route(rows, k, max_window)` — a per-part rung table measured on the causal staircase (rows 2K-32K, K ∈ {512, 2048}, bounds 2045/4093/8189, BLK/VPT/MINB menu, same node vs sglang topk_v2). B200 and B300 agree; Rubin differs: its slab is stronger at high row counts and the decode router's VPT=2/MINB=4 rung is register-starved there (the MINB=2 variant wins instead). `_reg_plan` mirrors `route()`'s register-band constants for an explicit rung.
- **API**: `top_k_varlen(..., row_starts=, max_seq_len=)` — the caller's bound on the window lengths (the longest prompt of the batch, host knowledge in every serving framework) selects the engine. Without it every row takes the slab, as in Part 1. A per-row split across two launches was built, measured and dropped: the slab launch that only skips rows still costs ~35 µs per 32K rows (one CTA per row at its smem occupancy), and without the bound the register launch must take the largest capacity class, the wrong kernel for short windows.

#### Perf

Causal staircase (R prompts x L tokens), fp32, graph replay, min of 3 interleaved repetitions, every column on the same node in the same job. `slab` = unhinted call (streaming engine, the Part 1 behaviour); `hinted` = `max_seq_len=L`; `sgl_v2` = SGLang's default `topk_transform_ragged_v2`; `upstream` = TRT-LLM #18702 `run_prefill`. Speedups are the other kernel's time over `hinted` (> 1 = we are faster). `fam` = engine the table picked. Rows with `L <= K` are identity rows and stay on the slab.

### Part 3: absolute-column output via `absolute_indices` (commit `feat(topk_varlen): absolute-column output for windowed top-k`)

Windowed (prefill) `top_k_varlen` returns **window-local** indices (`column - row_starts[r]`). The DSA prefill indexer's consumer wants the **absolute column** of the packed key axis, i.e. the flattened-KV slot: SGLang's `topk_transform_ragged_v2` produces exactly that by adding `out_offsets` inside its kernel, so a FlashInfer caller today has to run a separate offset-add over `num_rows x top_k` indices after every call (an extra launch on the critical path of every prefill layer; ~256 MB read-modify-write at 32K rows x K=2048).

This PR adds `top_k_varlen(..., row_starts=, absolute_indices=True)` and fuses that add into the index emit of **both** windowed gvr_2 engine families (streaming slab and register rungs):

- every emitted index already leaves the float4-rounded read frame through one subtraction (`- lead`); the absolute frame is the same single add with a different per-row constant (`+ col0`). No extra memory traffic, no extra launch, no extra register.
- `-1` pads untouched; identity (short) windows shifted; out-of-window columns never read; `return_values` gathers at the absolute columns.
- compile-time variant (`prefill_abs` in the compile keys, persist names `..._pf_abs`): the default path is byte-identical. The prefill launcher cache, `warmup_prefill(..., absolute_indices=)` and `prefill_ready(..., absolute_indices=)` key on it.
- decode mode refuses the flag with a `ValueError` (its indices are already columns of `logits`); non-bool values are refused.

Also fixes a `warmup_prefill` gap introduced with the register routing of Part 2: the register table admits every hint of the mid buckets, so the slab engine that an **unhinted** call of that width takes was never compiled by warmup (`prefill_ready` False right after warmup; capture would raise). Each bucket now also warms its slab tier at both promotion edges.

Part 1:
- Gate for the frame math: `test_prefill_packed_misaligned_ks` and `test_prefill_neginf_masks_in_window`. The +inf poison directly before a misaligned `ks` would become top-1 if any lead lane leaked; a missed `-lead` correction shows up as a negative index.
- `seq_lens` meaning under `row_starts` (window length, not end) is deliberate and documented in the API docstring; it keeps an SGLang-style adapter to two tensors it already has (`ks`, `ke - ks`).

Part 2:
- `max_seq_len` is deliberately a bound the caller vouches for, not something the host derives (that would need a device-to-host read of `seq_lens` and break CUDA-graph capture). Violations are loud (`-1` rows), never silent.

Part 3:
- The kernel diff is mechanical: in both engines every `idx - lead` emit became `idx + ofs` with `ofs = -lead` (local) or `+col0` (absolute).
