title: fix(mla): don't recommend backend='cutlass' on SM120/SM121 MLA fallback
body:
## Description

`BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper._maybe_warn_blackwell_auto_fallback` fires for all Blackwell GPUs (`major >= 10`) when `backend="auto"` falls back to a non-native MLA backend, and recommended `backend='cutlass'` as "the closest in-wrapper alternative".

But the in-wrapper cutlass MLA backend builds via `gen_mla_module(supported_major_versions=[10, 11])`, so on SM120/SM121 it raises at build time:

```
RuntimeError: No supported CUDA architectures found for major versions [10, 11].
```

So on consumer/workstation Blackwell the warning steered users toward a backend that cannot run. This makes the cutlass suggestion conditional on `major in (10, 11)`; SM120/SM121 now get only the working recommendation (`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`). SM100/SM110 text is unchanged.

## Related Issues

None — found while auditing SM120 MLA dispatch on an RTX PRO 6000.

## Tests

Verified on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, CUDA 13.0):

- `gen_mla_module().build_and_load()` → `RuntimeError: No supported CUDA architectures found for major versions [10, 11].` (cutlass MLA can't build on SM120).
- Warning text **before**: `... (Blackwell-native trtllm-gen); backend='cutlass' is the closest in-wrapper alternative ...`
- Warning text **after**: `... (Blackwell-native trtllm-gen).` (no cutlass suggestion on SM12x).

title: Recover SM107 (Rubin) test coverage lost to stale architecture gates
body:
## 📌 Description

Recovers test coverage on Rubin (SM107) that is skipped by architecture gates written before SM107 existed.

An audit of the nightly SM107 lane against GB300/GB200 found 442 test functions fully skipped on Rubin but running on both Blackwell SKUs. This PR addresses the subset where the gate is contradicted by something already in this repo — a sibling backend that lists 107, a library table the test ignores, an artifact pin that ships `sm_107a`, or a probe asking the wrong question. Gates that assert *validation* or *signoff* on SM107 are deliberately left alone and routed to their owners instead.

Measured against the 2026-09-17 nightly, the seven commits address **~8,400 skipped cases**:

| commit | change | cases |
|---|---|---|
| `test(mamba)` | probe the ptxas Triton actually uses | 761 |
| `fix(attention)` | drop stale NVFP4-KV and cute-dsl FMHA guards | 5,969 |
| `gemm` | add 107 to 11 backend lists that tests exercise | 1,030 |
| `test(moe,topk)` | align test-side arch sets with library tables | 607 |
| `test` | fix the `arch_blackwell` marker's description (docs-only) | — |
| `test(trace)` | admit SM107 in the reference-correctness gate | 10 |
| `gemm` | add 107 to the cuDNN batched BF16 list | — |

Each commit is independently revertable and stands on its own evidence:

**Stale guards.** `flashinfer/decode.py` and `flashinfer/prefill.py` raised `ValueError("KV Cache NVFP4 is not supported on SM107")`, mirrored by three test skips. The trtllm-gen FMHA pin in `flashinfer/artifacts.py` is `2d6a5a02…`, the pin that brought sm107a `KvE2m1` to parity — the claim has not been true since it landed. Likewise the cute-dsl FMHA prefill skips: `DSL_FMHA` is pinned at `6efb974a…` and `DSL_FMHA_ARCHS` lists `sm_107a` explicitly. The library raises are removed in the same commit as the skips on purpose; removing only the skips would turn a clean skip into a hard `ValueError`.

**Allowlist omissions.** Eleven `@supported_compute_capability` lists jump from 103 straight to 110, excluding Rubin while admitting newer architectures. The skip messages print the list back verbatim, e.g. `_check_grouped_mm_fp4 supports sm[100, 103, 110, 120, 121], got sm107`. The strongest evidence they are oversights is that the omission is inconsistent *within* the cuDNN backend — `_cudnn_gemm_fp4_requirement` and `_cudnn_bmm_fp8_requirement` already list 107 while `_cudnn_mm_bf16` and friends do not. One cuDNN cannot be four different pieces of hardware. Every deliberate 107 decision elsewhere in the tree carries a comment saying so; none of these does.

**The mamba probe.** `tests/mamba/conftest.py` blanket-skips the whole directory when Triton cannot target the device. The probe globbed the wheel's *bundled* ptxas and asked it for `sm_107a`, which can never succeed — Triton 3.8 bundles a CUDA 12.9 `ptxas` and a CUDA 13.3 `ptxas-blackwell`, neither containing `sm_107`. But Triton 3.8 does support SM107: it lowers LLVM/PTX as `sm_100` and assembles the raw arch through `get_ptxas(arch)`, which for `arch >= 100` reads `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH`. The probe now mirrors that resolution. It deliberately keeps the subprocess isolation and the fail-open default, because Triton's nvptxcompiler calls `abort()` on an arch it cannot target — that takes the whole pytest process down and cannot be caught at test time, so a wrong answer costs a CI shard rather than one red test.

## 🔍 Related Issues

<!-- none filed yet -->

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [ ] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> Partial, and worth stating precisely: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` were run at the pinned version (0.12.8) over all 17 changed files and pass. The full `pre-commit run --all-files` was **not** run — the dev box has no GPU and no torch, so the hooks that import the package cannot execute there.

## 🧪 Tests

- [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

> No tests are added: this PR removes and widens gates so that **existing** tests run on SM107, and the tests it unblocks are the verification.
>
> **Not yet validated on hardware.** The dev box has no GPU. The affected files should be run on an SM107 part (Hecate VR200 or a GR100 lab host) before merge. When they are, note that a widened gate can fail in three distinct ways and they mean different things:
> - an **import/build** error (traceback ends in `flashinfer/jit/`, ninja or nvcc; every test in the file fails identically) means no `sm_107a` artifact — revert, do not paper over it with a probe;
> - a **launch** failure (`no kernel image is available`; compiles then dies, and poisons the CUDA context so neighbours cascade) means the cubin is for a different arch;
> - a **numerical** mismatch (assertion in test code; neighbours unaffected) means the kernel ran and the question is tolerance — that is the only mode that should escalate rather than revert.
>
> Run with process isolation so a sticky CUDA failure cannot mask the classification.

## Reviewer Notes

Three things I would look at first:

1. **`test_unified_moe_fp8.py` is deliberately *not* widened**, and it looks like it should be. It hardcoded `((10, 0), (10, 3))`, and the obvious move is to defer to `_TRTLLM_ROUTED_ARCHS = (100, 103, 107)`. That would be wrong: the FP8 path has its own table, `_TRTLLM_ROUTED_FP8_ARCHS = (100, 103)`, carrying the comment "the FP8 kernels are validated on the SM100 family only". Test and library already agree and 107 is excluded on purpose. It is changed only to read that table rather than restate it, so the two cannot drift; behaviour is identical. Whether FP8 MoE is in fact validated on SM107 is a question for the MoE owners.

2. **The `trace` commit is the weakest and is last on purpose.** Its skip text says the tests are "only guaranteed to work on" SM100/SM103 — a statement about validation, not capability, and nothing in the repo contradicts it. If the Rubin run shows numerical mismatches there rather than passes, revert that commit and route the question rather than loosening a tolerance. The same applies to the bgmv `_SUPPORTED_SM` widening, whose original reason string was "not validated on SM107".

3. **Scope held back deliberately.** Seven cuTile `@supported_compute_capability` lists and `_tinygemm_mm_bf16_requirement` have the same 103→110 shape but no covering test, and cuTile is not installed in the Rubin CI image — widening them would be unverifiable either way, so they are left for a follow-up. A change to `_TRTLLM_GEN_ROUTING_SUPPORTED_CC` (whose own comment says the module is "compiled for SM 10.x and 12.x", and SM 10.7 is SM 10.x) is also held back for a separate reason: it trips an internal push-scanner rule, so it needs to be landed through a different route.

One implementation note for reviewers of the attention commit: it also deletes the now-unused `skip_if_nvfp4_kv_unsupported()` helper and its single call site. A stale caller there would have been a `NameError` at runtime rather than a syntax error, so the grep that caught it was deliberate rather than incidental.

title: feat(topk_varlen): gvr_2 decode: fused page-table output (page_table), decode latency floor, K=2048 clustered admission, two-CTA slab for unsplit rows
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Stacked on #5304 (prefill window mode); the last six commits are new here, one per part below. Decode-side work on the gvr_2 backend: the fused page-table output the DeepSeek-V4 decode integration asked for, the register-family latency-floor fixes found while measuring it, the K = 2048 admission to the clustered register family, the two-CTA-per-SM slab configuration for unsplit rows (these two close the decode cell classes that were behind SGLang), programmatic dependent launch for the slab and cluster families, and a staged coalesced epilogue for the clustered family's paged output. They were opened as two stacked PRs (#5312, #5315) and are consolidated here; #5315 is closed in favour of this PR.

### Part 1: fused page-table output via `page_table` / `page_size` (commit `feat(topk_varlen): fused page-table output for gvr_2 decode top-k`)

The DSA **decode** path needs the selected keys as **physical KV slots**, not as columns of the logits. SGLang's fused decode top-k (`topk_transform_512_v2`) takes the page table and emits `page_table[row, c // page_size] * page_size + c % page_size` directly; a FlashInfer `gvr_2` caller had to run a separate page-table transform over `num_rows x top_k` indices after every call. This is the output fusion Akhil asked for in the DeepSeek-V4 sync: it made the end-to-end comparison unfavourable even where the kernel itself was faster.

This PR adds `top_k_varlen(..., page_table=, page_size=)` (decode mode) and fuses the transform into the index emit of **all four** gvr_2 engine families (register, clustered-register, cluster, streaming slab):

- the hint-free compiles never read the `pre_idx` ABI slot, so the paged compiles carry the page table `[batch, max_pages]` in that slot and every valid emitted index leaves the kernel as a physical slot: one page-table read per selected index, no extra launch, no extra memory pass.
- `-1` pads untouched; the `next_n` rows of a request share the request's table row; columns and `page_size` are in logits units (compressed units under `compress_ratio=4`); the table must cover the logits width.
- compile-time variant per page size (`paged` + `page_shift` in the compile keys, persist names `..._pg{shift}`): the default compiles are byte-identical. `warmup_varlen(..., page_size=)` compiles the paged set for CUDA-graph capture; the `run_varlen` reference engine applies the same transform.
- not combinable with `return_values` (the raw indices are not kept), `row_starts` or `pre_idx`; the other backends refuse it (`auto` never routes it elsewhere).

Same mapping as `top_k_page_table_transform` (radix / clusters / CUB backends), now available on the gvr_2 engines with `top_k_varlen`'s `seq_lens` / `next_n` / `compress_ratio` semantics.

#### Perf

Fused paged output vs the window-local kernel alone, and vs the un-fused alternative a framework must run today (window-local kernel + a page-table transform pass); SGLang's fused `topk_transform_512_v2` where importable. fp32, CUDA graph, 3 interleaved reps, min; same node, one job. ### Part 2: decode latency floor: PDL launch, staged coalesced emit, early row load (commit `perf(topk_varlen): gvr_2 decode floor`)

Small-N decode top-k (rows ≤ 64, N ≤ 8K: the DSA decode shape) runs at a launch-and-latency floor of 3-5 us, and there SGLang's `topk_v2` was 5-27% faster than `gvr_2` (worst: K=2048, N=4096 at 0.73x). Profiling with Nsight Compute and CUPTI split that gap into two parts: about 0.4 us of launch overlap (SGLang launches with programmatic dependent launch, so consecutive kernels overlap in a graph) and a kernel-body gap dominated by scoreboard stalls. Three changes to the **register family** close it:

1. **Programmatic dependent launch** for the decode register families (`_DECODE_PDL`). The kernels already `griddepcontrol.wait` before their first read; passing the launch attribute lets the next kernel's launch processing overlap this kernel's tail, in a CUDA graph and in a serving stream alike. ~0.4 us on every decode cell.
2. **Staged coalesced output.** The per-bin-cursor emit writes each index to a position scattered across the row within a warp, so every emitted index cost one L1 store sector (5x the sectors of a coalesced write, ~1 us at k=2048). The k outputs are now staged in a k-word shared-memory region at the tail of the register kernel's dynamic window (all emit paths write raw indices there; unwritten slots surface as -1) and written to global in one coalesced pass after a barrier, which also applies the prefill / paged output transform. The host enables it for one-wave launches only (rows ≤ SM count, the latency-bound regime): several waves deep, the extra barrier + copy measured 3-4% slower than the scattered stores, so multi-wave launches and the prefill slabs keep the direct emit (compile-time `stage_out`). The existing warp-ballot emit arm was measured as the alternative and is slower on every cell.
3. **Early envelope-bounded row load** (decode). The float4 register batch is loaded at kernel start bounded by the launch envelope (≤ the row width, memory-safe) instead of after the per-row `kv_lens` read, so the two global latencies overlap; lanes beyond the row's own length are -inf-filled in the body. Prefill keeps its in-body load (its base depends on the `row_starts` read).

No API change. The register families' compile keys gain the `pdl` and `stage_out` flags; launch shared memory grows by `4 * k` bytes for the staging region on one-wave launches only.

Against SGLang's `topk_v2` on Rubin the register family is now at or above parity on every cell but one (K=1024, rows=1, N=8192 at 0.90x); the remaining losses are the few-row K=2048 cells at N >= 32K, which the router sends to the streaming slab (0.44-0.63x) - a routing/coverage item, not touched here.

### Part 3: K = 2048 admitted to the clustered register family (commit `perf(topk_varlen): admit K=2048 to the gvr_2 clustered register family`)

Few-row decode top-k at K = 2048 and N in (16K, 64K] ran on the streaming slab: the clustered register-resident family (2-8 CTAs of 1024 threads holding the row in registers, one DSMEM histogram merge) was gated at `k <= 1024` like upstream. The gate exists because the family's hint sample is one word per thread; every selection stage after it (merged scan, cursor emit, crossing-bin tie select over the striped DSMEM slabs, key-space fallback) is k-generic. This was the last decode cell class clearly behind SGLang's `topk_v2` (0.44-0.63x on Rubin at 1-64 rows, N = 32K, in the Part 2 tables).

- `route()`: the clustered family admits `k <= 2 * BLKC`. For K > BLKC the bracket comes from the first BLKC row values instead of the first k (a looser bracket, the same exact result). Above 32K the K > BLKC admission also requires the cluster grid to fit one GPC wave, `b * cs <= 7/8 of the SM count`: on B200/B300 (148 SMs) 32 rows x 4-CTA clusters are admitted and 37 x 4 are not (that band spills into a second wave, 0.89x of the slab at 37 x 48K); on Rubin (208 SMs) 37-44 x 4 are admitted (2.1-2.3x vs the slab) and 52 x 4 are not (1.2-1.35x there, left on the slab).
- `GvrRegClusKernel`: the short-row identity write (rows with n <= k) strides over k instead of assuming k <= BLK. No other kernel change.

### Part 4: unsplit slab rows at 75-148 take the two-CTA-per-SM configuration (commit `perf(topk_varlen): gvr_2 unsplit slab rows at 75-148 take the two-CTA-per-SM configuration`)

The streaming slab has two configurations: the "big" one for grids that fit one wave (`b * R <= 148`: 1024-thread CTAs, one per SM, sample caps SCAP 16384 / CMP 4096) and the b > 148 one ((512, U 8, MINB 2): 512 threads, two CTAs per SM, the smaller caps). Upstream picks by the wave test alone. For an unsplit row (R = 1, one CTA per row) in the 75-148 row band that is the wrong choice: at 32K-64K columns the 1024-thread slab costs 15-19 us on B200 for K in {512, 1024, 2048} while the same rows at b = 256, already on the b > 148 configuration, cost 7-14 us. Forcing the U = 8 unroll on the 1024-thread kernel changed nothing and the 512-thread shape ran the same with either set of host sample constants, so it is the CTA shape with its BLK-derived caps.

- `_big_regime(b, R, n4)`, one helper for `route` / `route_dynamic` / `route_streaming` / the varlen launcher: upstream's `b * R <= 148`, except unsplit rows with 75 <= b <= 148 and n <= 64K, which take the b > 148 configuration. The bounds are measured: 33-74 unsplit rows (only K = 2048 reaches the slab there, above 32K) lose at 64K (0.75x at 37 rows) and rows above 64K are mixed to bad (0.5x at 75-148 rows x 256K), so both keep upstream's regime, as do the split slab (R > 1) and b > 148. `route_dynamic` reads the regime off the static plan (1024-thread CTAs <=> big): the 64K bound is a band boundary of the static plan, not a per-row quantity.
- Affected cells: K <= 1024 at 75-148 rows, 32K-64K (below 75 rows the clustered register family takes them); K = 2048 at 75-148 rows, 20K-64K where Part 3's one-wave gate leaves them on the slab. Everything else is an identical launch.

### Part 5: programmatic dependent launch for the slab and cluster families (commit `perf(topk_varlen): programmatic dependent launch for the gvr_2 slab and cluster families`)

Part 2 gave the register families a programmatic dependent launch (`griddepcontrol.wait` as the first instruction, the launch attribute on the kernel) so a following kernel's launch processing overlaps the tail of the previous one; the streaming slab (`GvrMainKernel`) and the cluster split (`GvrClusKernel`) still launched without it. This adds the same `pdl` compile flag (part of the compile key and persist name, default off) to both and passes it from the varlen launcher, so every decode engine launches the same way. The wait precedes every global read (including the split slab's workspace) and no kernel triggers early, so ordering is exactly the stream order; only the launch latency overlaps. Prefill launches are unchanged.

### Part 6: staged coalesced epilogue for the clustered family's paged output (commit `perf(topk_varlen): staged coalesced epilogue for the gvr_2 clustered family's paged output`)

The clustered register family still emitted its paged output the way the register family did before Part 2: every winner as one scattered global store with the page-table transform inline (one L1 store sector per index, the table read on the emit path), 0.3-0.8 us over the unpaged kernel on the clustered cells.

- `stage_out` for `GvrRegClusKernel`: every rank writes its winners into a k-word staging region at the tail of rank 0's dynamic window (DSMEM stores through mapa; rank 0 clears it before the first cluster rendezvous), and after the final rendezvous rank 0 alone writes the row in one coalesced pass, applying the page transform there. The staged variant reads the page table from global in that epilogue instead of staging the table row in the prologue: concentrated at the tail the reads hit L2 and the prologue stage is pure overhead (0.1-0.3 us better than the smem row on every clustered cell).
- Host rule, measured on B200: paged output only, K <= 1024 at every row count and K = 2048 from 16 rows up. K = 2048 below 16 rows keeps the scattered emit (the two-pass epilogue over 2048 words costs more than it saves, -0.3 us at 1 x 32K); the unpaged output keeps it too (funnelling every rank's winners through rank 0 lost 0.3-0.8 us at 16-64 rows without a transform to amortise). Compile key and persist name gain `stage_out`; launch smem grows by 4k when staged.

Part 2:
- Occupancy: the staging region adds `4k` bytes (≤ 8 KB) per CTA; the register rungs stay at their MINB occupancy on B200/B300/Rubin (e.g. (512, VPT 1, MINB 4): ~29 KB x 4 CTAs).
- PDL correctness: the wait is the first instruction of the kernel (before the early row load and the `kv_lens` read), so no input produced by the preceding kernel is read early; outputs are written after the wait only.

title: perf(topk_varlen, attn_scores): upstream sync — gvr_2 hint-free engines (TRT-LLM #18410) + paged-MQA relu epilogue (DKG !27837)
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md kept; sections filled -->
## 📌 Description

Upstream sync of two kernel families FlashInfer vendors from NVIDIA sources, with every change measured same-node against the current tree before adoption (and two upstream heuristics rejected on measurement).

**1. Paged-MQA logits (`attn_scores`, fp8 + fp4 decode kernels) — DKG MR !27837 + d9adb3cfa77**
`relu(x) = (x + |x|) / 2` in the fp32 epilogue: two packed `FADD2` replace four scalar `max`. Bit-exact with the previous output. fp8 folds the /2 into the existing scale multiply; fp4 halves the register-resident fp32 weights once per q stage (upstream's per-output multiply form was 6-9% *slower* on B200; a four-tree bisect isolated it, see commit message). `tmem.free` receives the static column count.

**2. GVR V2 top-k (`top_k_varlen` backend `gvr_2`) — TRT-LLM #18410 `hint_free` + router follow-up**
- Hint-free calls run dedicated compiled engines (hint loads compiled out). The FlashInfer-local anchor table (`arange(k)` per (device, k), growth lock, keep-list, its share of `release_gvr2_resources`) is removed. Contract change: hint mode is a warm-up dimension for CUDA graphs (`warmup_varlen` compiles both; a hinted eager call no longer warms a hint-free capture — the capture raises the usual error).
- Per-family bracket policy, each choice measured (Rubin/B200, 3 interleaved reps, same-kernel control column): identity gather for main/clus and register VPT>=2, register fold only at VPT==1, DEG plans share one compiled object. Upstream's fold-for-every-VPT (2-14% slower on 43/90 cells) and compile-out semantics (4-6% slower) were not adopted.
- Router: the 4K<n<=8K register rung now also covers K=2048 up to 1024 rows — 15-39% faster than the slab on B200, 148-SM B300 **and** Rubin (upstream's SM103-only exception holds on SM100/SM107 too). The same extension for K<=1024 wins on mixed lengths but loses 5-26% on uniform full-length rows, so it was not taken.
- `auto`: `N <= top_k` (every row is the identity answer) prefers `radix_filter` (0.85 vs 1.1 us, both parts).
- Not adopted: `QC = QUADC` for every register plan (a wash within ~6% on Rubin and 148-SM B300), TRT-LLM #18702 prefill window mode (separate decision).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follows #4986 / #4811 (gvr_2). DKG #61 (router rungs) gets a follow-up note with the K=2048 finding.

title: fix(gdn): fence TMEM loads before cg1 shared_acc releases
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5334.

In the Blackwell GDN chunked kernel (`compute_group_1_chunk`), two `cg1_shared_acc` consumer releases signaled the producer that the TMEM stage was free while `tcgen05.ld` (`LDTM`) into that stage was still in flight. With `tmem_cg1_shared_acc_stages = 1`, the producer's next `tcgen05.mma` can overwrite cells mid-read.

This PR adds `cute.arch.fence_view_async_tmem_load()` immediately before:

1. `ks_handle.release()` (after the KS t2r + scale)
2. `nv_handle.release()` (after the NV t2r + cast loop)

These match the existing cg0 idiom at `kk0_handle` / `kk1_handle` (and QK epilogue) releases, so the following `SYNCS.ARRIVE` inherits the LDTM scoreboard wait mask.

### Changed vs preserved

| Site | Action |
|------|--------|
| `ks_handle.release` | **changed**: add load fence |
| `nv_handle.release` | **changed**: add load fence |
| `qs_handle.release` | **preserved**: intervening reg consumer + `fence_view_async_tmem_store` already drains LDTM |
| `o_qs_handle.release` | **preserved**: same class of lookalike; leave alone |
| cg0 `kk*` / `qk*` fences | **preserved**: already correct |

### Related

Possibly related to the nondeterministic NaN signature in #4704 (garbage into `v - k·s` / NV inputs is consistent with that class of failure), but this PR does **not** claim to fix #4704 or the production hang. Linkage remains speculative; the hang is non-completion, while this race predicts corruption.

## Diff

Two lines only in `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/blackwell/gated_delta_net_chunked.py`.

## Verification

No Blackwell GPU or CUDA `nvdisasm` toolchain on the machine used for this PR, so SASS control-bit re-check was not re-run here.

Verified instead:

- Against `main` @ `d7bfcab6091da2e1d98c1b26b46d8e613389c2e1` (same HEAD cited in #5334).
- Source parity with cg0: fences sit immediately before release after all t2r into the stage for that handoff (cg0 lines 3081/3109).
- Diff is exactly the two `fence_view_async_tmem_load()` insertions; `qs` / `o_qs` untouched.
- Issue #5334 already documents baseline FAIL / +fence PASS / revert FAIL via `nvdisasm -c -g -hex` on both reconstruction and the production binary (unordered ARRIVE wait masks at the two sites).

Suggested follow-up for a Blackwell/CUDA host: re-run the issue's compile+nvdisasm control-bit check and confirm those two ARRIVEs go from `wait=000000` to a non-zero LDTM wait mask.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reviewers with SM100/SM103: compile GDN chunked specialization and `nvdisasm -c -g -hex`; assert no `SYNCS.ARRIVE` releasing `cg1_shared_acc` leaves an `LDTM` scoreboard live
- [ ] Optional B200/B300 sanity (not a proof): existing GDN chunked correctness paths still pass

title: feat(cudnn): decode backend forwards q_len_per_req > 1, sliding window and attention sinks
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn")` (#4625) served one-token, full-window, sink-free decode only, so the wrapper rejected exactly the variants the popular decode models need: multi-token verification rows (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next MTP, GLM-4.5 MTP), a left sliding window and learned attention sinks (gpt-oss). cuDNN accepts all three on the same paged SDPA graph; this PR forwards them.

`flashinfer.cudnn.decode.cudnn_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` gains three keyword arguments:

- **`q_len_per_req`** (default 1): `q` has `batch * q_len_per_req` consecutive rows per request. The graph sees a `(batch, heads, q_len, d)` strided view (no copy) and applies the **bottom-right causal diagonal** (row `i` of a request with `kv_len` keys sees keys `0 .. kv_len - q_len + i`). `O` / `Stats` are bound token-major, so `out` is `(rows, heads, d_vo)` and `lse` `(rows, heads)` — the wrapper's shapes.
- **`window_left`** (default -1): FlashInfer counts the keys *before* the diagonal position (the position itself is always visible); cuDNN's `diagonal_band_left_bound` counts the diagonal too, so the graph gets `window_left + 1` under bottom-right alignment. (An off-by-one on either side shows against fa2 at windows 64 / 128 — tested.)
- **`sinks`** (default None): `(num_heads_qo,)` fp32 logits bound as a `(1, H, 1, 1)` `sink_token`: one extra softmax column with a zero value row, **unscaled** — FlashInfer's contract. Probe on B200: cuDNN matches the torch reference to 8e-3 with the unscaled sink; `sink * scale`, `sink * log2e`, `sink / log2e` are off by 0.5–2, so the convention is pinned by test. Whether a stack serves a sink at `q_len_per_req == 1` is decided by cuDNN's SDPA engines: the backend engine raises a not-supported error at graph build (test skips with the reason), cudnn-frontend 1.30+ with the FROST engines enabled serves it (every sink case passes on that stack, see Tests).

The graph-cache key (`_sdpa_decode_key_fn`) carries `q_len_per_req`, `window_left` and the sink tensor's layout, so same-shape calls that differ only in them do not share a graph.

`BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn")`: the `q_len_per_req > 1`, `window_left` and `sinks` rejections are gone; the generic multi-token checks know the cudnn path (it needs no tensor-core module) and the cudnn path enforces `q_len_per_req` equal to the planned value like the fa2 path. `benchmarks/routines/attention.py` no longer drops the cudnn wrapper backend for `--s_qo > 1` with the causal draft mask (the standalone `cudnn-native` stays one-row; `--spec_dec_mask` other than `causal` still skips cudnn, whose graph applies the bottom-right causal diagonal and takes no draft-block mask) and plans the wrappers with `q_len_per_req=s_qo`. The `cudnn_batch_decode` trace template gains the three optional inputs, a reference that honors them, and a decode-specific `num_q_rows` axis for `q` / `output` (`batch_size * q_len_per_req` rows) while `block_tables` keeps `batch_size`; the shared paged axis map is untouched. `docs/api/cudnn.rst` and the wrapper docstring updated.

**Not changed: `backend="auto"`.** On B200 cuDNN measures 3–4× ahead of the CUDA-core fa2 kernel `auto` resolves to for a default wrapper (64/8 heads, d128, page 16, 4k KV: 28 vs 96 µs at b=8, 91 vs 369 µs at b=32, 316 vs 1419 µs at b=128) and at parity with fa2 tensor cores (91 vs 94 µs at b=32, 316 vs 438 µs at b=128). It still should not pick cudnn: `auto` is resolved at `plan()` before `run()` sees `sinks`, and the backend engine cannot take a sink at `q_len_per_req == 1`, so `auto → cudnn` would turn gpt-oss-style callers on Blackwell into a hard error at the first run. That needs a sink-aware plan (or the FROST stack everywhere) first.

Observation for a follow-up (not fixed here): the plain fa2 tensor-core decode wrapper accepts `sinks=` at `run()` and silently ignores them unless the module was built with the `AttentionSink` JIT variant (`jit_args`) or via `BatchAttentionWithAttentionSinkWrapper` — its output equals the no-sink result to 8e-3 in the probe. That is why the sink tests here compare against the torch reference, not fa2.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follows #4625 (backend="cudnn" for the decode wrapper) and #4626. cuDNN-side coverage for these decode variants: cudnn-frontend #1094 (d128 decode tile), #1095 (sink at S_q == 1), #1109 (d256 decode tile).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. (`ruff@0.12.8 format` / `check` on every touched Python file: clean.)

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

`tests/attention/test_cudnn_decode.py` (B200, cuDNN backend 9.26.0.51, torch 2.14 nightly cu132):

- `test_cudnn_wrapper_mtp_matches_fa2[q_len 2 / 4 × fp16 / bf16 × HND / NHD]` — output + base-2 LSE vs fa2 tensor-core decode, row for row.
- `test_cudnn_wrapper_sliding_window_matches_fa2[window 64 / 128 × q_len 1 / 2]` — vs fa2.
- `test_cudnn_wrapper_sinks_match_reference[(32/8 d128, 64/8 d64) × window -1 / 128 × q_len 1 / 2]` — vs the torch reference (`_decode_ref` gained `q_len_per_req` / `window_left` / `sinks`, LSE includes the sink); also asserts the sink changed the output. title: feat(vibecuda_kda): add SM100/SM103 recurrent KDA prefill backend
body:
## Description

This PR adds a recurrent Kimi Delta Attention prefill backend generated by VibeCUDA, named `vibecuda`, for NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`) and NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (`sm_103a`). At commit [`a0858ca1`](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/commit/a0858ca17085e3d4c047babf344175ea22ce960b), the measurements achieve **6.2605x arithmetic / 2.6834x geometric mean speedup on NVIDIA GB200** and **6.1462x arithmetic / 2.6487x geometric mean on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC**, over CAKE across all 16 measured workloads on each GPU. Workloads come from [PR #4262](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4262), [PR #4571](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4571), and the H12 workloads in [PR #4445](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4445). The denominator is the CAKE backend at pinned pre-PR-4535 commit [`ee3fda10`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ee3fda10e0b9d82b71bda534bc2954d3176e6ded). **Minimum speedups are 0.9431x on GB200 and 0.9630x on B300; four shapes on each GPU remain slower than CAKE.** Repository correctness tests pass on both GPUs. Automatic backend selection remains unchanged.

The change includes generated kernels, architecture-specific bindings, JIT/AOT registration, public API and dispatch integration, numerical and CUDA Graph tests, and the canonical repository benchmark. The current head includes the FlashInfer `main` merge, corrected JIT cache-key tests, and benchmark compatibility with the pinned CAKE public API.

### Public contract and dispatch

* `recurrent_kda(..., backend="vibecuda")` selects the backend explicitly.
* The backend accepts BF16 prefill with 128-dimensional QK/VO heads, fixed or packed sequences, contiguous beta and recurrent state, optional caller-owned output, and optional final-state output.
* Dispatch selects architecture-specific M64, M128, split-sequence, slab, or persistent generated kernels according to the validated workload contract.
* Unsupported contracts, state pools, checkpoints, speculative decode, and unsupported architectures fail explicitly without falling back.
* CUDA Graph capture uses an explicit `RecurrentKDAPrefillWorkspace`, warmed eagerly with stable tensor addresses. Fixed and packed replay are covered by repository tests.

### Architecture and provenance

* Exact targets: `sm_100a` on NVIDIA GB200 and `sm_103a` on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC.
* CAKE tracker: [FlashInfer issue #4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254).
* Workload sources: six fixed/packed rows from [PR #4262](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4262), four fixed-layout small-BH rows from [PR #4571](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4571), and six H12 rows from [PR #4445](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4445).
* The measured denominator is the CAKE backend at pinned pre-PR-4535 FlashInfer commit [`ee3fda10e0b9d82b71bda534bc2954d3176e6ded`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ee3fda10e0b9d82b71bda534bc2954d3176e6ded). PR #4535 workloads are covered by a separate combined prefill/decode effort and are not included in these results.

## Validation

The candidate and CAKE baseline use identical deterministic inputs, preinitialized rotating state slots, public recurrent-KDA semantics, and output plus in-place recurrent-state validation. Timing uses CUPTI activity records with cold L2 before every timed iteration. Allocation, JIT, metadata construction, sequence ordering, and state-pool reset are outside the timed region.

* Current head `a0858ca1`: **344 passed, 1 skipped on NVIDIA GB200; 345 passed on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC** across `tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_prefill.py`, `tests/jit/test_flash_kda_prefill_jit.py`, and `tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_prefill_benchmark.py`. This includes candidate checks against the mathematical precision reference, in-place state mutation, workspace allocation, streams, and CUDA Graph replay.
* All **16/16 latency measurements completed on each GPU** for both implementations. These latency runs are separate from the precision test suite, not an additional per-row precision-pass claim.
* The complete `pre-commit run --all-files` suite passes.

## Performance

NVIDIA GB200, candidate commit `a0858ca1`, CAKE commit `ee3fda10`: CUPTI, cold L2, five warmup iterations, ten measured samples, no CUDA Graph replay in these latency measurements. Each speedup is CAKE median latency divided by candidate median latency; both means include every measured shape.

| GPU | Workload source | Shapes | Arithmetic mean | Geometric mean | Minimum |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`) | PR #4262 fixed/packed rows | 6/6 | 1.0001x | 0.9985x | 0.9431x |
| NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`) | PR #4571 long-context rows | 4/4 | 19.2998x | 14.3276x | 4.8920x |
| NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`) | PR #4445 H12 rows | 6/6 | 2.8282x | 2.3608x | 1.0504x |
| **NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`)** | **Combined** | **16/16** | **6.2605x** | **2.6834x** | **0.9431x** |

**Remaining GB200 regressions:**

| Shape | CAKE (us) | VibeCUDA (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| h96_mixed | 356.352 | 365.698 | 0.9744x |
| h96_uniform | 386.048 | 406.563 | 0.9495x |
| h64_mixed | 244.864 | 250.449 | 0.9777x |
| h64_uniform | 261.584 | 277.375 | 0.9431x |

### B300 measurements

NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, candidate commit `a0858ca1`, CAKE commit `ee3fda10`, using the same CUPTI, cold-L2, five-warmup/ten-sample protocol above.

| GPU | Workload source | Shapes | Arithmetic mean | Geometric mean | Minimum |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (`sm_103a`) | PR #4262 fixed/packed rows | 6/6 | 1.0114x | 1.0105x | 0.9630x |
| NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (`sm_103a`) | PR #4571 long-context rows | 4/4 | 19.0338x | 14.1194x | 4.8203x |
| NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (`sm_103a`) | PR #4445 H12 rows | 6/6 | 2.6892x | 2.2752x | 0.9942x |
| **NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (`sm_103a`)** | **Combined** | **16/16** | **6.1462x** | **2.6487x** | **0.9630x** |

**Remaining B300 regressions:**

| Shape | CAKE (us) | VibeCUDA (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| h96_mixed | 372.950 | 380.661 | 0.9797x |
| h64_mixed | 258.947 | 268.883 | 0.9630x |
| h64_uniform | 281.971 | 286.723 | 0.9834x |
| h12_packed_128x8 | 38.289 | 38.512 | 0.9942x |

## Reviewer commands

Run these commands at candidate commit `a0858ca1`. The
single-backend benchmark invocation reports candidate latencies; it does not by
itself reproduce the pinned-CAKE speedup table.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_prefill.py -q
python -m pytest tests/jit/test_flash_kda_prefill_jit.py -q
python -m pytest tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_prefill_benchmark.py -q
python benchmarks/bench_recurrent_kda_prefill.py \
  --case-set all --backend vibecuda \
  --dry-run-iters 5 --repeat-iters 10 \
  --json /tmp/kda-prefill.json
python benchmarks/bench_recurrent_kda_prefill.py \
  --case-set h12 --backend vibecuda \
  --dry-run-iters 5 --repeat-iters 10 \
  --json /tmp/kda-prefill-h12.json
```

## References

* [Benchmark](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/a0858ca17085e3d4c047babf344175ea22ce960b/benchmarks/bench_recurrent_kda_prefill.py)
* [Public API and dispatch](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/a0858ca17085e3d4c047babf344175ea22ce960b/flashinfer/kda.py)
* [Backend implementation](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/a0858ca17085e3d4c047babf344175ea22ce960b/flashinfer/kda_vibecuda.py)
* [Primary tests](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/a0858ca17085e3d4c047babf344175ea22ce960b/tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_prefill.py)

## Pull Request Checklist

* [x] Kernel sources and full public dispatch path are included.
* [x] Public API and exact architecture guards are tested.
* [x] Candidate and baseline use identical inputs and timing semantics.
* [x] CUDA Graph capture and replay are tested.
* [x] Unsupported contracts fail explicitly.
* [x] Retained performance evidence covers NVIDIA GB200 and NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC.
* [x] Repository correctness suites and matched-baseline latency measurements completed on current head `a0858ca1` on both GPU models.

title: feat: integrate TRTLLM-Gen sliding-window FMHA
body:
## 📌 Description

Integrates the TRTLLM-Gen sliding-window FMHA metadata and runtime contract into
FlashInfer.

This change:

- adds fixed left/right window propagation for the direct TRTLLM-Gen context API;
- adds per-query-token inclusive `VariableWindow` start/end bounds;
- updates paged and ragged launcher parameter plumbing and trace schemas;
- selects and hashes the new mask metadata without silently rewriting the caller's mask;
- centralizes C++ validation for causal, non-causal, fixed-window, variable-window,
  and chunked-attention combinations;
- preserves compatibility with generated metadata headers that spell the
  FP16-softmax/Spcompress slots either semantically or as `mReserved1/mReserved2`;
- adds Python validation and regression coverage for unsupported or malformed
  configurations; and
- preserves existing dense, causal, MLA-generation, and chunked-attention behavior.

The public wrapper continues to reject non-causal sliding-window attention for
the TRTLLM-Gen paged backend. The direct context API supports explicit
two-sided non-causal windows. `VariableWindow` requires an inclusive start/end
pair for every packed query token.

### Artifact dependency

This PR intentionally remains a draft until the corresponding FMHA artifact is
published to FlashInfer's public kernel repository. Until then,
`ArtifactPath.TRTLLM_GEN_FMHA` and `CheckSumHash.TRTLLM_GEN_FMHA` still point to
the legacy ABI and this branch must not be merged.

- The ABI-matched candidate has passed correctness and stability validation.

title: feat(vibecuda_mamba): add SM100/SM103 SSDCombined backend
body:
## Description

This PR adds an SSDCombined Mamba backend generated by VibeCUDA. On NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103), it achieves **2.363742x arithmetic-mean and 2.228626x geometric-mean speedup** over the optimized CAKE SSDCombined backend from [PR 4576](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4576) across 12/12 precision-passing public route-matrix workloads. The backend uses hand-written CUDA with asynchronous staging and tensor-core accumulation behind the existing `SSDCombined` public API.

### Public contract

- `SSDCombined(..., backend="vibecuda").run(...)` supports batched and packed-variable-length execution, optional D/z, initial states, sequence metadata, caller-owned output, optional final states, and selective checkpoint-state outputs.
- Geometry is `chunk_size=128`, `headdim=64`, and `dstate=128`; IO is BF16 and state storage is BF16 or FP16. Head counts must be positive and divisible by the group count.
- Dense-inner contiguous tensors and dense-inner gap-strided serving views are supported. Unsupported devices, shapes, dtypes, and metadata combinations fail before launch.
- CUDA Graph support is not claimed.

### Architecture and source provenance

- Performance in this description was measured on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103). The implementation also contains SM100 dispatch, but this revision makes no current-head SM100 performance claim.
- Target base commit: `971b0a6b9563be2af10048ce33dffe0d4bce6c8a`.
- CAKE baseline: [PR 4576](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4576) head `edc312de23f81e8ca38cc0e05be87c654c4b438c`, squash merge `624fce191f36ec143b32189ed01d14afb75c4594`.
- Measured repository commit: `d50d516364304046aa939c6b36bda5ec460f6bda`.
- Ordered SHA-256 of `csrc/vibecuda_mamba_ssd_combined.cu`, `csrc/vibecuda_mamba_ssd_combined_jit_binding.cu`, then `include/flashinfer/mamba/vibecuda_ssd_combined.cuh` (146,409 bytes): `2bd7930fca2ae460fec51865cdce09611dadd6435bec5e86c2fa08cb086e6b2a`.
- CAKE source catalog SHA-256: `ededb992d61b316eaa6f1d406c03d3f43ce1df4c3a82ef2161aa034794f4f5c6`; catalog source-archive SHA-256: `488aa69395f4c8f847a08920447e144e232d4b01df0503dd42be3b60d2aafb2c`.
- Measured toolchain: CUDA 13.2, Torch 2.12.0, Triton 3.7.0, CUPTI Python 13.3.0.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed on the measured commit.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/mamba/test_vibecuda_ssd_combined.py tests/mamba/test_vibecuda_ssd_contracts.py`: **30 passed** on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC.
- The repository benchmark reports **12/12 candidate rows passing** CuTe parity for output and final state at `atol=rtol=0.01`, plus NaN-sentinel full-write validation.
- The independent FP64 recurrence remains diagnostic. The candidate maximum error is no larger than CAKE's on every row; the zero-initial packed H=128/G=8 output exceeds the diagnostic `0.06/0.06` tolerance for both implementations.

## Performance

Protocol: CUPTI GPU-kernel activity, cold L2, eager execution without CUDA Graph, 5 dry runs and 100 measured repetitions, median per workload. Runners are constructed and warmed before measurement and caller output is preallocated. Host allocations inside `SSDCombined.run` are excluded by CUPTI's GPU-activity timing. Candidate and CAKE use identical inputs and call boundaries.

| Workload | CAKE | VibeCUDA | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 batched, H=8/G=8, vector D | 49.601 us | 19.744 us | 2.512x |
| FP16 packed, int64 sequence index, H=8/G=8 | 78.625 us | 37.249 us | 2.111x |
| BF16 preprocessing, batched H=8/G=8 | 104.113 us | 19.536 us | 5.329x |
| Packed H=128/G=8, zero initial state | 110.705 us | 82.865 us | 1.336x |

- **Arithmetic mean:** 2.363742x
- **Geometric mean:** 2.228626x
- **Minimum / maximum:** 1.335968x on packed H=128/G=8 with zero initial state / 5.329153x on BF16 preprocessing with H=8/G=8.
- Coverage and aggregates apply only to the 12 public PR-4576 route-matrix rows. No speed-floor claim is made for workloads outside that matrix.

### Direct verification commands

Run in a Python 3.11 environment with CUDA 13.2, Torch 2.12.0, `virtualenv`, `pytest`, and `pre-commit` available:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git
cd flashinfer
git fetch https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer.git feat/vibecuda-mamba-ssd-combined
git checkout --detach d50d516364304046aa939c6b36bda5ec460f6bda
export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH
virtualenv --system-site-packages .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps --ignore-installed triton==3.7.0
pre-commit run --all-files
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/mamba/test_vibecuda_ssd_combined.py tests/mamba/test_vibecuda_ssd_contracts.py
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/bench_cake_mamba_ssd_combined_matrix.py --fresh
```

## References

- [CAKE SSDCombined PR 4576](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4576) at `edc312de23f81e8ca38cc0e05be87c654c4b438c`
- [Pinned CAKE benchmark](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/edc312de23f81e8ca38cc0e05be87c654c4b438c/benchmarks/bench_cake_mamba_ssd_combined.py)
- [Repository matrix benchmark at the measured commit](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/d50d516364304046aa939c6b36bda5ec460f6bda/benchmarks/bench_cake_mamba_ssd_combined_matrix.py)
- [Primary tests at the measured commit](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/d50d516364304046aa939c6b36bda5ec460f6bda/tests/mamba/test_vibecuda_ssd_combined.py)
- [Contract tests at the measured commit](https://github.com/Edenzzzz/flashinfer/blob/d50d516364304046aa939c6b36bda5ec460f6bda/tests/mamba/test_vibecuda_ssd_contracts.py)
- [CAKE roadmap issue 4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254)

## Related Issues

Related to [issue 4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254), which tracks CAKE kernel integration work.

## Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Full repository pre-commit suite passes on the measured commit.
- [x] `git diff --check` passes.
- [x] Repository tests cover the public API, strided views, checkpoint outputs, invalid contracts, and stream isolation.
- [x] Candidate and CAKE use identical inputs and CUPTI timing boundaries.
- [x] All 12 advertised candidate rows pass CuTe parity and full-write validation.
- [ ] Current-head SM100 performance revalidation.
- [ ] CUDA Graph validation.
- [ ] Framework-level serving throughput validation.

## Reviewer Notes

The generated kernel is in `include/flashinfer/mamba/vibecuda_ssd_combined.cuh`. Public API and FFI changes are in `flashinfer/mamba/ssd_vibecuda.py`, `csrc/vibecuda_mamba_ssd_combined_jit_binding.cu`, and `csrc/vibecuda_mamba_ssd_combined.cu`. The benchmark now records the Git commit, exact candidate and CAKE source digests, GPU model, toolchain, precision policy, and timer contract, and rejects mixed-provenance summaries. Generated GPU result JSON is intentionally local because it is hardware and commit specific.

title: fix(cudnn): keep the ragged prefill on the exact-shape graph when FROST engines are opted in on cudnn-frontend < 1.30
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1` opts cudnn-frontend's FROST (python) SDPA engines in, and once opted in they rank ahead of the cuDNN backend plans, so they serve every cuDNN prefill graph FlashInfer builds. Before cudnn-frontend 1.30 their execute path read the **declared** geometry and could not honor execute-time shape overrides ([cudnn-frontend #1098](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/issues/1098), fixed by [#1119](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1119) and [#1132](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1132)). Since #5245 the ragged prefill builds one override-enabled graph per length class, declared at `(batch 4096, seq class 128 | 65536+)`, so on such a frontend every FROST-served call raises:

```
ValueError: cu_seq_len_q must have B + 1 = 4097 elements (prefix sums); got 4
```

(`tests/attention/test_cudnn_ragged_shape_override.py` with FROST opted in: all 31 numerics tests error on cudnn-frontend `develop@d34a6909c`, 31/31 pass on `develop@5567e2733`.)

This PR keeps the exact-shape graph, with one warning, when the FROST opt-in is set on a cudnn-frontend older than 1.30 (`_cudnn_supports_shape_override` gains the check; the frontend version parse is factored into a cached `_cudnn_frontend_version`). Nothing changes when the env var is unset (backend plans honor overrides from 1.29) or on 1.30+, where the FROST prepared launch honors them (measured through this wrapper: 124 → 88 µs per `run()` for #1119 → #1132, backend 67).

## 🔍 Related Issues

cudnn-frontend #1098 / #1119 / #1132; follows #5245.

The new `test_frost_opt_in_needs_cudnn_frontend_1_30` pins: opt-in + frontend 1.29 → exact shape and one warning (a second call warns no more); opt-in + 1.30 → override; no opt-in + 1.29 → override.

title: fix(cake_warp_decode): extend NVFP4 warp-decode coverage and synchronization
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## Current status: WIP — 199/448 rows qualify

The exported code remains at `d2fc2080219d1c9847842a9289fc2b2a33f400f6`, program identity `c80a679872a6346da17ac1cee829ae192bcd19995203f76adbfa49aef62a6a00` (inventory SHA-256 `9d4b098ce59cf6d8699de9ac730c6d0c02238982d376ed440d3ac77cef0892a9`).

**448/448 rows have valid, independently audited paired measurements; 199 meet both current performance gates. All 448 satisfy the 3% export-latency limit; 199 beat the official baseline.** These are separate conditions. Coverage is SM103 224/224 and SM100 224/224. All 448 rows use the frozen exported program identified above.

As updated on September 16, current acceptance permits **export latency / independently paired source latency ≤1.03** (equivalently **source/export ≥1/1.03 ≈0.970873786**) and still requires **official baseline / independently paired export >1** on every row. A baseline tie fails. The latency ratio is the exact 3% rule; the older ≥0.97 ratio is not substituted for it. Correctness, semantics and the measurement protocol are unchanged. Gate flags use saved unrounded measurements; no timing was repeated for this reclassification. The prior ≥1 export gate remains recorded as historical evidence: 221 export passes and 109 both-gate passes.

The complete table is still an incomplete delivery: **249 valid rows still fail the official-baseline speedup requirement**. Unified optimization candidates are still being validated and contribute **zero rows** to this frozen-artifact table. Their code and binaries are separate from this PR head; successful preparation, build or proof checks do not grant performance credit.

## 📌 Description

Extends NVFP4 warp-decode to seven public MoE configurations on SM100 and SM103, for **1–32 tokens with all routed experts local** (`local_num_experts == num_experts`). The public API, Python/C++ contracts, activation-aware dispatch, generated CUDA programs and route manifests cover the same geometries. All four previously supported geometries and the SM103 production dispatch contract are preserved.

|Model / routed expert bank|Hidden|Intermediate|Experts|Top-k|Activation|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|Qwen3-30B-A3B|2048|768|128|8|SwiGLU|
|Qwen3-235B-A22B|4096|1536|128|8|SwiGLU|
|Qwen3.5-35B-A3B|2048|512|256|8|SwiGLU|
|Qwen3.5-397B-A17B|4096|1024|512|10|SwiGLU|
|MiniMax-M2|3072|1536|256|8|SwiGLU|
|MiniMax-M3|6144|3072|128|4|SwiGLU: alpha=1.702, beta=1, clamp=7|
|Kimi-K3 latent expert bank|3584|3072|896|16|SiTU: gate scale=4, linear scale=25, no clamp|

M3 and K3 use their actual per-expert activation parameters, including changes replayed through CUDA Graphs. SiTU FC1 retains strict math through per-source compilation options. For parameterized SwiGLU with non-unit gate scale, the exported interface consumes logical beta/clamp, while the official comparison view uses beta and clamp divided by `output1_scale_gate_scalar`; alpha and physical weights/scales remain shared. The API documentation explains preparing and refreshing these derived buffers outside timing and capture.

The additional model identities and activation semantics come from the public [MiniMax-M3 configuration](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3/blob/f0e1c1e04d40177e4673a22097036854f536e9c0/config.json) and [Kimi-K3 configuration](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/blob/f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06/config.json). K3's 3584 width is its latent routed-expert width; surrounding projections, normalization, routing and shared experts remain caller-owned. M3's shared expert also remains separate. The entry points consume the **NVFP4 group-16 physical ABI**. Native MXFP4 group-32 checkpoint tensors require conversion; full-width routed-bank validation does not validate TP8 intermediate-width-384 configurations or whole-model serving. [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3#model-architecture) is a dense diffusion model and does not add an applicable routed-MoE shape.

The combined generated delivery contains **704 routes** across the eleven geometries and both architectures, with 48 modules, 38 sequences and 137 inventory files. Generated sources, typed headers and selected runtime fields match their architecture-specific export inputs.


The code refresh changes 131 selected routes while preserving the 704-route geometry/architecture scope. It updates generated packed-input work feeds, K512 variants and fixed-top-k finalizers, with matching bindings, contracts and manifest. Unvalidated optimization candidates are excluded.

Current performance evidence includes correctness and raw paired-measurement audits for all 448 rows of the frozen program. This completes measurement coverage, while 249 rows still fail performance acceptance. Unified candidates still require their own affected correctness, separately bounded sanitizer checks, source/export/build/runtime correspondence and both-architecture validation before final acceptance.

Historical validation for the preceding published program remains recorded separately: source GPU slices passed 21 cases per architecture on B200/B300; exporter CPU checks passed 91 cases, public JIT/contract checks 138, and the comparison harness 107 CPU plus 8 GPU checks. Public correctness covered all seven new geometries at T1–32 on both architectures, including graph/boundary behavior. ## Reviewer notes and measurement protocol

The comparison uses the actual matching official FlashInfer TensorRT-LLM baseline with shared physical NVFP4 inputs and matched activation semantics. Kernel latencies use **CUPTI with cold L2** and symmetric external CUDA Graphs: all six source/export/official creation-order permutations, six instances per arm with equal coverage, same-instance prime, and correctness checks before and after replay. Three counterbalanced groups use seed 28301, with **50 ms warmup + 100 ms measurement per arm/group**. Directional disagreement and the registered endpoint-drift statistic must be ≤2%; SM clock must be ≥1900 MHz; FP4 tolerance is atol=1/rtol=0.1. title: perf(cute-dsl): skip inactive pages in windowed decode
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Skip whole paged-KV pages that are entirely before a sliding-window decode
request's earliest active key. The kernel advances the page-table origin and
rebases the effective sequence length before constructing page and sequence
tile counts; the existing mask still handles the retained leading partial
page.

The rebase preserves three invariants:

1. key and query coordinates shift by the same whole-page token count, so
   causal and sliding-window mask decisions are unchanged, including
   multi-token decode;
2. the sequence-length remainder modulo page size is unchanged, so partial
   last-page handling is unchanged;
3. skipped pages plus retained pages equals the original page count, so fixed
   and ragged page-table segments remain in bounds.

BLASST threshold normalization intentionally continues to use the original
full sequence length. Dense and causal-without-left-window paths do not enter
the new branch.

### Performance

Fresh same-GPU results compare parent `231f708` with exact candidate
`117518a` on one NVIDIA B300 SM103. The workload is BF16
B16/Q1/Hq32/Hkv16/D256 with `window_left=1023`. Compilation, allocation, and
graph capture are outside timing. Each measurement uses 50 warmups and 300
CUDA Graph iterations; cells run A/B/A for three cycles. The parent median is
over six samples and the candidate median over three.

| Page | K | Parent median (us) | Candidate median (us) | Latency reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 1024 | 42.185 | 42.237 | -0.12% |
| 16 | 4096 | 152.694 | 42.585 | 72.11% |
| 16 | 8192 | 304.258 | 42.872 | 85.91% |
| 32 | 1024 | 41.880 | 41.714 | 0.40% |
| 32 | 4096 | 152.613 | 41.899 | 72.55% |
| 32 | 8192 | 305.401 | 42.022 | 86.24% |
| 64 | 1024 | 41.927 | 41.814 | 0.27% |
| 64 | 4096 | 153.293 | 41.639 | 72.84% |
| 64 | 8192 | 306.466 | 41.854 | 86.34% |

K1024 is the no-skip control because the requested window already covers the
entire sequence; it remains flat. At longer K the candidate remains near the
cost of the retained window while the parent scans the full sequence.

CLI-equivalent command used by each arm (with `$P` and `$K` expanded per row):

```bash
python flashinfer/cute_dsl/attention/gqa_decode_paged.py \
  --b 16 --p 1 --s "$K" --pg "$P" --h_q 32 --h_k 16 --d 256 \
  --kv_splits 0 --reduction auto --window_left 1023 --window_right 0 \
  --warmups 50 --iterations 300 --skip_ref_check --quiet
```

The CLI's derived throughput labels use the original full K and are not
reported here after page skipping; only measured latency is compared.

- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Local source checks completed:

- `uvx pre-commit run --all-files`
- `uvx ruff check flashinfer/cute_dsl/attention/gqa_decode_paged.py tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_decode.py`
- `uvx ruff format --check flashinfer/cute_dsl/attention/gqa_decode_paged.py tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_decode.py`
- `python3 -m py_compile flashinfer/cute_dsl/attention/gqa_decode_paged.py tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_decode.py`

B300 checks completed for exact candidate `117518a`:

- 10 focused tests passed: Q1/Q4, page sizes 8/16/32/64, ragged split-K,
  split early-exit, CUDA Graph replay with growing lengths, and the BLASST
  full-length-normalization discriminator;
- the direct fixed-length B2/Q4/K2051/page16/split-K3 CLI path passed its

title: perf(norm): tune CuTe-DSL qk_rmsnorm and fused_add_rmsnorm_quant tiling for SM100/103/107
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

Two tiling adjustments to the CuTe-DSL norm kernels on Blackwell and Rubin (SM100, SM103, SM107), gated on an explicit architecture list (`_LATENCY_BOUND_SMS`) so all other architectures are unchanged. No kernel body, layout, or math changes.
  
**`qk_rmsnorm`: fewer threads per row for small head_dim.** The kernel reused the RMSNorm threads-per-row table, which for head_dim ≤ 256 leaves every thread with a single 16-byte vector. With at most 2048 resident threads per SM that is only 32 KB in flight per SM, and the kernel is latency-bound at large M. On the listed architectures each thread now owns ~32 elements (4/4/8 threads per row for head_dim 64/128/256 instead of 8/16/32). Adding threads per CTA instead was measured to be monotonically worse. `QKRMSNormKernel` now takes `sm_version`, which is part of the compile-cache key like the other norm kernels.
  
**`fused_add_rmsnorm_quant`: no 256-thread bump for H > 8192.** The two-rows-per-CTA rule doubles the two  shared-memory tiles and halves resident CTAs. On the listed architectures the kernel keeps 128 threads and one row per CTA. Output is bit-identical.

 shown where measured.

title: fix(tests): skip cuDNN KDA kernel-oracle arm where the oracle has no SM107
body:
## 📌 Description

On the Rubin (VR200 / SM107) lane, all 12 parametrizations of
`tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_cudnn_backend.py::test_cudnn_backend_matches_default` fail:

```
E   ValueError: backend='cute-dsl' does not support this recurrent_kda prefill contract
E   ValueError: backend='cake'     does not support this recurrent_kda prefill contract
```

The cuDNN backend under test is fine there. The failure is in the test's **oracle** — the same
shape as #5246, one exception type further out.

This test compares cuDNN against FlashInfer's own recurrent KDA prefill backends, parametrized over
both of them, and both are gated to compute capability `{(10, 0), (10, 3)}`:

| | gate | value |
|---|---|---|
| cute-dsl prefill | `flashinfer/kda_prefill_cute.py:34` | `_SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES = {(10, 0), (10, 3)}` |
| Cake prefill | `flashinfer/kda_prefill.py:59` | `_FLASH_KDA_SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES = {(10, 0), (10, 3)}` |
| cuDNN engines (module gate) | `tests/test_helpers/cudnn_linear_attention.py:39` | `{(10, 0), (10, 1), (10, 2), (10, 3), (10, 7)}` |

cuDNN serves five capabilities, the oracles two. On the three in between, the module runs and the
oracle cannot. Because the test names a backend explicitly rather than using `"auto"`, the
dispatcher refuses instead of falling back (`flashinfer/kda.py:553` for cute-dsl, `:662` for Cake),
so the reference call raises before cuDNN is reached. 12 = 2 oracles × 2 `use_initial_state` × 3
`seq_lens`, each failing in under a second, host-side.

### Why #5246's guard does not catch it

#5246 routed this very call through the shared `reference_kernel_or_skip` helper, which catches
`ImportError` and `NotImplementedError` — the two ways a backend reports *unavailable* (DSL too old,
backend missing, GDN prefill needing CUDA 13+). A backend that is merely **architecture-ineligible**
reports it as a `ValueError`, which escapes the helper.

Widening the helper to catch `ValueError` would be wrong: the same exception is how a real contract
regression would surface on B200, and swallowing it would turn a genuine failure into a silent skip.
So this gates on the capability instead, reading the supported sets from the product modules rather
than restating them, so the skip follows automatically if SM107 support lands.

### The other cuDNN linear-attention tests

Four test files use the cuDNN linear-attention helper; only two ever use an in-tree kernel as an
oracle, and they are exactly the two `reference_kernel_or_skip` call sites:

| File | In-tree oracle | Exposure |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_cudnn_backend.py` | `recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl"/"cake")` | **this PR** |
| `tests/gdn/test_prefill_cudnn_backend.py` | `chunk_gated_delta_rule` (default backend) | not arch-gated this way; passes the SM107 dispatch check (`_arch_major in (9, 10, 12)`) and does not fail on the Rubin nightly |
| `tests/gdn2/test_prefill_gdn2_cudnn_backend.py` | none | FlashInfer has no GDN-2 kernel — `auto` and `cudnn` are one path, and the cross-family GDN comparison passes `backend="cudnn"` |
| `tests/gdp/test_prefill_gdp_cudnn_backend.py` | none | same: no GDP kernel, cross-family comparison is `backend="cudnn"` |

`tests/mamba/` has no cuDNN coverage at all — it never imports the frontend — so there is nothing to
audit there.

The Rubin nightly agrees: pipeline #68147175 on VR200 / CUDA 13.4 reports
`tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_cudnn_backend.py (12 failed nodes)` and no GDN, GDN-2 or GDP cuDNN
file in the failed set.

## 🧪 Tests

This box is B200 / CUDA 13.0 with cudnn-frontend 1.27 < the required 1.29, so the module gate skips
the file wholesale here (59 skipped), exactly as in #5246. The new branch was therefore driven
directly, with only the two host-side facts the module gate reads faked:

- Gate forced open, capability faked to `(10, 7)`: **12 failed → 12 skipped**, reporting
  `reference backend cute-dsl does not support sm107` / `... cake does not support sm107`.
- Gate forced open, real `(10, 0)`: the skip does **not** fire, so supported hardware is unaffected.
- Unfaked: 59 skipped, unchanged from `main`.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_cudnn_backend.py` → clean.

Please run CI to confirm the Rubin column: `/bot run tests/kda tests/gdn tests/gdn2 tests/gdp`

## 🔍 Related Issues

Sibling of #5246. The Rubin failure was surfaced by the VR200 lane on #5253.

## Note, out of scope

Whether the cute-dsl and Cake KDA prefill backends should support SM107 at all is a kernel-coverage
question, not a test fix, and is left alone here.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Tests**
  * Updated cuDNN backend comparisons to run only on GPUs supported by the selected reference backend.
  * Tests now skip unsupported compute capabilities instead of producing invalid comparison results.

title: fix(sampling): index per-request thresholds by request, not by probs row
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

When `indices` is given, several requests can share one row of `probs`, so the batch is larger than the number of rows. The documented contract is per request: `probs` is `(unique_batch_size, num_classes)`, while `top_k`, `top_p` and `min_p` are `(batch_size,)` and "each request has its own threshold".

The kernels disagree about that. `TopKSamplingFromProbKernel` reads `top_k_arr[bx]` and `MinPSamplingFromProbKernel` reads `min_p_arr[bx]`, indexed by the output slot, but `TopPSamplingFromProbKernel` reads `top_p_arr[row_idx]` and `TopKTopPSamplingFromProbKernel` reads both arrays at `row_idx`, indexed by the probs row. So a request gets the threshold belonging to whichever request owns the row it reads. With `indices = [1, 0]`, two rows and `top_p = [0.5, 1.0]`, request 0 samples tokens its own `top_p` excludes and request 1 is restricted by the other request's threshold.

The shared validator also sizes these arrays against `probs`, so the documented per-request tensor cannot be passed when the batch is larger than the number of rows, and the kernels that index by `bx` read past the end of a row-sized array. `compute-sanitizer --tool initcheck` reports uninitialized reads in `TopKSamplingFromProbKernel` for one row, three requests and a length-1 `top_k`. memcheck stays quiet because the allocator pads the block.

This indexes every per-request parameter by the output slot and sizes them by the batch in the validator. The renorm entry points take no `indices`, so their batch already equals the row count and their behaviour is unchanged.

title: fix(topk): add missing __syncthreads before AdvanceRadixGroupBarrier
body:
Adds the missing `__syncthreads()` before `AdvanceRadixGroupBarrier` at the two multi-CTA histogram-accumulation sites in `topk.cuh` (`RadixSelectOneRound` and `RadixSelectFromSharedMemory`).

**What the sync guards against.** Each CTA's threads accumulate their local histogram into the shared global histogram with per-thread `atomicAdd`, and the leading CTA's threads clear `next_hist`, immediately before the group barrier. The barrier's release is a thread-0-only `red_release`, whose fence — per its own comment — "releases data that was weakly-written by other threads **prior to the last syncthreads**". There is no `__syncthreads()` between those per-thread writes and the barrier, so the release does not cover them:

- a peer CTA can pass the barrier and read `current_hist` before some contributor's `atomicAdd` lands → undercounted histogram → wrong or CTA-divergent pivot → silently wrong renorm probabilities in top-k sampling;
- a peer CTA can start the next round's `atomicAdd`s into `next_hist` before the leader's lagging threads finished clearing it → contributions wiped by a late clear.

This is the same syncthreads + thread-0-release idiom already documented in `RadixGroupResetStateLastCTA` (and #3610).

Validation: instruction-level scheduling-delay stress on `RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA` (per-thread delays of 10µs–1ms injected at the global-atomic ops): unpatched, renorm output deviates ~0.03 from an exact reference on every run; patched, exact under the same delays. No behavior change without delays.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved synchronization during multi-CTA top-k selection to ensure results are consistently visible across participating processing units.

title: feat(attention): add causal + bidirectional-ranges batch prefill
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

FA2 supports custom attention variants, but there is currently no packaged batch-prefill path for sequences that are causal except for spans that attend in both directions. Callers either have to materialize a dense custom mask or use a different backend.

The dense mask is `O(qo_len * kv_len)`. For example, 16384 scheduled query tokens against a 262144-token context require 4 GiB just for a boolean mask.

This PR adds an FA2 paged-prefill wrapper that computes the mask directly from a compact `int32 [total_q, 2]` range tensor:

```text
(causal AND causal_window) OR (in_range AND range_window)
```

Each query row contains an inclusive `[start, end]` span in request-local KV positions. `(-1, -1)` means that the query has no bidirectional span and remains purely causal. At 16384 query tokens, this tensor is 128 KiB regardless of context length.

The implementation uses the existing `variant_owns_mask` path in `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`; it does not change the default prefill dispatch.

The public API added here is:

| Symbol | Exported from |
|---|---|
| `BatchPrefillWithCausalBidirectionalRangesWrapper` | `flashinfer`, `flashinfer.attention` |
| `gen_batch_prefill_bidirectional_ranges_module` | `flashinfer.jit.attention` |

The wrapper and generator share one internal spec for the URI and JIT tensor and scalar arguments.

Two kernel details are worth calling out:

- The variant sets `window_left = kv_len` to keep FA2's normal sliding-window tile pruning from discarding keys that may still belong to a bidirectional range. The causal and range windows are applied inside the variant instead.
- Padded `CTA_TILE_Q` lanes are clamped to the last real query row before indexing the range tensor.

The wrapper is FA2-only because this path relies on a custom `LogitsMask` being evaluated for every KV tile. Its JIT specialization is fixed in the constructor; `plan()` and `workspace_size()` inherit omitted dtype values from that specialization and reject explicit mismatches. Options that conflict with the variant-owned mask are rejected rather than silently ignored.

Packed NVFP4 KV caches use the existing `maybe_k_cache_sf` and `maybe_v_cache_sf` JIT tensor conventions.

title: feat(moe): CUTLASS FP8 per-tensor runner takes the TRT-LLM static-scale activation pack
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`(TrtllmFp8PerTensorConfig(), CutlassFp8PerTensorConfig())` could not share one `MoEActivationPack`: TRT-LLM keeps a static calibration multiplier in its weight view and carries no pack scale; the unified CUTLASS runner expected a dynamic (per-call, amax-derived) 0-dim dequant scale on the pack. vLLM / SGLang feed static scales to the flat CUTLASS FP8 path, so CUTLASS now speaks the static contract.

- `CutlassFp8PerTensorConfig.prepare_weights(..., hidden_states_scale_global=, intermediate_scale_global=)` takes the TRT-LLM static multipliers (`q = x * scale`) and folds the flat `quant_scales` at load time: `fc1_dequant_scale = fc1_dequant / a1`, `fc2_act_quant_scale = a2`, `fc2_dequant_scale = fc2_dequant / a2`, `fc1_act_dequant_scale = 1 / a1`. `fc1_dequant` / `fc2_dequant` and the two globals stay in the view as metadata.
- `CutlassFp8PerTensorRunner` validates and passes the four through. GEMM2 input is requantized with the calibrated intermediate scale (was an implicit 1.0); `hidden_states_scale` must be `None`.
- `prepare_activations` is the TRT-LLM helper; `prepare_cutlass_fp8_per_tensor_activations` (dynamic scale) is removed. A CUDA-tensor scale skips host-side validation, so the per-step path is sync-free and graph-capturable.
