title: refactor(sparse-mla): unify SM120 execution, calibration and DSv4.1 support
body:
## 📌 Description

### TLDR

Reorganize SM120 sparse MLA into a package with clear ownership and add **DSv4.1 dual-cache attention** (FP8/BF16 compute, FP4/FP8 extra cache), **runtime page/head/topk dispatch** for the six ordinary families, and **per-configuration L2-cold calibration** with unified prepared execution. Fixes empty-effective-KV semantics (#4484), startup calibration recovery (#5142), and the finite-instantiation dispatch gaps reported in #4541/#5135/#5192. 947 tests pass on SM120 (CUDA 12.9 and 13.2) and SM121 (GB10); kernel performance is within 1% of the pre-refactor baseline on a 95-point matrix, with DOTS3 SG 6.9–11.9% faster.

### Features

- **DSv4.1 dual cache**: primary FP8 cache plus optional FP4/FP8 extra cache, independent topk/page sizes, FP8 or BF16 compute. New public APIs `dsv41_fp4_quantize_pack_sparse_mla_cache` / `dsv41_fp4_quantize_append_sparse_mla_cache` with docs, trace templates, and generated examples. The DSv4 compatibility layout accepts page 32, covering vLLM's page-32 DSv4.1 allocation.
- **Runtime dispatch**: all six ordinary families (`dsv4`, `dsv3_2`, `glm_nsa`, `glm53_nope`, `dots3_swa`, `dsv4_1`) accept **positive integer runtime page sizes, including non-powers of two**, in decode and their supported prefill routes, with independently sized main/extra pages for dual caches. Existing constraints remain: inline prefill requires gap-free pages (row padding is supported); footer caches require aligned page strides. **DSv4 NVFP4 is not broadened** (main page 64, extra pages 2/64, existing finite head/topk instantiations).
- **Calibration**: every ordinary family gets per-configuration, per-device token-bucket profiles alongside NVFP4 in the shared schema-v3 store. The cold protocol measures **100 samples and their mean** with a **4x L2** eviction before each timed call (eviction outside the interval); a protocol identifier discards stale measurements. Off-grid token counts are refined outside the store lock and merged atomically; `force` replaces complete profiles. Profiles apply to canonical packed layouts only. `calibrate_sparse_mla_sm120` gains keyword-only precision, page-size, extra-cache, topk-length, and sink options; defaults preserve single-cache behavior.
- **Prepared execution**: downstream entry points share cached plans, modules, and workspaces. Eager calls execute from growable per-wrapper scratch arenas (sweeping tokens 1→64 grew device memory by ~103 MiB before, ~33 MiB now ≈ the largest signature); a warmed signature's first capture pins dedicated buffers before recording, so captured graphs survive arena growth. Caller-supplied and functional-path scratch are unchanged; eager calls sharing wrapper-owned scratch must not race across streams (documented).

### Bug fixes

- **#4484 empty effective KV**: rows with zero length or only `-1` padding indices now return **O = 0 and LSE = -inf** (base 2) from every SM120 sparse store path; a finite attention sink still contributes (`LSE = sink·log2(e)`, O = 0). Producers previously scaled the `-1e30` sentinel so all-padding rows got spurious unit probability; masked probabilities are now zeroed by validity, internal partials keep the finite sentinel, and only the final store exports `-inf`. Covered for zero-length and all-negative rows, single/dual caches with either side empty, finite and extreme sinks, real CUDA `merge_state` neutrality, and graph replay with in-place metadata updates.
- **#5142 startup calibration**: `torch.AcceleratorError` OOM is recognized, restoring pool-size fallback (initializer references are released before retrying); an implausible analytical fit is remeasured once without relaxing the residual threshold; failed fits do not roll back successful profiles. The recommended workflow — idle pre-calibration in a separate process, then cache-only warmup via `skip_ops` (which also suppresses off-grid refinement) — is documented on the API. Concurrent load can still contaminate measurements; SM121 TP2 startup has not been revalidated.
- **Finite-instantiation dispatch gaps** (#4541 non-instantiated decode topk falling through to prefill, #5135 H16/K512 dual prefill, #5192 extra page 32): removed by the runtime dispatch above. These shapes are reachable in the resolver and generic runtime-page tests; their exact serving configurations have not been rerun end to end.
- **#5001 hang guard**: swapAB spectator IO warps retire after CTA sync and register release, as upstream #5048 established — they gather nothing and no barrier counts them, so waiting on ring phases could spin forever at kernel drain. Verified with 24,000 swapAB executions/replays on both SM120 and SM121.
- **CUDA 12.9 mixed-cache BF16 conversion**: uses the `mov.b16` low-byte extraction and `h` constraint matching CUDA's FP4 header; the five original CI failures were reproduced first. The remaining `mov.b32` form in `e2m1x2_code_to_float2` is safe because its `uint8_t` input guarantees zero upper bytes (documented in code); checked on 13.2 with a maximum 0.68% slowdown at three points.
- **Review hardening**: capability probing is JIT-free again (static coarse pre-filter; C++ dispatch stays authoritative); the custom op's new `extra_fp4` parameter has a default; functional entries accept padded-capacity LSE buffers like the wrapper; the calibration store self-heals a corrupt same-schema cache during locked merge and keeps failure marks process-lifetime; ordinary lazy calibration has the NVFP4-style re-entry guard and failed refinements are suppressed in-process; NVFP4 pool floors account for `2x L2` (large-L2 parts) and its profiles are gated to canonical packed layouts; NVFP4 merge2 handles partial head blocks; MG dual prefill no longer reads extra indices past the row end (compute-sanitizer: 133 invalid reads before, 0 after); dead exports/fields removed; standalone bindings range-check narrowing overrides and require `num_splits` to cover the resolved chunking.

### Organization and compatibility

- `flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py` becomes a same-named package with explicit root re-exports and separate API, execution, prepared-plan, policy, calibration, and NVFP4 owners. Root entry points used by vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM, and b12x remain available, including dispatch iteration for capability probes. Old auxiliary module paths, root monkeypatch reassignment, and pickles referencing them are not compatibility guarantees.
- C++ bindings/dispatch are split by format and headers by responsibility under one `sparse_mla_sm120` JIT/AOT module, including NVFP4 exports and the test-only MMA layout probe; the removed `gen_sparse_mla_nvfp4_sm120_module` / `_tile_module` names remain as compatibility aliases.
- Kernel work: SG pointer arrays replaced by base-plus-offset addressing (256 B less local storage); DOTS3 keeps its four page-64 SG performance specializations; DSv4 tile addressing simplified; H32 FP8 single-cache MG uses a 240/24 register split.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #4802. Defines the empty-effective-KV contract requested by #4484 for the SM120 sparse MLA paths (other backends are out of scope), addresses the calibration recovery and OOM fallback from #5142, and removes the dispatch gaps reported in #4541, #5135, and #5192.

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

- **CUDA 13.2.86, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120): 949 passed, no skips** on the final tree across the seven files below plus `test_sparse_mla_sm120_binding_guards.py`. CUDA 12.9.86 ran 882 passed on the pre-#4484 tree; the conversion fix itself is re-covered by the current suite.

- **Seven-file CPU-only run: 112 passed / 770 skipped.** Earlier architecture-skip checks with no GPU and simulated major architectures 9/10 each yielded 99 passed / 116 skipped on the four host-policy files. These are not GPU execution results for SM90/SM100.

title: perf(topk_varlen): gvr_2 decode floor: PDL launch, staged coalesced emit, early row load
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Stacked on #5312 (→ #5310 → #5307 → #5304); review the last commit only.

Small-N decode top-k (rows ≤ 64, N ≤ 8K: the DSA decode shape) runs at a launch-and-latency floor of 3-5 us, and there SGLang's `topk_v2` was 5-27% faster than `gvr_2` (worst: K=2048, N=4096 at 0.73x). Profiling with Nsight Compute and CUPTI split that gap into two parts: about 0.4 us of launch overlap (SGLang launches with programmatic dependent launch, so consecutive kernels overlap in a graph) and a kernel-body gap dominated by scoreboard stalls. Three changes to the **register family** close it:

1. **Programmatic dependent launch** for the decode register families (`_DECODE_PDL`). The kernels already `griddepcontrol.wait` before their first read; passing the launch attribute lets the next kernel's launch processing overlap this kernel's tail, in a CUDA graph and in a serving stream alike. ~0.4 us on every decode cell.
2. **Staged coalesced output.** The per-bin-cursor emit writes each index to a position scattered across the row within a warp, so every emitted index cost one L1 store sector (5x the sectors of a coalesced write, ~1 us at k=2048). The k outputs are now staged in a k-word shared-memory region at the tail of the register kernel's dynamic window (all emit paths write raw indices there; unwritten slots surface as -1) and written to global in one coalesced pass after a barrier, which also applies the prefill / paged output transform. The host enables it for one-wave launches only (rows ≤ SM count, the latency-bound regime): several waves deep, the extra barrier + copy measured 3-4% slower than the scattered stores, so multi-wave launches and the prefill slabs keep the direct emit (compile-time `stage_out`). The existing warp-ballot emit arm was measured as the alternative and is slower on every cell.
3. **Early envelope-bounded row load** (decode). The float4 register batch is loaded at kernel start bounded by the launch envelope (≤ the row width, memory-safe) instead of after the per-row `kv_lens` read, so the two global latencies overlap; lanes beyond the row's own length are -inf-filled in the body. Prefill keeps its in-body load (its base depends on the `row_starts` read).

No API change. The register families' compile keys gain the `pdl` and `stage_out` flags; launch shared memory grows by `4 * k` bytes for the staging region on one-wave launches only.

title: feat(topk_varlen): absolute-column output for windowed (prefill) top-k (absolute_indices)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Stacked on #5307 (which stacks on #5304); review the last commit only.

Windowed (prefill) `top_k_varlen` returns **window-local** indices (`column - row_starts[r]`). The DSA prefill indexer's consumer wants the **absolute column** of the packed key axis, i.e. the flattened-KV slot: SGLang's `topk_transform_ragged_v2` produces exactly that by adding `out_offsets` inside its kernel, so a FlashInfer caller today has to run a separate offset-add over `num_rows x top_k` indices after every call (an extra launch on the critical path of every prefill layer; ~256 MB read-modify-write at 32K rows x K=2048).

This PR adds `top_k_varlen(..., row_starts=, absolute_indices=True)` and fuses that add into the index emit of **both** windowed gvr_2 engine families (streaming slab and register rungs):

- every emitted index already leaves the float4-rounded read frame through one subtraction (`- lead`); the absolute frame is the same single add with a different per-row constant (`+ col0`). No extra memory traffic, no extra launch, no extra register.
- `-1` pads untouched; identity (short) windows shifted; out-of-window columns never read; `return_values` gathers at the absolute columns.
- compile-time variant (`prefill_abs` in the compile keys, persist names `..._pf_abs`): the default path is byte-identical. The prefill launcher cache, `warmup_prefill(..., absolute_indices=)` and `prefill_ready(..., absolute_indices=)` key on it.
- decode mode refuses the flag with a `ValueError` (its indices are already columns of `logits`); non-bool values are refused.

Also fixes a `warmup_prefill` gap introduced with the register routing in #5307: the register table admits every hint of the mid buckets, so the slab engine that an **unhinted** call of that width takes was never compiled by warmup (`prefill_ready` False right after warmup; capture would raise). Each bucket now also warms its slab tier at both promotion edges.

## Reviewer Notes

- The kernel diff is mechanical: in both engines every `idx - lead` emit became `idx + ofs` with `ofs = -lead` (local) or `+col0` (absolute). The slab keeps `col0` in a shared-memory word next to the existing lead-lane slot (published once, read per emit); its identity epilogue re-reads `row_starts[row]` because short rows skip the body and its barriers. The register rungs run at a 32-register cap, so the absolute variant keeps `ks` (= `col0 | lead`) as the ONE per-row value live through the sampling ladder and recomputes `lead = ks & 3` (in-range count, once per level) and `col0 = ks & -4` (per emit region). Alternatives measured on the VPT=1 rung and rejected: a second live register next to `lead` (3% slower), a global re-read of `row_starts[row]` at emit (5%), a broadcast shared-memory word (3%; the load gets hoisted back into a register).
- The default (window-local) compile is unchanged in register/stack footprint (`cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage` identical); the local column of the tables above matches the #5307 numbers.
- Emit order of the engines is not fixed, so the tests compare row-wise index sets (sorted), not raw tensors.

title: perf(topk_varlen): route windowed (prefill) rows to the register-resident gvr_2 family
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Routes windowed (prefill) `top_k_varlen` rows to the register-resident gvr_2 family and gives that family a windowed mode. Follow-up to #5304 (stacked on it; only the last commit is new here).

#5304's window engines existed only for the streaming `main` slab, so every prefill row ran the slab, while the decode router sends rows of the same length to the register-resident `reg` kernels, which are 1.6-2x faster on windows up to 4K tokens. SGLang's prefill top-k kernel picks its path per row by window length, which is exactly where it was still ahead of us.

### What changed

- **Device**: `GvrTopkRegKernel(prefill=True)`. The row is read from the float4-rounded window base; the `ks & 3` lead lanes (thread 0's first float4) are excluded from the bracket fold, the identity hint positions, the histogram classify, the key-space escape and every emit by a 4-bit lane mask; indices are shifted to the window frame. A row whose scan extent exceeds the rung's register capacity (the caller's bound was violated) is reported as all `-1`, never as a truncated ranking. The slab engine is unchanged.
- **Host**: `_prefill_reg_route(rows, k, max_window)` — a per-part rung table measured on the causal staircase (rows 2K-32K, K ∈ {512, 2048}, bounds 2045/4093/8189, BLK/VPT/MINB menu, same node vs sglang topk_v2). B200 and B300 agree; Rubin differs: its slab is stronger at high row counts and the decode router's VPT=2/MINB=4 rung is register-starved there (the MINB=2 variant wins instead). `_reg_plan` mirrors `route()`'s register-band constants for an explicit rung.
- **API**: `top_k_varlen(..., row_starts=, max_seq_len=)` — the caller's bound on the window lengths (the longest prompt of the batch, host knowledge in every serving framework) selects the engine. Without it every row takes the slab, as in #5304. A per-row split across two launches was built, measured and dropped: the slab launch that only skips rows still costs ~35 µs per 32K rows (one CTA per row at its smem occupancy), and without the bound the register launch must take the largest capacity class, the wrong kernel for short windows.

### Perf

Causal staircase (R prompts x L tokens), fp32, graph replay, min of 3 interleaved repetitions, every column on the same node in the same job. `slab` = unhinted call (streaming engine, the #5304 behaviour); `hinted` = `max_seq_len=L`; `sgl_v2` = SGLang's default `topk_transform_ragged_v2`; `upstream` = TRT-LLM #18702 `run_prefill`. title: perf: reduce split W4A16 routing and output overhead
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

@humansand

Reduce split CuTe DSL W4A16 routing and bounds overhead, and use complete output subtiles for ordinary scratch stores.

- **Routing:** mark top-k `cutlass.Constexpr`, include it in the private kernel cache key, and omit the runtime argument. This removes runtime division from routing-scale lookup and output scatter.
- **Output bounds:** derive whether M covers complete physical CTA clusters, cache that Boolean, and remove feature predicates/clipping only for those shapes. Route guards and the partial/padded fallback remain. Checking the full cluster span is necessary for a padded peer CTA.
- **Scratch stores:** for non-fused output, use the existing plain TMA store for each fully valid subtile before a route boundary; retain predicated stores for the tail. Expert output ownership and FP32 combine remain unchanged.
- **Contract:** public APIs, weight layouts, numerical operations, two weight-dequantization warpgroups and autotune tactics are unchanged. Matrix dimensions and token counts remain dynamic. Non-fused finalization stores BF16 expert outputs, then combines in FP32 in fixed top-k order before one BF16 output cast; it uses no atomic or TMA reduction.
- **Tests:** extend existing route-boundary and padding test products with top-k 2/3, both finalize modes, full-prefix-plus-partial-tail cases and aligned→padded→aligned cache reuse. Preserve existing W4A4 cases, reference calculations and tolerances.

### Environment and source

- **Hardware/image:** one B300 SXM6 AC GPU on an 8-GPU c2 node (`hu-pdx-43`); GPU0 exclusively used. Driver590.48.01; explicit container `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3`.
- **Software:** Python3.12.3; Torch2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.5.50603568 (runtime reports2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.05), CUDA runtime13.2; CuTe DSL4.7.1; CUPTI Python13.4.0/library13.4.58; pytest9.1.1. System nvcc/ptxas is13.2.78. The DSL extension contains bundled compiler13.3.27 and emitted PTX identifies that version; these measurements do not establish system-ptxas13.2 code generation.
- **Source:** before `488ffbd9fe4455c3b4c3030cf668b5603c6698e4`; current `88ff7db6a558e8acbc0cd964275410cf94e5c22c`. GPU runs used the baseline checkout plus the exact candidate patch; measured implementation/test hashes match this commit. No source changes followed validation.
- **Execution:** `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`, `TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL=1`, `FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0`; project-local JIT caches, isolated venv preserving the image's Torch installation. Both sides use the same GPU/compiler stack.

### Validation

- **GPU tests:** 66 passed: 48 route-boundary cases, 4 extended padding/cache cases, 2 simulated EP8 functional cases and 12 CUDA-graph cases. Full repository suite was not run. The grouped-weight fixture requires feature widths divisible by 128; W4A16 numerical coverage uses widths 256→384→256 to exercise aligned and padded clusters.
- **Native:** fixed GEMM2 tactic `(128,64,256)`, cluster `(1,1)`, M-major, N256/K512, 8 experts, PDL/CLC disabled. Top-k specialization removes runtime `div.s32`/reciprocal sequences for top-k 2/3 (1640→1584 SASS instructions). At M256, bounds specialization further reduces the checked fused top-k2 case to 1568 and ordinary output from 1664→1624. At M288, both fallback SASS files are byte-identical to their immediate controls; these partial-width exports were compiled but not launched. The scratch-store change keeps the checked ordinary N64 instruction count at 1624; its N16 ordinary and N64 fused control SASS are byte-identical. Registers 128, stack 0 and local memory 0 remain unchanged.
- **Determinism:** six forced N64/N128/N192 × top-k2/3 tail cases, each repeated three times with PDL off and on, match the immediate control bit-for-bit (36 launches per source). Input hashes, unchanged references and zero absolute differences were checked. Ordinary native code uses plain `cp.async.bulk.tensor` / `UTMASTG.2D`, with no TMA reduction; the fixed-order FP32 combiner is unchanged.
- **Profiling:** Nsight Systems2026.2.1 and NCU2026.1.1 `--set full` captured current non-fused T2048 with its saved tactic, without retuning. FC2 uses grid2×1×74, cluster2, 512 threads, 128 registers/thread and222208 bytes dynamic shared memory (plus1024 driver bytes), with no local-memory accesses. NCU used40 kernel-replay passes; six CTC metrics were unavailable and separate native exports provide source line information. Instrumented durations are diagnostic, not benchmark evidence.
- **Local checks:** scoped pre-commit hooks, including mypy/Ruff, syntax and `git diff --check` passed.

```text
66 passed, 28 deselected, 1420 warnings in 46.07s
```

Warnings are existing CuTe DSL deprecations. Reproduce with:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL=1 FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE=0 \
python -m pytest \
  tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py::TestCuteDslMoeW4A16::test_route_tile_boundary_accuracy \
  tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py::TestCuteDslFusedMoeFunctional::test_finalize_handles_cluster_padding_and_partial_tiles \
  tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py::TestExpertParallelism::test_functional_with_ep \
  tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py::TestCuteDslMoEWrapper::test_wrapper_cuda_graph \
  -k 'w4a16 or test_finalize_handles_cluster_padding_and_partial_tiles' -v --tb=short
```

### Final performance

- **Workload:** upstream DeepSeek-like benchmark, H7168/I2048, 256 global experts, top-k 8, 32 local experts (single-GPU simulated EP8, TP1), SwiGLU, BF16 activations/output and NVFP4 weights. Routing is timed; weight preparation/autotuning and inter-GPU communication are excluded.
- **Timing:** normal autotuning for every complete sweep; ten warmups and 100 cold-L2 CUDA-graph CUPTI iterations per row, reporting medians. Fused and non-fused modes are evaluated separately; non-fused is the primary optimization target for its deterministic FP32 combine. Tokens 1/2/4 are reported and excluded from retention.

#### Non-fused finalize (primary)

One saved upstream sweep versus the latest complete current-source sweep on the same unchanged node/stack. Speedup is Before/After. Geometric-mean speedup over 8–8192 is **1.0056×** (**0.55% lower latency**); this is a small measured difference, not a statistical-significance claim. The scratch-store change repeatedly improves 1024–4096 against its immediate control; 8192 varied across repeats, so its final row does not establish a stable gain.

Speedup is `sqrt((Before R1 * Before R2) / (After R1 * After R2))`; no row minima or fixed-tactic substitutions.

title: feat(MSA): Add NVFP4 paged-KV MSA sparse decode and prefill for SM100/SM103
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Compute capability 10.0/10.3 (B200/GB300) had no NVFP4 route for MiniMax Sparse Attention: msa_sparse_attention and msa_sparse_decode_attention rejected packed uint8 K/V and tensor block scales on these parts. This adds that capability behind the existing public API. The only signature change is a new optional out= argument on the decode entry point.

Supported inputs (both routes)
- A packed NVFP4 paged KV cache: one planar 73,728 B page per block laid out as [K data | K scale | V data | V scale], passed as four strided views of the same allocation -- uint8 (num_pages, 4, 128, 64) data and (num_pages, 4, 128, 8) block scales. The kernels read the page in place and never materialize a dense or dequantized copy in global memory.
- e2m1 values with one e4m3 block scale per 16 elements. K scales are stored linearly, V scales in the cache writer's (4, 4) swizzle. Scale views may be uint8 or float8_e4m3fn. k_global_scale and v_global_scale are required.
- BF16 queries and BF16 output. The kernel bodies are built for 64 query heads, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128 and page_size 128; the guard enforces that geometry and the page layout, including the byte offsets between the four views.
- Batch size, per-request KV length (seqused_k), block-table width and the outer strides of q2k_indices are runtime arguments, so the head-major view of a token-major selection buffer is read without a copy.
- A call outside this surface falls through to the pre-existing NotImplementedError, whose message now names the axis that declined.

Decode (msa_sparse_decode_attention)
- top-k in [1, 32], seqlen_q >= 1 for speculative decode, causal or not.
- Two implementations sit behind one route and are chosen internally from the call geometry:
  * csrc/msa_decode_nvfp4_specialized.cu, a warp-specialized CUDA kernel that dequantizes e2m1 to e4m3 with the block scales folded in and runs QK and PV on tcgen05 kind::f8f6f4 with FP32 accumulation. It holds a parametric instantiation family plus a family pinned to the geometry above.
  * flashinfer/msa_ops/cute_dsl/sparse_decode_nvfp4_sm100.py, a CuTe-DSL kernel that dequantizes to FP16, runs mma.sync with FP32 accumulation, splits the selected blocks across a thread-block cluster and combines the partials through distributed shared memory. Both keep an online row maximum and neither issues a native FP4 MMA. FLASHINFER_MSA_DECODE_NVFP4_ROUTE=auto|pingpong|specialised overrides the choice.
- CUDA-graph capturable without an MSASparseAttentionWorkspace: everything before the launch is host-side shape arithmetic and no call shape can trigger a compile. One eager launch per device is needed before capture; msa_decode_nvfp4_specialized_warmup(device) provides it.
- out= lets the caller supply the destination (contiguous BF16 of q.shape), so no output temporary is allocated or copied.

Prefill (msa_sparse_attention)
- Only supports CUDA 13.X. No CUDA 12.x support
- Causal only, no LSE, top-k 16, paged layout with seqused_k as the sole source of per-request KV length (cu_seqlens_k is refused). Per-request query length and total query count are arbitrary.
- csrc/msa_prefill_nvfp4_specialized.cu: each CTA dequantizes the K and V sides of one selected page into its own dynamic shared memory and runs QK and PV on tcgen05 kind::f16 with BF16 operands and FP32 accumulation. The per-tile block union is a 128-slot hash table keyed on block id, so the block-table width is free up to the 24-bit block id (about 2^31 tokens at page_size 128) and the route allocates nothing beyond the output.
- The softmax fast path exponentiates against a fixed origin, paired with a range check on the row denominator and an exact replay, against a data-derived running maximum, of any tile that fails it. Output is bitwise reproducible run to run up to 16,384 tokens of context per request; above that the accumulation order may vary while staying correct.

Packaging and introspection
- Both kernels are registered in flashinfer/aot.py for sm100a and sm103a and build on CUDA 12.8+ toolkits: the BF16/E4M3/E2M1 conversions use native cvt instructions on CUDA 13.1+/13.2+ and bit-exact fallbacks below.
- msa_{decode,prefill}_nvfp4_specialized_stats() and the capability manifests in flashinfer/msa_ops/*_workloads.json expose the supported surface and the CUDA-graph contract to callers.
- An FP32 composable reference for each route is exported for tests.

Tests
- Host-only guard tests for both routes, and device tests against the FP32 reference across batch sizes, KV lengths, top-k values, block-table widths, multi-token decode, empty selections, strided selection views, both decode implementations, CUDA-graph capture and out=.

title: feat(prims-ts): extend QToken-KvBlock-Sparse-Attention shapes and patterns
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Extend QToken-KvBlock-Sparse-Attention to G1–G8, D64/D128/D256, and semantic KV blocks of 4/8/16/32/64/128 tokens. Support shared or per-KV-head sparse patterns and persistent execution. Existing QToken entry points remain compatible.

### Interface

| Input/config | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Packed Q | `[T,Hq,D]`; device `qo_indptr` partitions request-safe groups of at most G |
| Fixed Q | `[B,Nq,G,Hq,D]`; plan for `B*Nq` groups |
| KV cache | Separate HND K/V tensors `[pages,Hkv,page_size,D]` |
| Physical pages | Dense `block_table[num_requests,max_pages]` |
| Sparse patterns | `indexer_block_ids[T,K]` when shared; `[T,Hkv,K]` otherwise |
| Group capacity | `G*(Hq/Hkv) <= 128`; partial groups are supported |
| Split permission | `split_kv=False` disables splitting; True permits useful splits, independently of Q layout |

`share_pattern_across_kv_heads` defaults to True for QToken and False for the existing Q-block sparse APIs. Both support either setting. Q/K/V/output may be matching FP16/BF16, or FP8 E4M3 Q/K/V with FP16/BF16 output.

```python
num_groups = group_offsets.numel() - 1 if packed else q.shape[0] * q.shape[1]
wrapper = QTokenKvBlockSparsePagedTSWrapper()
wrapper.plan(
    num_groups, G, Hq, Hkv, D, kv_block_size, page_size, K, model_len,
    device=q.device, workspace_buffer=workspace,
    q_data_type=q.dtype, o_data_type=out.dtype,
    use_packed_q=packed, split_kv=allow_split,
    share_pattern_across_kv_heads=shared,
)
wrapper.run(
    q, (k_cache, v_cache), block_table, indexer_block_ids,
    token_to_request, query_positions,
    qo_indptr=group_offsets if packed else None, out=out,
)
```

Allocate the arena with `get_q_token_kv_block_sparse_workspace_size` using matching options. Warm up outside capture, then capture `run`. The cache writer must zero unused page padding. Inputs, output and workspace must obey the documented non-aliasing contract.

### Implementation

- G1 resolves raw indices inside attention without a metadata launch.
- Grouped routes sort/union selected blocks and store packed membership bytes; workspace is bounded by top-k and per-request model length, not cache-pool capacity.
- Cache membership rows in SMEM only when the full resource/barrier allocation fits; larger routes read packed words directly from existing GMEM metadata without changing G or split permission.
- Reuse common Q-tile, split and CLC scheduling helpers. Explicit G is preserved; the optional suggestion helper uses caller-provided SM capacity.
- One/two `cp.async` producers stage locators. Persistent work items refresh logical request/head bindings; a producer-to-softmax dependency protects membership-buffer reuse.
- Persistent grouped Keeps kernels reuse the existing per-task register budgets.
- Reuse compact geometry tests and existing trace examples; no new snapshots. FMHA tracing preserves the plan's split permission and the actual native/encoded page size.

`split_kv` is a common FMHA configuration option exposed by paged-decode and QToken APIs. Other existing Q-block sparse storage/interface contracts are unchanged; this PR does not introduce the later unified facade.

### Standalone performance

GB300/SM103, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1. TP2-local Hq/Hkv=12/1, D256, BS1 prefill, real recorded block4 selections. Identical Q/K/V and route hashes; CUDA Graph, non-compressible cold L2, 20 warmups and 300 samples. Latency includes metadata, attention and any reduction. These are standalone TP-shaped measurements, not all-layer or all-reduce timings.

Historical incremental comparison: `89b89153` versus the best previously supported G4/G5 result on main `c1c8e3e5`. These measurements are preserved below; the matched rebase check is reported separately. Speedup = previous/new; >1 favors the new configuration.

| Dtype | Context | Previous config | Previous µs | New G8 µs | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | 8K | G5 | 544.61 | 388.03 | 1.404× |
| BF16 | 16K | G5 | 1174.31 | 842.49 | 1.394× |
| BF16 | 32K | G5 | 2515.21 | 1818.75 | 1.383× |
| FP8 | 8K | G5 | 540.20 | 385.97 | 1.400× |
| FP8 | 16K | G5 | 1164.97 | 828.41 | 1.406× |
| FP8 | 32K | G5 | 2492.45 | 1780.94 | 1.400× |

In the same historical experiment, holding G8 fixed, persistent scheduling reduces BF16 prefill complete-path latency by 4.4–4.6% but makes FP8 0.2–0.9% slower; the 1.38–1.41× gains above also include the larger query grouping.

Rebased onto main `26617bc3` at `78d973d0`, preserving main's experimental API annotations. Both maintained suites (56 cases) passed twice before and after on the same GPU, comparing `944847a3` with `78d973d0`. Complete-path geometric-mean latency changed +0.01%; the largest increase was 1.90% (19.61 → 19.99 µs). Inputs, route hashes, launch choices, CUDA Graph and cold-L2 settings match. No meaningful rebase regression was observed.

The two [maintained sparse suites](https://github.com/PerkzZheng/flashinfer-prims-ts-validation/blob/main/docs/sparse_attention.md), same-G controls and static/persistent comparisons are recorded in the local validation report. The PR table focuses on this change's incremental benefit, not the broader Triton comparison.

title: feat: Add SM100 cuteDSL ReplaySSM GDN MTP decode kernels
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

Add SM100-family ReplaySSM verification and accepted-prefix commit to FlashInfer GDN MTP. Speculative verification normally stores a full FP32 recurrent state after each token so an accepted prefix can be committed. This PR keeps the checkpoint frozen during verify and saves only raw K/V, log-decay and sigmoid-beta windows, then reconstructs the accepted state in one all-layer commit launch.

- Extend `flashinfer.gdn_decode.gated_delta_rule_mtp` with opt-in `cache_replayssm` and four caller-owned window buffers.
- Add `flashinfer.gdn_decode.gated_delta_rule_replayssm_commit`. Verify writes the windows by pool slot; commit consumes the accepted prefix exactly once before the next verify overwrites it.
- On SM100/SM103, use TMA and tcgen05 TF32 contractions for frozen FP32 128x128 checkpoints, normalized Q/K, T=4..8, B=1..256, BF16 output, int32 indices and an even value-head/key-head ratio. Other supported SM100 inputs use the FP32 MTP fallback.
- For normalized K without tracking, commit auto selects tcgen05 for T=8, or T=6/7 when B>1 and `layers * B * HV >= 256`; otherwise it uses SIMT. Explicit tcgen05 supports T=4..8. `backend="simt"` retains FP32 contractions, and optional tracked checkpoints use the SIMT path. TF32 outputs/checkpoints are not bitwise identical to FP32 recurrence.
- Preserve upstream device-specific compile targets and persistent CuTe-DSL caches, including layout-sensitive cache identities; add API docs, trace templates and trace examples.

ReplaySSM is restricted to FP32 checkpoints, K=V=128 and SM100/SM103. FP16 inputs follow the existing MTP BF16 conversion convention. Live source slots must be unique and in range; optional track destinations must be disjoint from all live source and track slots. Zero acceptance and reserved slots are no-ops. These device-side index contracts are documented without introducing host synchronization.

Dispatch uses tcgen05 for eligible T=4–8 verification and, with normalized K and no tracking, for T=8 commit or T=6/7 commit when B>1 and `layers * B * HV >= 256`; other cases use the generic verify or SIMT commit path.

### Performance

All values are microseconds. Verify columns are per layer; commit and total columns cover four layers. Full acceptance (4/4 or 8/8):

| B | T | Upstream verify + snapshots | ReplaySSM verify | Upstream total | ReplaySSM total | Speedup |

title: prefill: use fa2 backend for small per-request query lengths
body:
## 📌 Description

On SM90, `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="auto")` resolves to the
`fa3` backend, which runs `PrefillWithKVCacheKernel<SparseCollectiveMainloop<...>>`.
That kernel uses a fixed `CTA_Q=128` query tile, so when each request only
verifies a few query tokens (MTP / speculative decoding, `q_len_per_req=2`),
almost the entire tile is padding and the tensor-core work is wasted. This is
the ~10x gap reported in #3420.

`determine_attention_backend()` selects the backend from device, dtypes and
head dims only — it never sees the query length — so `auto` has no way to know
it is being called with an MTP-shaped batch. Notably, `backend="fa3"` combined
with `q_len_per_req > 1` raises `NotImplementedError: q_len_per_req > 1 is
currently only supported on the fa2 tensor-core backend`, confirming fa3 is not
intended for this case at all.

**What this PR changes.** In `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.plan()`
(`flashinfer/prefill.py`), after `auto` resolves, fall back to `fa2` when the
maximum query length per request is small:

```python
if (
    self._backend == "fa3"
    and qo_indptr is not None
    and qo_indptr.numel() > 1
    and int((qo_indptr[1:] - qo_indptr[:-1]).max().item()) <= 64
):
    self._backend = "fa2"
```

`fa2` selects an adaptive query tile instead (`CTA_TILE_Q=16` for `q_len=2`,
`64` for `q_len=8`). The guard is limited to the SM90 `fa3` case, so other
backends and other architectures are unaffected.

**Performance (H20 / SM90, FP16, NHD paged KV, page_size=16, GQA 32/8,
head_dim=128, KV=8192, 4 warmups + 12 CUDA-event samples, p50):**

| q_len | fa2 (us) | fa3 (us) | fa3/fa2 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 213.0 | 2141.3 | 10.05x |
| 8 | 570.1 | 2142.9 | 3.76x |
| 16 | 570.7 | 2145.1 | 3.76x |
| 32 | 1055.8 | 2144.0 | 2.03x |
| 64 | 2033.7 | 2145.1 | 1.05x |
| 128 | 3483.5 | 2142.9 | 0.62x |
| 256 | 6803.1 | 4180.3 | 0.61x |

fa3's cost is essentially independent of `q_len` (2141-2145 us at batch=16,
337-343 us at batch=1) while fa2 scales linearly, which is the fixed-tile
signature and confirms the mechanism above. The crossover is at `q_len=128`,
which is why the guard uses `max_q_per_req <= 64`.

End to end through `backend="auto"` with `q_len=2, KV=8192, batch=1`: 337 us
before, 56 us after.

**Reproduction.** Each number is one wrapper call timed with CUDA events after
4 warmup iterations:

```python
wrapper = flashinfer.prefill.BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
    workspace, "NHD", backend="fa2"   # or "fa3"
)
wrapper.plan(
    qo_indptr=torch.arange(0, (batch + 1) * q_len, q_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    paged_kv_indptr=torch.arange(0, (batch + 1) * pages, pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    paged_kv_indices=torch.arange(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").repeat(batch),
    paged_kv_last_page_len=torch.full((batch,), 16, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    num_qo_heads=32,
    num_kv_heads=8,
    head_dim_qk=128,
    page_size=16,
    pos_encoding_mode="NONE",
    causal=True,
    q_data_type=torch.float16,
    kv_data_type=torch.float16,
)
# then time wrapper.run(q, kv) with start/end CUDA events
```

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related to #3420.

title: feat(attention): add skip-softmax to SM120 PRIMS
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add opt-in skip-softmax to the SM120 CuTe DSL PRIMS FP8 ragged and paged prefill APIs, building on the merged #4714.

- The direct APIs accept `skip_softmax_threshold: Optional[Union[float, torch.Tensor]]`. A float supplies the final e-based threshold for every request; a contiguous CUDA float32 tensor of shape `[batch_size]` supplies one final threshold per request. There is no sequence-length normalization.
- A compute warp skips a K/V tile only when every valid row satisfies `exp((tile_max - running_max) * sm_scale) < threshold`. Skipping omits both online-softmax updates and PV MMA. The first visited tile always runs the initialization path.
- `None` selects the dense specialization. Any supplied threshold, including zero, selects the skip-enabled specialization; zero preserves dense behavior. Dynamic threshold loads follow the PDL dependency wait. Caller-owned threshold tensors can be updated in place between CUDA Graph replays.
- The D128 Q128/KV128 path uses a three-stage unified K/V TMA ring. V tiles are still transported and their pipeline barriers consumed when PV is skipped.
- Shared batch-prefill wrappers retain their existing APIs; skip-softmax through those wrappers remains unsupported for `cute-dsl-prims`.

The implementation is scoped to FP8 Q/K/V, with FP16/BF16 output. Tests cover API validation, JIT specialization, CUDA Graph/PDL, ragged/paged storage, and real skipping with output and log2 LSE checks for D64/D128/D256.

### D128 TMA pipeline optimization

One dedicated load warp prefetches the K/V tensor-map descriptors, initializes the arrived/consumed mbarriers, reduces its register allocation to 24, and issues asynchronous TMA copies into shared memory. TMA hardware transfers the tile payload; the load warp controls the copies and pipeline state. The compute warps receive 240 registers and consume the shared-memory stages.

Before this optimization, D128 used two type-fixed slots (`sK`, `sV`). After QK consumed `K0`, the producer could reload `K1` into the K slot while `V0` was still live, but startup held only `K0,V0`, `V1` remained blocked until `V0` was fully consumed, and every iteration serialized the producer through separate K-then-V consumed waits.

The optimized path treats K and V as one ordered three-slot ring. Its initial contents are logically `K0, V0, K1`; afterwards the producer waits only when it wraps around and reuses a consumed slot. For FP8 D128, one 128x128 operand tile is 16 KiB, so the ring uses 3x16 KiB = 48 KiB of shared memory. This adds K lookahead and overlaps TMA transport with QK/softmax/PV work without changing attention math.

The optimization does not yet suppress V transport for skipped tiles: tensor work and memory traffic measurements below remain effectively unchanged. The gain comes from overlap and reduced producer/consumer serialization.

### RTX PRO 5000 performance

Synthetic controlled-skip microbenchmark, not an end-to-end model claim:

| Realized tile skip fraction | Dense | Skip specialization | Speedup vs dense | max abs | relative L2 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.000000 | 235.425 ms | 245.553 ms | 0.9588x | 0 | 0 |
| 0.248996 | 237.767 ms | 214.058 ms | 1.1108x | 0 | 0 |
| 0.500000 | 237.781 ms | 180.761 ms | 1.3154x | 0.00012207 | 0.000340933 |
| 0.748996 | 237.200 ms | 147.742 ms | 1.6055x | 0.000244141 | 0.00058125 |
| 0.899598 | 236.882 ms | 128.137 ms | 1.8487x | 0.000244141 | 0.000673415 |
| 0.989960 | 236.825 ms | 116.889 ms | 2.0261x | 0.000976562 | 0.00265553 |
| 0.997992 | 236.632 ms | 115.881 ms | 2.0420x | 0.00390625 | 0.00593319 |

At zero skipped tiles the specialization costs 4.1%; the measured crossover is below 25% skipped tiles. The feature remains explicitly opt-in through its threshold argument.

Configuration: SM120 RTX PRO 5000, GPU 6, driver 580.95.05, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, batch 1, ragged non-causal attention, q_len=kv_len=63744, 56 Q/KV heads, head_dim=128, Q/KV tile 128x128, FP8 E4M3 Q/K/V, BF16 output, legacy threshold scale factor 1.0 (equivalent to final `skip_softmax_threshold=1/63744` with the current API), 5 warmups, 30 repeats, warm L2, CUDA-event timing because CUPTI Python timing was unavailable.

#### Same-GPU schedule A/B

| Mode | Two-stage baseline | Three-stage | Three-stage improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dense | 261.852 ms | 232.138 ms | 1.128x |
| Skip specialization, no tiles skipped | 269.336 ms | 239.996 ms | 1.122x |
| Skip specialization, 99.8% tiles skipped | 176.888 ms | 115.325 ms | 1.534x |
| Active-skip speedup vs its own dense | 1.480x | 2.013x | +0.533x |

The three-stage schedule reduces active-skip latency by 34.8% relative to the two-stage implementation. The following Nsight Compute metrics are for active skip on the same GPU and shape:

| NCU metric | Two-stage | Three-stage |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Duration | 176.888 ms | 115.325 ms |
| SM throughput | 56.13% | 86.34% |
| Issue active | 12.99% | 22.94% |
| Eligible warps | 0.18 | 0.29 |
| Long-scoreboard stall | 5.71% | 3.87% |
| Wait stall | 22.77% | 34.71% |
| Math-pipe throttle | 28.89% | 32.91% |
| MIO throttle | 6.33% | 0.04% |
| Barrier stall | 0.01% | 0.05% |
| Tensor work ratio vs dense | 0.501 | 0.501 |
| L2 traffic | 425.148 GiB | 425.150 GiB |
| DRAM read | 1.291 GiB | 1.292 GiB |

The key changes are higher SM utilization and issue activity, more eligible warps, lower long-scoreboard stalls, and the near-elimination of MIO throttling. The higher wait-stall percentage is a share of a much shorter kernel and is not an increase in absolute runtime. Stable tensor work and traffic show that the result is a scheduling improvement, not less input data or a changed skip decision.

Measured kernel commit: `9965a38b483847f0d770bbbe72ff50bc8fc9e3b6`; fraction-sweep runner commit: `b68dd3b45d8b23ca5213579c6fd94e54e123217f`. These are historical pipeline measurements taken before the direct-threshold API and PDL updates. The current revision has been correctness-tested as described below; these performance measurements were not rerun for the test-only follow-up.

title: perf(quantization): SM107 dispatch tuning and 128x4 tile kernels for nvfp4/mxfp4/mxfp8
body:
## 📌 Description Tunes the CuTe-DSL quantization kernels (`nvfp4_quantize`, `mxfp4_quantize`, `mxfp8_quantize`) for SM107. Every change is gated on `get_compute_capability() == (10, 7)`; SM100/SM103 dispatch and codegen are unchanged. - **128x4 tile kernels** (one per quantizer). In the row-based kernels a warp owns one row, so its 1-byte scale stores in the 128x4 layout touch 8 different 128 B lines per 32 SF blocks. A CTA now quantizes a 128-row × 4-column tile whose scales are one contiguous 512 B block, stages them in shared memory, and writes them back with full-line stores. Loads stay coalesced; output is byte-identical to the row kernels. Used for wide inputs (M ≥ 1024, K ≥ 2048, rows ≥ 8 KiB with ≥ 16 MiB input, or rows ≥ 4 KiB with ≥ 64 MiB). The nvfp4 TMA kernel keeps precedence where it applies. - **nvfp4 vector path**: 2 persistent CTAs/SM for inputs ≥ 1M elements; FP8 input pairs two strided SF blocks per thread (`pair_fp8_blocks`, part of the kernel cache key, requested only for FP8) so each thread keeps two 16 B loads in flight; TMA enabled for FP16/BF16 with layout-specific crossovers. - **mxfp8**: 256-thread "small blocks" kernel for wide rows (K > 16384 all dtypes, 8192 < K ≤ 12288 for 16-bit); lower persistent grid caps (FP32 linear keeps the default). **mxfp4**: 2 CTAs/SM from 32M elements. **Performance** on Rubin (SM107), speedup of this branch over `main`, geomean over the swept shapes (1024×8192 to 8192×24576), cold L2: | Config | linear | 8x4 | 128x4 | |---|---|---|---| | nvfp4 bf16 | 1.02x | 1.04x | 1.08x | | nvfp4 fp16 | 1.02x | 1.04x | 1.09x | | mxfp4 bf16 | 0.99x | 1.00x | 1.03x | | mxfp4 fp16 | 0.99x | 1.00x | 1.03x | | mxfp8 bf16 | 1.01x | 1.04x | 1.05x | | mxfp8 fp16 | 1.01x | 1.04x | 1.05x | | mxfp8 fp32 | 1.00x | 1.03x | 1.04x | The 128x4 layout, which the GEMMs consume, gains the most; shapes below the SM107 thresholds are unchanged by construction.

title: fix(gdn): point the gated_delta_rule_mtp deprecation marker at 0.8.0
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`gated_delta_rule_mtp()`'s `disable_state_update` deprecation marker names **0.7.0** as the
release where the implicit default flips to `False` — in three places, one of which is a runtime
`warning_once`. `main` and `release-v0.7.0` are both 0.7.0, and the default there is still `True`
(`gdn_decode.py` resolves `None` → `True`). So 0.7.0 ships a warning promising a change that
0.7.0 does not make, naming itself as the release.

**0.8.0 is the correct target, not a deferral.** The deprecation first shipped in **v0.6.7** —
`git tag --contains 7cb016df` (PR #2730), earliest non-rc, non-nightly tag. Under the window
documented in `docs/deprecation_survey_v0.7.0.md`:

> **Window.** A deprecated public API is guaranteed for **two minor releases**, then may be
> removed. Deprecated in 0.5.x → removable at **0.7.0**. Deprecated in 0.6.x → removable at
> **0.8.0**.

a 0.6.x deprecation is not eligible until 0.8.0. The marker was written one minor early; honouring
it in 0.7.0 would itself violate the two-minor guarantee. This is the same failure mode the survey
records in its §3 for two `bsa_attn` docstrings: *"Trust git, not the docstring."*

This PR amends the three strings and changes nothing else. The resolved default is still `True`.


## 🔍 Related Issues

Follows up #5218 (`chore: remove deprecated APIs eligible at the 0.7.0 boundary`), which surveyed
this symbol and left the decision open. Deprecation introduced in #2730.

title: feat(cake_gqa): add experimental prepared SM110 GQA decode
body:
## 📌 Description

Add an explicit prepared SM110 GQA decode API for repeated launches and CUDA Graph replay. It reuses caller output and per-instance workspace, while preserving the existing `sm110_gqa_decode` convenience API unchanged.

The default routes are original short, B4/capacity256 N32 direct output (zero global workspace), B1/capacity1024 N64 KV-last with ten splits, and B1/capacity4096 N32 ring3 with ten splits. The optimized QK/PV bodies use `tcgen05.mma`, TMA and TMEM. Other shapes fall back to original long; explicit `num_splits=1` also keeps that route above capacity64.

The generated kernel bodies are source-equivalent to the qualified implementation, with mechanical symbol/include renames only. The new manifest authenticates the added source closure. No AOT or automatic backend routing changes are included.

The source study preserves all four original shapes (FP16, Hq=32, Hkv=8, D=128) and reports **38.11% lower primary GPU latency** against the pinned original under controlled partial KV reuse, **52.22% / 16.73%** reductions on the two long shapes, and **32.70%** in the separate ordinary-launch crosscheck. Hot candidate/XQA latencies are **11.144 / 13.376 us** and **21.816 / 37.792 us**.

Measured on aarch64 NVIDIA Thor with CUDA 13.4 and PyTorch 2.14.0a0+b2c75dd062.nvinternal.main, using strict CUPTI, six paired groups of 32 retained samples, and matched observed GPC/EMC clocks of 1.386/3.2 GHz. The original is pinned to #5052 head `223e0706c9398ec628d87a8a93ed1548efcd7900`; XQA uses a fixed cubin specialization. The primary score aggregates nine cells: B4/cap256, B1/cap1024 and B1/cap4096 crossed with producer-hot, recent-64 and recent-256 KV conditioning. It uses geometric means of condition-level paired ratios, not ratios of marginal medians.

Representative producer-hot GPU latencies (evict, then update Q and the final valid K/V token):

| Batch / capacity | Valid lengths | Original / candidate / XQA (us) | Paired latency reduction vs original |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |

## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #4703 (per the discussion in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4703#discussion_r3877766942). That PR taught `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper` to snapshot `q_seq_lens_cpu` / `kv_seq_lens_cpu` at plan time and forward them at run time, but only the `trtllm-gen` branch of `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek` consumed them — `backend="cute-dsl"` silently ignored the mirrors.

This matters because the CuTe DSL varlen kernel skips batches with `seqlen_k <= 0` without writing their output rows, and `out` defaults to `torch.empty`, so rows with `q_len > 0` and `kv_len == 0` return uninitialized memory.

- Hoist the CPU-mirror validation out of the trtllm-gen branch so both backends share it.
- On the cute-dsl branch, when mirrors are provided, neutralize empty-kv rows before the launch (`out = 0`, `lse = -inf`), matching trtllm-gen's empty-row semantics; skip the launch entirely when every row is empty. Unlike trtllm-gen there is no in-kernel UB on empty rows, so no compaction is needed — the kernel still sees the original uncompacted tensors.
- The fill stays CUDA-graph-capturable: decisions read only the CPU mirrors, and the fill itself uses only device-resident ops (`repeat_interleave(..., output_size=...)` + `masked_fill_`).
- Mirrors remain optional on cute-dsl (no new raise for omitting them), so existing all-active capture callers keep working.

Behavior note: previously the cute-dsl backend ignored the mirrors entirely, including malformed ones; after this PR malformed mirrors (unpaired, wrong device/dtype/shape, mismatched sums) raise a `ValueError` on both backends. The wrapper always forwards a valid pair snapshotted at plan time, so only direct callers passing invalid mirrors are affected — and for them the raise replaces silent garbage.

Scope: the wrapper forwards mirrors only on its cute-dsl FMHA path (`head_dim == 128`, no variant, no sliding window); the modular cute-dsl path has no mirror contract and is unchanged here.

Perf: on the common all-active path the only addition is a few CPU-side `.item()` reads on the CPU mirrors — no extra device work and no extra launches.

Tests: mirror-validation tests, stubbed-kernel tests for the pre-launch fill / skip-launch behavior, numerical parity against a compacted call, and a wrapper-level CUDA-graph capture/replay integration test with asymmetric zero-length rows (as suggested in #4703's review). The real-kernel tests gate on SM100, which I don't have access to — verified the wrapper logic on CPU with a stubbed kernel; would appreciate a CI run for the kernel-level tests.

Follow-up to #4703 (and #4609 context).

title: fix(attention): size prefill partial outputs by query rows, not packed indices
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

The FA2 prefill planner reserves the split-KV buffers `tmp_v` and `tmp_s` per (query row, head) pair instead of per query row.
With GQA that is group-size times too much: 16x for Qwen3.5 (32 query heads, 2 KV heads).

Symptom: vLLM fails at startup on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B with `--max-num-seqs 512` or more:
`Buffer overflow when allocating memory for batch_prefill_tmp_v`.

What changes:

- The planner reserves per query row. The bound uses the same plan-time values, so CUDA-graph replans keep their offsets.
- `plan()` checks that the planned rows fit.
- Decode with `use_tensor_cores=True` uses the same planner and benefits too.
- Every CUDA-graph case now fits a workspace sized by `workspace_size()`. The two prefill tests xfail'd for workspace overflow are re-enabled and size their workspace that way.
- `tests/conftest.py` skips a CUDA OOM without keeping the test's GPU tensors alive, and also catches an OOM re-raised by `assert_close`. Before, one OOM skip left its tensors allocated and later tests failed with OOM on small GPUs.

Workspace needed with CUDA graphs, head dim 256:

| case | query / KV heads | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5: 512 sequences of 1 token | 32 / 2 | 514 MB | 32 MB |
| 128 sequences of 577 tokens | 32 / 4 | 18.4 GB | 2.3 GB |
| 128 sequences of 577 tokens | 32 / 1 | 72.7 GB | 2.3 GB |

Before, the Qwen3.5 case overflowed vLLM's 394 MB workspace with the exact byte count from the reports. Now it fits.

End to end with vLLM main (435c96f9d) on an RTX 6000 Ada: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B config with dummy weights, cut to 4 layers and 8 experts, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER --max-num-seqs 512`, default CUDA graphs:

| main | engine fails during CUDA graph capture: `Buffer overflow when allocating memory for batch_prefill_tmp_v with size 536346624` |
| this PR | all PIECEWISE and FULL graphs captured (51 + 51), server starts and returns a completion |

title: fix(tests): skip tests/prims_ts instead of erroring when CUTLASS DSL < 4.7
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

> **Rewritten.** This PR originally proposed raising the `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`
> floor in `requirements.txt` to 4.7. That was wrong — see the comment below;
> the low floor is deliberate. The branch name is a leftover from that first
> attempt. The change here is entirely different.

## 📌 Description

`tests/prims_ts/conftest.py` calls `require_cutlass_dsl_experimental()` at module
scope. Prims-TS imports `cutlass.experimental.primitives` and
`cutlass.experimental.task_scheduling`, which exist only in CUTLASS DSL 4.7+, so on
any environment resolved against our own declared floor (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.6.2a0`)
that call raises during collection:

```
ERROR tests/prims_ts - RuntimeError: Prims-TS requires the CUTLASS DSL wheel.
Install the pinned release-branch wheel before using Prims-TS kernels.
```

It is a *collection* error, not a test failure, so it takes out the entire
directory rather than the tests that actually need the wheel.

**Raising the floor is not the fix.** FlashInfer's lower bound is aligned with
vLLM's and SGLang's on purpose: CuTe DSL is a diamond dependency, and pinning up
would make FlashInfer unsatisfiable in those stacks. Features that need 4.7 are
meant to be gated at runtime and light up when the environment provides them —
which is already the house pattern:

- `flashinfer/attention/cute_dsl/sm120_fmha.py` — `_MIN_CUTLASS_DSL_VERSION = Version("4.7.0")`, checked at call time
- `flashinfer/kda.py` — needs `>=4.7`; below that `backend="auto"` falls back to Cake, and only an explicit `backend='cute-dsl'` raises
- `flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/context.py` — guards a 4.8 feature the same way

Prims-TS was the outlier. This makes it degrade like the rest.

The blanket require was also over-broad — **20 of the 21 test modules here import
fine without the wheel**. Only `test_batched_gemm_captured_schedule_tasks.py` pulls
in `batched_gemm_kernel` at module scope. Two of the modules it blocked,
`test_moe_bf16_support.py` and `test_moe_fp8_block_support.py`, call
`monkeypatch.setattr(support, "is_prims_ts_available", ...)` — they exist precisely
to exercise the unavailable path, and could never run.

### Why mark collected items instead of skipping at module level

A module-level `pytest.skip(..., allow_module_level=True)` collects **nothing**, so a
run scoped to this directory exits with pytest's "no tests collected" code **5** —
trading one red for another. Marking collected items keeps them collected, so the run
reports skips and exits **0**. I verified both behaviours directly rather than
assuming:

| Mechanism | Report | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=True)` in conftest | `1 skipped` | **5** |
| `collect_ignore` only | `no tests ran` | **5** |
| `collect_ignore` + skip marker via `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (this PR) | `3 skipped` | **0** |

As a side effect this makes `pytest_report_header`'s unavailable branch reachable for
the first time — it could never fire before, because the require above it raised first.
That dead branch is also the evidence that graceful degradation was the original intent.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- Fixes #5213

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

This changes test collection behaviour, so the test *is* the CI run: on a DSL 4.7
lane `tests/prims_ts` must run exactly as before (this path is a no-op there), and on
a lane below 4.7 it must report skips instead of a collection error.

The collection mechanism itself was validated standalone — `collect_ignore` drops the
un-importable module, every other module collects, all items report as skipped, exit 0.

## Reviewer Notes

**Scope I deliberately did not take.** When the wheel is missing this skips the whole
directory, including the ~8 modules that are pure Python and would pass anyway
(`test_moe_api_signature.py`, `test_moe_config_packaging.py`,
`test_moe_tensor_adapter_validation.py`, the two `*_support.py` ones, …). Narrowing the
skip to just the modules that reach the kernels would recover that coverage, but it
means classifying each module by whether it touches `batched_gemm_*` at runtime —
`test_moe_compile_cache.py` and `test_moe_nvfp4_support.py` do, and the
`test_batched_gemm_` filename prefix alone does not catch them. I kept the behaviour
change minimal and symmetric (directory errors today → directory skips) rather than
guessing at a classification I cannot verify without a 4.6.x box. Happy to follow up
if you'd rather have the finer split.

**On coverage.** This does mean a lane below 4.7 reports green with Prims-TS untested,
where today it reports red. That is the intended contract for a version-gated feature,
but it only holds if at least one lane actually carries DSL ≥ 4.7 — otherwise #4361
ships with no coverage anywhere and nothing says so. Worth confirming that's true of
the Blackwell lanes. `scripts/setup_test_env.sh` already supports a
`CUTLASS_DSL_VERSION` override that does a clean uninstall first, which looks like the
intended lever.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved Prims-TS test handling when the experimental runtime is unavailable.
  * Affected test modules are now ignored during collection instead of causing collection failures.
  * Collection errors now point to the appropriate test-collection configuration for troubleshooting.

* **Tests**
  * Added regression coverage confirming Prims-TS tests collect successfully with limited experimental runtime support.

title: bench: compare DeepSeek MoE against TRTLLM MXFP8
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

@humansand

Extend `benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py` with **TRTLLM MXFP8**, immediately before **TRTLLM BF16**, following #4985.

- **Implementation:** reuse `bench_trtllm`; add the explicit `mxfp8` precision branch and `trtllm-mxfp8` selector. Reuse public `TrtllmFp8BlockConfig.prepare_weights` / `prepare_activations`, including gated weight reorder and shuffled MajorK scales. No kernel changes.
- **Contract:** E4M3 activations/weights with one UE8M0 scale per 32 elements along K; native `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` / routed variant with `Fp8QuantizationType.MxFp8`. `--include-activation-quant` includes the initial BF16-to-MXFP8 quantizer. Weight preparation stays outside timing. The public shuffled-weight preparation requires H and I divisible by 128, satisfied by this workload.
- **Presentation:** full precision names in selectors, tables, CSV, winners, and profiling; MXFP8 latency and speedup appear immediately before BF16. Existing unsupported-precision error remains explicit.
- **Evidence:** five arms: CuteDSL W4A4, CuteDSL W4A16, TRTLLM NVFP4, TRTLLM MXFP8, TRTLLM BF16. The 8192/16384 rows extend the original range. Only TRTLLM NVFP4 inference per-tensor was additionally rerun across the full range after correcting its scale layout. CUTLASS is omitted as requested to reduce compilation time.
- **Baseline correction:** the existing TRTLLM NVFP4 per-tensor arm produced swizzled activation scales but called a native API whose default layout is linear. Produce linear scales and pass `hidden_states_scale_layout=SfLayout.layout_linear` explicitly. The 45 superseded timings remain in raw evidence and a separate table; they are excluded from performance comparisons. FP4 per-token/RL paths already produced linear scales.

### Workload and three configurations

- **DeepSeek-V3:** H=7168, I=2048, E=256, top-k=8, 8 groups / top-4 groups, routed scale=2.5, seed=42, routing-bias scale=0.01. Native logits routing; BF16 source inputs/weights are regenerated identically per token row. TRTLLM routing weights use its native precision; no cross-backend numerical parity is asserted.
- **Parallelism:** EP8 local simulation (32 local experts, offset 0), TP1, one GPU. This times one local expert partition, with no expert-parallel communication.
- **Tokens:** `1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384`. Original batch: 9 processes × 13 token counts × 5 arms = 585 measurements. Appended batch: 9 processes × 2 token counts × 5 arms = 90. Corrected TRTLLM NVFP4 per-tensor batch: 3 processes × 15 token counts = 45. **720 raw measurements; 675 selected comparison cells; 45 superseded cells**, with three valid repeats at every configuration/token/backend point. All three batches use the retained devbox, in separate fresh processes.

| Configuration | FP4 per-token activation | NVFP4 4over6 | CuTe DSL finalize |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inference per-tensor | False | disabled | atomic fused |
| Inference per-token | True | disabled | atomic fused |
| Deterministic RL configuration | True | enabled, exact environment below | deterministic two-stage |

MXFP8 always uses its native 32-element UE8M0 blocks; FP4 per-token/4over6 flags do not change it. All TRTLLM arms keep native finalize. “Deterministic RL” names the benchmark recipe and CuTe finalize choice; it does not claim all TRTLLM implementations are deterministic.

### Timing and provenance

- **Measurement:** 10 warmups / 100 iterations, CUDA graphs, CUPTI, cold L2, initial activation quantization included for quantized-activation arms; W4A16 and TRTLLM BF16 consume BF16 directly. Timing includes routing, both GEMMs, activation, and finalize. Source generation, weight quantization/reorder, and autotuning are excluded. No external profiler is active during performance collection.
- **Autotuning:** each backend's prewarm executes under `autotune(True)` before measurement/capture; measured calls run outside that tuning context. Default wrapper API for CuTe DSL. No distribution-aware routing, external autotune cache, or host-loop timing is used.
- **Comparison with #4985:** same workload and final CUPTI/CUDA-graph/cold-L2 measurement path. The current upstream autotuner profiles isolated cold-L2 candidates with an explicit 2×L2 flush and median CUDA-event timing; #4985 used rotated-input / back-to-back candidate timing. Every arm is freshly retuned here. These are current-source comparisons, not a regression claim against historical #4985 numbers.
- **Sources:** original batch `1cafd1a22ea7be32497c1b8e66c466ea873bb0af`; 8192/16384 extension `48f8a7a7bf2282cdb976dd4e28ec01ff32bf9cd1`; corrected TRTLLM NVFP4 per-tensor `964f6fd2a582da1a7b57b5c20e3872caea80f693`. The extension adds `tune_max_num_tokens=max(n,8192)` so 16384-token candidates tune at 16384 instead of the native 8192 cap; at ≤8192 it equals the previous default. The final change only fixes NVFP4 activation-scale layout. The report verifies these narrow semantic differences and every batch's source/hash/settings. Other cells retain their measured source attribution; none is relabeled as a fresh final-head measurement.
- **Version:** based on upstream `7c194873672f629f04bd3a862c3c881502419fed`, FlashInfer **0.7.0**; #4985 measured FlashInfer 0.6.18. Raw tables retain all repeats; derived latency is the median of three sweeps per point, with ratios computed from unrounded result objects.
- **TFLOPS:** estimated local work assumes uniform routing: `tokens × top_k × (32/256) × (2×7168×4096 + 2×2048×7168) / elapsed_seconds / 1e12`. It is not an achieved hardware-counter measurement.

### Environment

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | C2; 1 NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC used (GPU 0), SM103, 148 SMs, 267.7 GiB; 8 GPUs on host |
| Container | `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3` |
| Resolved image | `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch@sha256:222d8b18e671be5c3ef91cb41727a2572a0b23f59ded6c39f373a96946f6f2ba` |
| CUDA toolkit / nvcc | 13.2.1.009 / 13.2.78 |
| Host driver / loaded compatibility libcuda | 590.48.01 / 595.58.03 |
| Python | 3.12.3 |
| PyTorch | `2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.05` |
| CuTe DSL | `4.7.0` (`cu13` extras installed) |
| CUPTI Python / runtime | `13.2.0` / `13.2.86` |
| TVM-FFI / nvdisasm | `0.1.13.post3` / `13.4.92` |
| Compilation | `BUILD_NVEP=0 FLASHINFER_BUILD_NO_PIP=1 MAX_JOBS=8` |

The container was selected as the newest CUDA 13.2 NGC PyTorch release using the [official release matrix](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/frameworks/pytorch-release-notes/rel-26-08.html). The devbox and warm compilation caches are retained for follow-up benchmarks.

### Reproduce performance

Run inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3` on a B300. The following commands remeasure the complete 1–16384 range on the final source. Published cells retain the three-batch provenance above. Existing cache files can remain; source/version changes trigger normal cache invalidation.

```bash

git clone https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git
cd flashinfer
git remote add benchmark https://github.com/zianglih/flashinfer.git
git fetch benchmark zianglih/bench-deepseek-moe-mxfp8
git checkout 964f6fd2a582da1a7b57b5c20e3872caea80f693
git submodule update --init --recursive
export BUILD_NVEP=0 FLASHINFER_BUILD_NO_PIP=1 MAX_JOBS=8
python3 -m pip install 'setuptools>=77' 'apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.13.post3'
python3 -m pip install 'nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.7.0' 'cupti-python==13.2.0' 'nvidia-cuda-cupti==13.2.86' ninja einops pytest pytest-timeout
python3 -m pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps -e .

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 MAX_JOBS=8
unset FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNER_LOAD_FROM_FILE FLASHINFER_DIST_AWARE_AUTOTUNE
unset FLASHINFER_DA_DISTRIBUTIONS FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_TIMER

unset FLASHINFER_DISABLE_FP4_QUANT_FAST_MATH
mkdir -p ../benchmark-results
base_args=(--num-tokens 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384
  --ep 8 --tp 1 --warmup 10 --iters 100
  --routing-input-mode logits --routing-bias-scale 0.01
  --include-activation-quant
  --backends cutedsl,trtllm-nvfp4,trtllm-mxfp8,trtllm-bf16)
for repeat in 1 2 3; do
  python3 benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py "${base_args[@]}" \
    2>&1 | tee "../benchmark-results/inference-per-tensor-$repeat.log"
  python3 benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py "${base_args[@]}" --use-per-token-activation \
    2>&1 | tee "../benchmark-results/inference-per-token-$repeat.log"
  env FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6=1 FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_E4M3_USE_256=1 \
```

## Derived performance summary

Latency is the median of three selected fresh-process measurements for that cell. TRTLLM NVFP4 inference per-tensor uses the corrected linear-scale batch at every token count; all other cells use their original/extension batches. Superseded values are excluded. Speedup = comparison backend latency / CuteDSL W4A16 latency; **>1 means W4A16 is faster**. Ratios use unrounded values.

- **TRTLLM MXFP8 versus TRTLLM BF16:** The speedup (TRTLLM BF16 latency / TRTLLM MXFP8 latency) ranges from 1.31× to 1.72× across the 45 configuration/token medians. TRTLLM MXFP8 is faster at every point.
- **Repeat variability:** the largest `(max − min) / median` among the three-sweep samples is 14.6%, for TRTLLM NVFP4 at 2 tokens (Inference per-token). All samples are retained; near-1× ratios should not be interpreted as decisive differences.

title: feat(moe): native OCP-MX-FP8 (W8A8) grouped MoE for SM120/121
body:
## Motivation

The CUTLASS grouped-MoE path on SM120/121 (DGX Spark GB10, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090) currently only
admits NVFP4 weights — `get_candidate_configs_sm120` throws *"SM120 group GEMM only supports nvfp4"*
for anything else, and `isValidSM120MOESpecialisation` accepts only `(fp4,fp4)` and `(fp8-act, fp4-weight)`.
There is **no native OCP-MX-FP8 (block-32, W8A8) grouped MoE** for these arches anywhere, so MXFP8 MoE
checkpoints fall back to MARLIN (W8A16 dequant), leaving the `tcgen05` MX FP8 tensor cores unused. The
TRTLLM-gen MoE cubins that cover MXFP8 on SM100 are prebuilt and not shipped for SM120/121 (#3294).

MXFP8 is near-lossless vs BF16 (NVFP4 costs ~2–5%, worse on low-active-param MoEs), so a high-VRAM
workstation Blackwell card is exactly where you want MXFP8 MoE on the tensor-core path.

## What this does

Enables the existing SM120 block-scaled grouped collective to run `(e4m3 weight, e4m3 act)` = W-MXFP8,
by composing the working dense SM120 MX-FP8 collective with the grouped-FP4 path. Compiler-guided,
one error at a time — each change grounded in the dense MX-FP8 SM120 kernel and the SM100 reference.

8 files:
- `moe_tma_warp_specialized_traits.h` — admit `(e4m3, e4m3)` to `isValidSM120MOESpecialisation`.
- `generate_kernels.py` — emit the `(e4m3, e4m3)` SM120 grouped op with `is_mx_fpx=True` (block-scaled).
- `moe_gemm_tma_ws_launcher.inl` — use `mx_float8_t` (not `mx_float4_t`) for an fp8 weight; force
  `StageCount<2>` for the SM120 W-MXFP8 block-scaled collective.
- `moe_gemm_template_dispatch_tma_ws.h` — emit only the MX path for `(e4m3,e4m3)` on SM120 (the plain
  fp8×fp8 SM120 launcher is invalid and would otherwise be referenced → undefined symbol at load).
- `gemm_configs.h` — new `CutlassGemmConfig::MXFP8_ONLY` bit.
- `cutlass_heuristic.cpp` — accept `MXFP8_ONLY` alongside `FP4_ONLY` in `get_candidate_configs_sm120`.
- `moe_gemm_template_dispatch.h` — set the W-MXFP8 flag in `getTmaWarpSpecializedConfigs`; exclude
  W-MXFP8 from the Ampere-config and the SM89-fallback execution paths so it reaches the TMA-WS dispatch.
- `tests/moe/test_trtllm_cutlass_fused_moe.py` — enable `test_moe_mxfp8_mxfp8` on SM12x (`[10] → [10, 12]`).

## Correctness

`pytest tests/moe/test_trtllm_cutlass_fused_moe.py::test_moe_mxfp8_mxfp8` → **6/6 PASS** on GB10 (SM121),
fp16+bf16 output × 3 SwiGLU variants, within `rtol/atol=1e-1` of the dequantized BF16 reference.
Verified end-to-end in vLLM (companion PR) on `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-MXFP8W8A8`: coherent, MARLIN-quality output.

## Performance (in-vLLM A/B, gemma4-26B-A4B MXFP8, GB10, vs MARLIN W8A16)

| concurrency | flashinfer_cutlass tok/s | marlin tok/s | speedup |
|------------:|-------------------------:|-------------:|--------:|
| 1  |  30.1 | 31.6 | 0.95× |
| 4  | 131.0 |119.0 | 1.10× |
| 16 | 493.3 |367.5 | 1.34× |
| 32 | 878.3 |688.4 | 1.28× |

≈ MARLIN in the memory-bound decode regime (both load 8-bit weights); **1.28–1.34× faster compute-bound**
(FP8 tensor cores vs BF16 dequant).

## Repro
Build on SM120/121, then the pytest above. Notes: the FlashInfer autotuner currently faults building
W-MXFP8 dummy tensors (separate issue) — run with autotune disabled; the partial-N-tile case requires the
caller to pad the intermediate dim to a 128-multiple (handled in the vLLM companion PR).

## Cross-links
- #3294 (SM120/121 TRTLLM-gen MoE cubins unavailable) — this is the native-kernel alternative.
- vLLM companion PR (oracle + FlashInferExperts + ModelOpt wiring): to follow.

## 📌 Description

Hey! This PR enables XQA for sm80 family. The kernels already had all the necessary code, it's a dispatch-only change.

The only behavior change is for `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache`, with `backend="auto"` - for sm8x users it was raising RuntimeError, now it runs XQA.

The main motivation is to speed up FI-based attention in vllm (in a fork). Without this change, with vllm's + FI I was getting flat 60-70tps for Qwen3.8 27B model with dflash2; by switching to XQA, it raises to 100tps, falling to ~80tps at large context sizes.

Isolated flashinfer_benchmark shows that XQA is much faster at short context sizes, and a bit slower at larger context sizes; E2E behavior is different (when integrated in vllm, etc); I haven't debugged it, because e2e numbers are very good.

<details>
<summary>benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py, measured on cmp170hx</summary>

### Benchmark

(presented and run by AI; I can provide raw logs if needed).

Decode sweep (s_qo ∈ {1, 8}, s_kv ∈ {4096, 32768, 131072, 204800},
 batch 1; batch 4 spot-checked at 131072). For s_qo=1 pass
 --backends fa2 trtllm-native; for s_qo=8 pass --backends trtllm-native
 (fa2 skips multi-query by design):

 ```bash
   python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py \
     --routine BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper \
     --batch_size 1 --num_qo_heads 32 --num_kv_heads 8 \
     --head_dim_qk 128 --head_dim_vo 128 --page_size 16 \
     --s_qo 8 --spec_dec_mask causal --s_kv 32768 \
     --backends trtllm-native -n 10 --refcheck
 ```

 Prefill-fallback emulation (the stock sm80 verify path: prefill kernel,
 8 query rows, causal mask):

 ```bash
   python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py \
     --routine BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper \
     --batch_size 1 --num_qo_heads 32 --num_kv_heads 8 \
     --head_dim_qk 128 --head_dim_vo 128 --page_size 16 \
     --s_qo 8 --s_kv 32768 --causal --backends fa2 -n 10 --refcheck
 ```

 Prerequisites on this branch: the two gate commits (this PR), plus the
 one-line "8.0" row addition in the harness backend table
 (benchmarks/routines/flashinfer_benchmark_utils.py, cc 8.0 row +=
 trtllm-native) — without it the harness skips trtllm-native on sm80
 with a warning. 

   | ctx | plain decode: fa2 | plain: XQA | spec verify, 8 rows (causal): XQA | spec verify: prefill-fallback emulation |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 4K | 0.128 ms | **0.024 ms (5.3×)** | **0.042 ms** | 0.098 ms |
   | 32K | 0.149 ms | **0.117 ms** | **0.116 ms** | 0.138 ms |
   | 128K | **0.426 ms** | 0.475 ms | 0.548 ms | **0.374 ms** |
   | 200K | **0.647 ms** | 0.729 ms | 0.760 ms | **0.566 ms** |

     8 query rows — the "prefill-fallback" column is that call shape run
